title: [C4] Jev geocoding validation: hidden-GPS test, San Francisco
body:
## Goal
Measure whether CrashIQ can place crashes that have no GPS by street names alone, and whether Jev beats code-only matching. Decided by the user 2026-10-18: city = San Francisco, run overnight.

## Component
C3 ccrs (pull + clean) · C4 locate (normalize → exact → fuzzy → Jev Choice on leftovers)

## Read first
- docs/03-requirements.md § J1 detail, Q9–Q11 (98% bar, hidden-GPS method)
- docs/04-design.md § C3, C4, seam 1

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pull SF crashes WITH coordinates from CCRS (most recent complete year), cached locally, cleaning steps logged
- [ ] SF intersections + street names from OSM (Overpass), cached
- [ ] Street-name normalizer with versioned alias table (file, not prompt), unit-tested
- [ ] Sample 1,000 crashes (fixed seed), hide GPS, place by PrimaryRoad/SecondaryRoad (+ distance/direction offset)
- [ ] Arms: code exact · +fuzzy · +Jev (top-5 candidates + "none of these") — Claude arm optional
- [ ] Score per arm: accuracy (assigned within 250 ft of true GPS), coverage (% auto-placed vs sent to review), with the lower confidence bound on accuracy
- [ ] Pick τ (Jev cut-off) where accuracy ≥ 98% by lower bound, report the coverage that leaves
- [ ] Jev spend capped and logged
- [ ] Results table in the PR description; no decision taken on the user's behalf if the bar is missed

## Out of scope
UI, FastAPI app scaffold, other cities.

## Depends on
none

title: Research: crash data and study methods by state (nationwide rollout)
body:
## Goal
The user wants CrashIQ to go nationwide eventually (2026-10-18): California first, then New York, Texas, Washington, Massachusetts and other important states. ISOAP, HSIP-California rules etc. are California-only, so each state needs its own data source and its own study methods. Research what exists before we design for it.

## Per state (CA baseline, then NY, TX, WA, MA, plus 3 to 5 more you recommend)
- Crash data: public source, API or bulk download, licence/commercial use, years available, update lag, GPS coverage, severity scale (KABCO?), party/vehicle tables, known gaps
- Volumes/AADT source; road inventory (for SPFs)
- State safety programs and required study formats (HSIP application format, ICE/intersection control policy, local road safety plans)
- Federal layers that cover every state: FARS (fatal), CRSS, HPMS, FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, HSM. What they can and can't do nationally

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Report in reports/ (same style as the industry-methods report), with a state x data-availability matrix and sources cited
- [ ] Recommended state rollout order with reasons
- [ ] What must be state-specific vs. shared in CrashIQ (data adapter, severity mapping, study modes)
- [ ] Decisions for the user listed as questions (not decided by Hermes)

title: [C3/C4] Crash placement without GPS: SF validation (98.7%, bar met for exact tier)
body:
## What this does
First real engine pieces, plus a measured answer to "can CrashIQ place crashes that have no GPS from the street names in the report?"

- `backend/crashiq/sources/ca_ccrs.py`: California adapter (CCRS, data.ca.gov). Shared crash shape so other states plug in later. Runtime resource ids, cached pulls, cleaning counts (`cleaning_log`), CHP-deleted rows dropped, feet-typed-as-miles fixed.
- `backend/crashiq/names.py`: street-name normalizer; `data/aliases/<city>.csv` alias files (header only, entries need user approval), wired into the locator.
- `backend/crashiq/osm.py`: OSM network for the agency's jurisdiction (Wikidata boundary), named footways/plazas, address index, street index.
- `backend/crashiq/locate.py`: tiers `address → exact → relaxed → near → fuzzy → jev → review`, offset along the primary road, and **`Gate`** (seam 1): only proven tiers auto-place; Jev τ / margin are config values, default "Jev never auto-places".
- `backend/crashiq/jev.py`: Jev Choice wrapper, pinned model, cache, call cap, spend log (input $0.042/M; output tokens are free).
- `backend/scripts/validate_geocode.py`: hidden-truth test, dev/test halves, arms, Jev-vs-fuzzy, summary JSON per run. `tests/`: 20 unit tests.
- `knowledge/`: what was learned (sources, method, lessons).

## Method (change from issue #1, needs the user's OK)
Issue #1 said: hide GPS on same-city crashes that have it. In SF those are CHP freeway crashes, while the crashes to place are SFPD city-street reports (~1% GPS). So SFPD crashes in CCRS are linked by report number to **SF's own geocoded crash locations (DataSF)**. Note: that's SF's geocoder, not GPS, so "accuracy" means agreement with SF's own placement. Rules were tuned on the dev half and reported once on the untouched test half. Lower bounds: **Wilson score, 95%**.

## Final results — SF test half (one run: `data/results/geocode_sf_test_summary.json`)
SFPD 2023–2025, 8,056 linked, 4,028 test crashes. Cleaning: 12,305 CCRS rows · 0 deleted · 5 unit fixes · 25 duplicate/blank report numbers dropped · 18 truth records with unrelated streets dropped (sample-selection filter; count shown so its effect is visible).

| Arm (what auto-places) | Coverage | Accuracy (≤250 ft) | Wilson 95% low |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A: exact only (default gate)** | **90.2%** | **98.8%** | **98.3% ✓ bar 98%** |
| B: exact + relaxed + near + fuzzy | 94.1% | 98.5% | 98.1% ✓ (98.0% on dev: borderline) |
| C: exact + Jev on all leftovers | 95.1% | 98.2% | 97.8% ✗ |
| C′: exact + fuzzy + Jev on the rest | 95.2% | 98.2% | 97.8% ✗ |

- **Jev vs fuzzy at the same review rate** (docs/03 J1 ship rule), 326 leftovers: fuzzy family **92.5%**, Jev top-159 by p **88.1%**. Jev 1.14 (released 2026-10-14): same 88.1%. → **Jev does not beat fuzzy, so it doesn't ship as an auto-placer.** It's very good on typos and is kept as a one-click review suggestion.
- **Jev spend:** 169 calls, 69,900 input tokens, **$0.0029** (cap 3,000 calls ≈ $0.06); 5 calls failed (sent to review).
- **Data finding:** in ~9% of SFPD crashes, CCRS drops the distance-from-intersection that SF's own record has.
- **Address tier** (1.7%): 81% vs SF's *approximate* address truth. Not in any arm until the user decides.

## Second city: Los Angeles — not certified
LAPD open data links by report number too (strip the dash). But LAPD's points are snapped to the intersection (median 6 m from it even when the report says 87 m away) and some are kilometres off (Canoga & Burbank: ours at the real intersection, LAPD's 1.6 km away). On the 2024 dev half the chosen intersection agrees with LAPD's street names 93–96%, but **LAPD's data can't certify 98% in LA.** Details: `knowledge/methods/geocoding.md`.

## Decisions for the user (not taken here)
1. Accept DataSF (SF's own geocode) as truth instead of hidden GPS?
2. Gate: arm A (exact only, 90% auto) or arm B (94% auto, lower bound right at 98%)?
3. Address tier: auto-place with an "address" flag, or review?
4. Provenance tags: add `address`, `relaxed`, `near` (and `review` vs `unmatched`) to the vocabulary?
5. Agency open data first (DataSF etc.) where it exists?
6. Anthropic API key, so a Claude arm can be compared?
7. LA truth: hand-check ~200 LA placements or pull TIMS geocodes, so LA can be certified?

## How to run

title: Why crashes don't auto-place: investigate review reasons and fix (later version)

## Goal
The user wants every crash we can't auto-place understood and, in a later version, fixed. Today ~10% (SF) and more in Long Beach go to review.

## Known causes (from PR #16 runs, see knowledge/methods/geocoding.md)
- Streets that never meet in OSM (ramps, plazas, officer error, e.g. 15TH AV & MISSION ST)

- Offsets lost in CCRS (~9% of SFPD crashes)

- [ ] Results added to knowledge/

Changing the auto-place gate (user decision).

title: [C2] network: corridor polyline → OSM intersections + segments
body:
Closes #7

## What it does
`PUT /studies/{id}/corridor` takes the drawn line (A → B). It fetches nearby roads from Overpass, cached in SQLite, and stores the corridor's intersections in order from A to B. All of it is code, no AI (`crashiq/network.py`):
1. **Corridor ways** are ways that run *along* the line: nodes within 80 ft and direction within 25°. A divided road's two carriageways both count.
2. **Intersections** are nodes shared by a corridor way and another road way (motorway → residential, plus links) between A and B. Nodes close along the line that share a cross-street name merge into one intersection: two per divided road, plus unnamed slip lanes. The pin sits on the named cross street, not on a slip lane.
3. **Control** comes only from OSM tags within 120 ft: `traffic_signals` → `signal`, `stop` → `stop`, otherwise `unknown`. Never guessed.
4. **Segments** run between adjacent *study* intersections and the limits A/B. Length in ft and mi along the line, in a projected CRS (`crashiq/geo.py`, a local ellipsoidal projection, tested to within 0.1% of a Vincenty geodesic). No stub segment when A or B sits within 50 ft of an intersection.

**Edits:** add, remove or rename an intersection, flag or unflag it as a study intersection, and set AADT (intersection major/minor, segment), stored for #8/C6. Segments recompute after every edit. Provenance: `auto` (OSM) or `manual` (user). A renamed OSM intersection stays `auto` with `name_source: user`.

**Failures:** retry with backoff on 429/5xx/timeouts. Overpass's "200 + runtime error remark" counts as a failure. A failure returns **502 with a plain message**, never an empty list, and is never cached.

Also adds `radius_ft` (default 250) and `buffer_ft` to the study, editable via `PATCH /studies/{id}` (used by #8 and #10).

## For the user to confirm
- **Corridor buffer default = 100 ft each side** of the line. Provisional: the docs say "user-adjustable" but give no default. It's one constant (`DEFAULT_BUFFER_FT`) and a per-study setting.

## Test data: hand-built, not recorded
The issue asks for a recorded Overpass response for Crenshaw (Marine → 132nd). The build sandbox can't reach Overpass, so `tests/fixtures/overpass_crenshaw.json` is **hand-built** by `make_crenshaw_overpass.py`, using the mockup's intersection positions. It includes a divided road, a T intersection, signals mapped on approach nodes, an unnamed slip lane, and cross streets outside the limits. To record the real response on a connected machine, run `backend/scripts/record_fixtures.py`; it prints the detected list for comparison.

## Tests (+19, no network)
Ordered list A → B with control types; divided road → one intersection; slip lane joins without moving the pin; cross streets outside the limits excluded; reversed line reverses the order; segment lengths vs hand-computed (Vincenty); unflagging a study intersection merges its segments; stub segments at the limits; cache hit skips the network; 504 retried; failure raises and caches nothing; Overpass error remark = failure; API round trip with rename/add/remove/AADT/clear; 502 message; bad edits → 409/404/422.

title: [C3] ccrs: corridor crash pull (Crashes / Parties / IWP) with per-study cache
body:
Closes #9

## What it does
`POST /studies/{id}/crashes/pull` pulls every CCRS crash the study needs. `GET /studies/{id}/crashes` returns them with the cleaning log. All code lives in `crashiq/crashes.py`. Everything California-specific is in `crashiq/sources/ca_ccrs.py` (the future state pack, #19); the CKAN client is `sources/ckan.py`.

1. **Resources resolved at runtime** from the CKAN `ccrs` package: Crashes / Parties / InjuredWitnessPassengers per year. No hardcoded IDs. A year missing from the datastore is logged (`years_missing`, `parties_missing_years`, `iwp_missing_years`), not fatal. (Parties_2025 was download-only on 2026-10-18; see `clue_reliability.py`.)
2. **Columns resolved at runtime too.** Each logical field has a candidate list matched against the datastore's real columns. A missing *required* column stops the pull with a plain message; a missing optional one is logged in `missing_fields`. Numeric SQL works whether a column is stored as number or text.
3. **(a)** Crashes with coordinates in the corridor's bounding box plus a margin (max(500 ft, radius, buffer) + 150 ft). **(b)** Crashes without coordinates in the same cities whose PrimaryRoad/SecondaryRoad mention the corridor street (SQL `LIKE`), then kept only if a road *normalizes* to the corridor street (#1's normalizer). (b) crashes are tagged `unmatched` until C4 places them.
4. **Parties + IWP** joined by Collision Id (150 ids per query). Witness-only IWP rows are skipped.
5. **Severity, counted once per crash at its most severe outcome:** KABCO from IWP `ExtentOfInjury`; any NumberKilled → K; injured with no IWP row → `U` ("injury, level not reported"), counted and never guessed. Mode flags (ped / bike / motorcycle / heavy truck) come from parties and collision fields.

**Cleaning log, counted per step:** rows read, outside window, CHP-deleted dropped, duplicate Collision Id (keeps the highest Report Version, counts what's dropped), `Is Preliminary` kept and counted, no-coordinate rows read / not on the corridor street, feet-typed-as-miles offsets fixed, cities, unknown injury values.

**Cache:** one pull per study in SQLite. A re-run uses it; `?refresh=true` re-pulls. Changing the window or the corridor re-pulls automatically. A data.ca.gov failure returns **502 with a message** after retries, never an empty list.

## Test data (offline)
The sandbox can't reach data.ca.gov. `tests/fixtures/ckan_crenshaw.json` is built by `make_ckan_crenshaw.py` from the **121 real CCRS Crenshaw crashes** in the mockup. Injury levels, parties and some codes are synthetic (documented in the script). Edge cases added: a deleted report, a duplicate with two versions, preliminary rows, no-coordinate rows (on the street / not / another city), a far-away crash. `sources/fake_ckan.py` loads it into SQLite and runs the **exact SQL the app sends** (kept to the Postgres/SQLite common subset).

**Live:** `tests/test_live.py` is skipped by default (`CRASHIQ_LIVE=1 make test-backend`). `backend/scripts/record_fixtures.py` now also prints which real CCRS columns every logical field resolves to and records one year's Crenshaw pull. ⚠️ For fields the earlier spike never used (PCF violation, surface, Parties vehicle type, IWP extent), the candidate column names come from the CHP layout doc. Run the recorder once on a connected machine to confirm them.

## Nuances touched (docs/06-nuances.md, for Hermes/the user)
- N1/N3: implemented as "one row per Collision Id after de-duplication, severity = most severe IWP extent". The KABCO mapping covers both the CCRS wording and the older SWITRS wording. Unknown values are listed in the log.
- New: injured but no IWP row → `U`. KSI is undercounted if IWP is incomplete; the profile caveat will show the count.

## Tests (+13, 1 live skipped)
Runtime resource and column resolution; text-vs-numeric SQL; counts for every cleaning step; the I-105 crash outside the box excluded; another city not pulled; non-corridor no-coordinate row dropped; duplicate keeps v2; severity once per crash (two C victims → one C crash; serious → A; missing IWP → U); parties and ped/motorcycle flags; generated SQL (bbox, names, city, IN lists); missing required column → clear error; missing year logged; CKAN retries then raises; API pull → cache hit with zero queries → refresh; window change re-pulls; 502 and 409/404 paths.

title: [C5] assign: intersection / segment / excluded by the 250 ft rule
body:
Closes #10

## Rules (`crashiq/assign.py`)
1. No coordinates yet → **`unmatched`**: counted, never dropped.
2. Within the study's influence radius (default 250 ft) of a **study** intersection → that intersection. Inside more than one radius → the **nearest**, which splits at mid-block when intersections are < 2 × radius apart. The rule lives in one function (`_pick_intersection`), so the formal HSIP < 500 ft rule (#3 Q6) can replace it alone.
3. Otherwise between A and B and within the corridor buffer → the **segment** it projects onto (by station along the drawn line).
4. Otherwise → **`excluded`**, with the reason: `outside_study_limits` or `outside_buffer`.

Per crash: `location_id`, `kind`, `distance_ft` (to the intersection centre, or perpendicular to the line for a segment), `rule`, and `location_provenance` carried through from the pull (`gps` / `unmatched`, later `exact` / `fuzzy` / `jev(p)` / `user`). Distances are in feet in the corridor's projected CRS.

**Not stored:** `GET /studies/{id}/assignment` recomputes from the cached pull every time, so a radius or buffer change applies immediately with no re-pull. The function asserts that intersection + segment + excluded + unmatched = total.

Unflagged (non-study) intersections attract no crashes. Crashes near them are segment crashes, matching R2.3's "between adjacent study intersections".

## Tests (+12, hand-built geometry in projected feet)
Exactly 250 ft → intersection; 251 ft → not; overlapping radii → nearest (both sides of the split); segment by projection, including the last segment to B; outside the buffer and past B excluded with the right reason; no coordinates → unmatched; a radius change re-assigns; an unflagged intersection doesn't attract; provenance carried through; **conservation** on 517 random crashes (17 with no coordinates); on the Crenshaw fixture, 124 crashes in both cases, 3 unmatched, and fewer intersection crashes at 150 ft than at 250 ft.

title: [C6] profile: deterministic crash profile tables (core)
body:
Closes #11

## What it does
`GET /studies/{id}/profile` returns the crash profile as **cited tables**: every number the user or the analyst will see. `GET /studies/{id}/profile/locations/{location}` returns the same distribution tables for one location, plus its crash list for drill-in. All in `crashiq/profile.py`; nothing is computed in the frontend or by AI.

| ID | Table |
|---|---|
| T1 | Study summary: crashes, per year, KSI, fatal, injury, PDO, people killed/injured, darkness, years, length, crashes per mile per year, unplaced, excluded |
| T2 | Locations in corridor order (intersections and segments interleaved): crashes, per year, KSI, fatal, injury, dark, ped, bike, length, crashes/mi/yr (segments), rate when AADT is entered |
| T3 | Severity, each crash counted **once** at its most severe outcome (K, A, B, C, U = injury level not reported, O) |
| T4–T8 | Collision type, primary collision factor, lighting, weather, road surface (crashes, injury, KSI, share) |
| T9 | Hour × day of week |
| T10 | Road users involved (ped, bike, motorcycle, heavy truck) |
| T11 | By year |

- **Cell addressing:** `"<table>/<row>/<column>"` (e.g. `T3/A/crashes`), resolved by `profile.cell()`. Per-location tables are `T4@<location id>`. The KPI strip is defined as cell addresses, so the UI only displays.
- **Rates only with AADT** (standard FHWA forms, unit-tested): segment = N × 10⁸ / (365 × years × AADT × miles) per 100M VMT; intersection = N × 10⁶ / (365 × years × (major + minor AADT)) per MEV. Without AADT the rate is `null` and the caveat "rates not computed" is added.
- **Provenance:** every table carries its location-provenance mix. `?exclude=jev` re-runs everything without Jev-placed crashes (J1 detail).
- **Caveats, computed and listed only when they apply:** preliminary reports, COVID year in the window, unplaced crashes (flagged as a data limitation above 10%, Q10), injury level not reported (KSI may be undercounted), years missing from CCRS, rates not computed, and provenance excluded.
- Scope: crashes placed at a study intersection or segment. Unplaced crashes appear in T1 and the caveats; excluded crashes count in T1.

## Assumption to confirm (nuance list)
- Intersection exposure = major-road AADT + minor-road AADT as entering vehicles (R3 says "major and minor approach AADT (entering vehicles)").

## Tests (+10)
Golden set: 50 placed crashes, 6 unplaced and 4 excluded, built by hand with every expected number worked out on paper (summary, locations, both rates, severity shares adding to the total, collision types, road users, year, hour × day). Plus: rate formulas, no AADT → rate null + caveat, caveats appear only when they apply (10.7% unplaced → limitation), provenance mix and the exclude-jev re-run, every KPI address resolves, and on the Crenshaw fixture T1 matches the assignment counts and the location drill-in matches T2.

title: [C6] Crash profile dashboard screen (step 3)
body:
Closes #12

## What it does
Step 3, **Crash profile**. On open it pulls the crashes (uses the cache after the first time, #9), then shows:
- **Severity-colored crash map** (the one loud element): fatal, serious, other injury, property damage. Injuries draw on top. Opening a location dims the rest.
- **4 KPIs**: Crashes, KSI, Injury crashes, Crashes per mile · year. Each is a T1 cell address given by the API (`profile.kpis`), so the UI only formats.
- **Caveats**, shown only when they apply (preliminary, COVID, unplaced with the >10% limitation flag in amber, unknown injury level, missing years, rates not computed).
- **Collision type bars** (T4, injury vs property damage), **hour × day heatmap** (T9), **locations table** (T2, corridor order; the Rate column appears only when AADT was entered).
- **Per-location drill-in:** severity, collision type, lighting and the crash records for that location (`/profile/locations/{id}`).

title: [C10] findings contract + validator (contract first)
body:
Closes #13

## Contract (`crashiq/findings.py`, JSON schema at `GET /findings/schema`)
```
Finding { id, location_id, text,
          numbers: [{ value, table_id, cell: "<row>/<column>" }],
          pattern_ref, evidence_refs: { tables: [...], records: { location_id, severity[], collision_type[],
                                         lighting_dark, ped, bike, day_of_week[], hour_from, hour_to, year[] } },
          status: proposed|accepted|rejected|edited, audit: {} (reserved, waits for #3 Q6) }
```
Cells are the C6 addresses from #11, including per-location tables (`T4@<location>`).

## Validator: a finding is rejected (logged with reasons, never shown) when
- it cites no table, or a cited table or cell doesn't exist;
- a declared number doesn't equal the cell it cites;
- **any number in the text** isn't backed by a cited cell: integers, decimals, thousands separators, percents, "3 of 5" (both numbers), and spelled-out two through twenty plus thirty/forty/fifty;
- its evidence filter selects **zero crash records**.

**The one rounding rule:** a number written with *d* decimals matches a cell value when the value, rounded half-up to *d* decimals, equals it. "38%" matches 38.46, "38.5%" matches 38.46, "38.4%" doesn't. Half-up, not banker's rounding.

**Allowed without a citation:** years inside the study window; ordinals in street names ("135th"); IDs like `T4` and `osm-123`; and numbers inside a *quoted* span only if that exact text appears in one of the finding's evidence records (CCRS codes like "VC 22350", road names). "one" isn't checked because it's usually a determiner; the analyst prompt (C9) will say to write counts as digits.

**Injection (§4 #12):** CCRS free text is matched as a string and never acted on. A quoted instruction carrying a number passes only if it's a verbatim record value. The same text unquoted, or quoted but in no record, has its numbers checked like any claim.

**API:** `POST /studies/{id}/findings` (array) → `{shown, rejected: [{id, reasons}]}`. Rejected ones go to `finding_rejected` and are never returned. `GET` lists the shown findings plus a rejected count. `PATCH …/findings/{id}?status=accepted|rejected|proposed` sets the user's decision. C9 will post here.

## Tests (+14 seam tests, docs/04 §4 #14)
Sourced finding passes; unsourced number (45%) rejected while a window year passes; wrong table / wrong value / missing cell; no table cited; rounding edges (40% / 40.0% pass, 39.6% / 40.4% fail; 38.46 → 38 / 38.5 but not 38.4; 2.5 → 3); spelled-out numbers; zero-record evidence; ordinals, thousands and IDs parsed right; injected CCRS text (verbatim quote ok, unquoted or fabricated quote rejected); API shows the valid one, logs the rejected one, and the rejected one can't be accepted.

title: [C15] budget: per-study AI spend cap + token/$ log
body:
Closes #14

## What it does (`crashiq/budget.py`)
- **One wrapper for Claude and Jev:** `Budget(db, study_id, cap).call(provider, model, step, est_input_tokens, max_output_tokens, fn)`. Before calling, it prices the *worst case* (estimated input + max output) and **refuses** if that would push the study past its cap. After the call it logs the actual tokens and dollars.

title: [C14] spine: read/write the Oracle project context object
body:
Closes #15

## What it does (`crashiq/spine.py`)
- **Import:** `PUT /studies/{id}/context` stores a context object from another tile (e.g. DemandIQ) verbatim and returns what CrashIQ can prefill: project name, termini, corridor line from `geometry_ref` (GeoJSON LineString/Feature or a coordinate list; GeoJSON lon/lat is flipped to lat/lon), intersections, functional class, setting. The Corridor screen starts from that line, and the user still runs detection and edits.
- **Export:** `GET /studies/{id}/context` returns the object with CrashIQ's results written in, following the spine rules:
  - **Additive:** a field another tile already filled is never overwritten. DemandIQ's `corridor.name`, `length_mi` and their provenance stay as they were.
  - `corridor.intersections[]` only if absent, from OSM (`method: auto`, or `manual` for user-added). Control is `signal`/`stop`/`null`, never guessed. Also `spacing_ft_to_next`.
  - `analysis.flags[]` += `data_gap` (unplaced share, missing CCRS years); `safety_pattern` stays empty until findings exist. `analysis.completed` += `crashiq_profile` (once). `data_holdings` += the CCRS pull (one per study, replaced on re-export).
  - **`safety` block** per docs/04 §3: window, `locate_summary` (gps/exact/fuzzy/jev/user/unmatched), `locations` (id, kind, crashes, KSI, crashes/mi/yr, rate). `safety.findings` stays `[]` in this issue.
  - **Provenance** (source, method, date) on every field written. `project.version` bumps when CrashIQ changes something.
  - **Unknown fields** (e.g. a `demand` block, `lane_profile`, generators) pass through untouched.

## Spine extension proposed (rule 4: extend in the spine, not privately)
For whoever maintains the oracle-spine skill; I didn't edit the skill:
```json
"safety": {
  "window": {"from_year": 2021, "to_year": 2025, "preliminary_included": true},
  "locate_summary": {"gps": 0, "exact": 0, "fuzzy": 0, "jev": 0, "user": 0, "unmatched": 0},
  "locations": [{"id": "", "name": "", "kind": "intersection|segment", "crashes": 0, "ksi": 0,
                 "crashes_per_mi_yr": null, "rate": null}],
  "findings": [{"id": "", "location_id": "", "pattern_ref": "", "evidence_refs": [], "status": "accepted"}]
}
```
Plus two optional keys on `corridor.intersections[]` items: `source_id` (the tile's own id) and `method`.

## Tests (+6 backend, +1 frontend)
Reads a DemandIQ-style object (`tests/fixtures/context_demandiq.json`) for prefill; writes results with provenance; never overwrites another tile's values and keeps unknown fields; **round trip** (export → import into a new study → export) stays stable with no duplicate `completed`, flags or holdings; export with no import starts from a blank object; `geometry_ref` forms. The Corridor screen starts from an imported line.

Union City Blvd (Jean Dr to Rocklin Dr) returned 0 crashes. CCRS has 227 Union City PD crashes in 2024 alone, 0 with GPS, several on the corridor (UNION CITY BL & DELORES DR, & ROSE WY).

## Causes

title: Fix #35: crashes found and placed in cities without police GPS (Union City)
body:
## What this fixes (rebased on current main, after #48)
The user's Union City Blvd study returned **0 crashes**. Union City PD records GPS on **0%** of its reports, so main's crash pull (which learns the county/city only from GPS crashes inside the corridor box) never searches the no-coordinate reports. Also, the locator validated in PR #16 isn't wired into the app, so no-GPS crashes are never placed.

1. **Area from street names when there's no GPS in the box** (`_area_by_street_names`): reports naming the corridor street **and** one of its study cross streets identify the county/city; then main's existing study-stretch filter (#48) runs unchanged.

title: Findings without AI: HSM over-representation + pattern library (#45)
body:
## What
The Findings step was empty: nothing generated findings (the Claude analyst waits for the API key, deferred). This adds the deterministic part, at zero AI cost.

- **C7 `patterns.py`:** for every intersection and segment, 9 patterns (broadside, rear-end, sideswipe, head-on, hit object, pedestrian, bicycle, dark, KSI) tested with the **HSM beta-binomial threshold-proportion test** (decision D2). Reference = the corridor's other locations of the same kind; flagged when ≥ 2 target crashes and P ≥ 0.90. Results are a cited table **T12** in the profile (so Excel/PDF and the validator see the same numbers).
- **C8 `config/pattern_library.json`:** a **seed** (HSM Ch. 6 / LRSM App. B): possible factors (intersection vs segment), field checks, countermeasure categories (for v3). **Awaiting the user's review**; per CLAUDE.md it changes only with approval.
- **Findings:** one templated finding per T12 row, every number cited to T12, run through the C10 validator. `POST /studies/{sid}/findings/generate` keeps the user's accept/reject on regenerate. The Findings screen generates on first visit and says plainly when nothing stands out.

## Results (live CCRS)
- Crenshaw (Marine → 132nd): 1 finding: hit-object crashes on the W 135th – W 132nd segment, 2 of 6 vs 8% on the corridor's other segments, P = 90%. Passed the validator.
- Union City (current corridor): nothing over-represented.

## Decision for the user (not taken here): how sensitive should it be?
When the corridor's locations have very similar shares, the HSM variance can't be estimated. My first fallback (uniform prior) flagged **5** patterns on Crenshaw, e.g. darkness at W 135th St, 12 of 20 crashes vs 42%. HSM logic says sites that agree should make flagging *harder*, so I switched to a conservative pooled prior, which flags **1**. Options: (a) keep conservative (fewer, stronger findings); (b) lenient (more candidates for the engineer to review); (c) show both, marking the lenient ones "possible". Recorded for docs/06-nuances.

## Checks
pytest 139 passed · vitest 28 passed · ruff + eslint clean · browser-checked on Crenshaw.

title: [Review] Step 3 ingest hardening: no silent undercounts
body:
Closes #47

These are the fixes from the 2026-10-18 independent review of the step 3 data pipeline. The data QA reviewer recomputed every number in the profile from the raw fixture rows with its own code and matched the app crash by crash (0 differences). Conservation holds: kept = placed + excluded + unmatched, and every table totals to T1. The problems below are ways real CCRS data could be silently miscounted that the fixture never exercised. Each one now has a test (`tests/test_ingest_hardening.py`, 13 tests).

## Ingest
- **Row cap:** `Ckan.sql` raises on `records_truncated`. Paging shrinks to the server cap and continues, ordered by Collision Id + Report Version so no row is skipped or repeated. Party and injury lookups split their id list when capped. A test with a 7-row cap gives identical results.
- **CHP coded values** are normalized once in the adapter: code-letter prefixes are stripped and "VEHICLE/PEDESTRAIN" becomes "VEHICLE/PEDESTRIAN". "Dark" matching is word-based. A test with CHP-style values gives identical results.
- **Dates:** ISO and `M/D/YYYY h:mm:ss AM` both parse. Unrecognized dates are counted, and more than 2% of them stops the pull, so it can no longer return 0 crashes as a success.
- **Coordinates outside California** (swapped, sign dropped, NaN) are treated as missing and counted, not lost.
- **No-coordinates search** covers the county (Crenshaw crosses Hawthorne/Gardena/LA), not only cities that already had a GPS crash. A crash is kept only when one road is the corridor street (address-style names included) and the other is a study intersection. Others are counted as `no_coords_off_study_stretch`.
  - **Effect on Crenshaw:** the fixture's Gardena crash at Crenshaw/135th is now found. Kept goes from 124 to 125 and unplaced from 3 to 4. Tests are updated with that reason.
- **Parties:** one row per (Collision Id, Party Number).
- **Freeway:** `IsFreeway` crashes are excluded under rule `freeway`. A ramp-terminal option is left for the user to decide (#34).
- **Missing tables / bad ids:** no crash table for any window year is an error. Id literals follow the column's datastore type (a text id compared to bare numbers fails in PostgreSQL).
- **Errors:** 400/409 bodies (the real SQL error) are kept in the message, and non-JSON responses are retried.
- **Fake CKAN** now treats double-quoted names as identifiers (PostgreSQL semantics) and can emulate a row cap.

## Using the data
- **Stale pull:** `for_study` returns 409 "The study changed since the crashes were pulled…" when the window, corridor or radius changed. `progress.crashes` is true only for a current pull.
- **Findings:**
  - `POST /findings` forces `status=proposed` and `source=analyst`, and gives a fresh id when the id is taken or `c7-…`, so nothing can approve itself or overwrite another finding.
  - Accepting re-validates the finding first (409 when stale) and records `decided_at`.
  - `GET /findings` re-validates every finding and marks stale ones. Stale accepted findings are left out of the PDF with a note. The UI shows a "Stale" badge and disables Accept.
- **PDF method statement:** data, years, the 250 ft / 100 ft rules, exclusions by rule, the unplaced count, the severity rule, and "does not compare … with statewide or peer-group averages". The unplaced caveat now names any fatal/serious crashes it hides (Crenshaw: 1).
- **Setup text** no longer says "every reported crash" or "what's going wrong".

## Live verification
`CRASHIQ_LIVE=1 make test-backend` now also runs `test_live_ccrs_contract`. It checks dates, unmapped injury values, the Parties join rate (≥90%), normalized collision types and lighting, and the implausible-coordinate share. It prints CKAN calls and wall time, and saves the live column types to `tests/fixtures/live/ccrs_fields_2023.json`.

title: Decision needed: how sensitive should the crash-pattern test be? (PR #46)
body:
Raised in PR #46 (Claude Code), needed for #45 / C7.

**What it is:** when the corridor's locations have almost the same share of a crash type, the HSM over-representation test can't estimate how much sites normally differ, so a fallback rule is needed. The fallback decides how easily a location gets flagged.

**Example (Crenshaw, Marine → 132nd, live CCRS):**
- Conservative fallback (current PR): **1** finding: hit-object crashes at W 135th – W 132nd, 2 of 6 crashes vs 8% on the corridor's segments, probability 90%.
- Lenient fallback (uniform prior): **5** findings, e.g. darkness at W 135th St, 12 of 20 crashes vs 42%.

**Options:**
- (a) Conservative: fewer findings, each stronger. **Hermes recommends this one**, because HSM says sites that agree should make flagging harder, and the engineer can still read every number in the profile tables.
- (b) Lenient: more candidates for the engineer to review, more false alarms.
- (c) Both: conservative findings shown normally, the extra lenient ones shown as "possible", one level down.

Related (PR #46 review item 3): when sites differ *a lot*, the code currently also uses the strict fallback. With (a) it stays strict; with (b)/(c) it would use the lenient rule.

The answer will be recorded in docs/03-requirements.md (under D2) and docs/06-nuances.md.

title: [C7] Screen to HSM: same-kind reference, HSM variance, rank by excess
body:
Closes #50

- **Same-kind reference:** each intersection is compared with the corridor's intersections, and each segment with the corridor's segments. T12 gets a "Compared with" column, and the finding text says "vs X% across the corridor intersections".
- **HSM variance:** s² = 1/(m−1)·[Σ(x²−x)/(n²−n) − (1/m)(Σx/n)²] over sites with n ≥ 2. A new test draws 3,000 sites from a known Beta(6,14): this variance recovers the true 0.01 within 15%, while the old raw-spread formula overstated it by more than 1.5×. The formula is from HSM Part B Ch. 4 as the domain reviewer gave it; please check it against your copy (noted in the module docstring).
- **Ranking:** sites passing the threshold are ranked by excess proportion (HSM), with probability as the tie-break.
- **Honest labels:** when the beta prior isn't valid (fewer than 3 sites, or no spread beyond noise), the value is labelled a binomial confidence in T12, the Findings audit and the PDF.

**Effect on Crenshaw:** with only 6 intersections, the beta prior is invalid for several crash types, so they use the binomial test. 135th St after dark is still the top finding: 12 of 20 (60%) vs 41.2% across the corridor intersections, binomial confidence 0.93, Moderate.

title: [C2/C5] Grade separations: don't count crashes on roads passing over or under the corridor (N7)
body:
## Goal
Crashes on a road that passes **over or under** the corridor (an interchange, overcrossing or undercrossing) are not counted for the corridor. On a freeway corridor, crashes on the crossing road and at the interchange are not counted as freeway crashes. User decision 2026-10-18 (docs/03, docs/06 N7). It goes with #39: only at-grade intersections the corridor passes through count.

## Why it leaks today
- The 100 ft buffer (C5) is 2D, so a crash on an overpass above the corridor falls inside it.
- `locate.py` treats streets within `NEAR_M` = 30 m as meeting even with no shared node (meant for ramps, medians and plazas). An overcrossing street passes that test, so its crashes place as if at an intersection.
- The corridor's intersection list comes from OSM shared nodes, but nothing checks `bridge`, `tunnel` or `layer` tags.
- Already handled: on arterial studies, CHP `IsFreeway` crashes are excluded by default (#34 item 9). That covers freeway mainline and ramps. It does **not** cover non-freeway grade separations, or freeway corridors.

## Component
C2 network (intersections), C4 placement (`locate.py`), C5 assign. `spine.py` already has an empty `corridor.grade_separations` slot to fill.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] C2 marks each crossing as `at_grade` or `grade_separated`, using OSM `bridge`/`tunnel`/`layer` tags and whether a node is shared. Grade separations are stored on the network and sent to the spine's `grade_separations`.
- [ ] Grade-separated crossings never count as corridor intersections: not in T2 locations, and the `NEAR_M` rule can't turn them into one.
- [ ] Arterial corridor: a crash whose other road is a grade-separated crossing (and not the corridor street) is excluded with rule `grade_separated_crossing`, counted and listed like buffer exclusions.
- [ ] Freeway corridor (corridor is a freeway): only crashes with `IsFreeway` on the corridor's route count. Crashes on the crossing road, at ramp terminals or on ramps are excluded with a rule, except ramps when the ramp-terminal include switch is on (#34 item 9).
- [ ] Tests on fixtures: an arterial under a freeway overpass, an arterial over a local street undercrossing, a freeway with a diamond interchange. Each test asserts the excluded count and rule.
- [ ] The Export / methods text says how grade separations are handled.

## Out of scope
Placement accuracy work (#17). Using route/postmile (TASAS) for state highways is a possible later improvement and needs its own issue.

## Depends on
#36 (no-GPS placement in the app) with #39 applied.

## Docs to read
docs/03 (#39 and N7 decisions, #34 item 9), docs/04 C2/C4/C5, docs/06 N4 and N7.

title: [C5] Apply the reported distance before excluding a crash referenced to a corner outside the study stretch
body:
## Goal
A no-GPS report referenced to a cross street that isn't one of the corridor's intersections is excluded by name today (`cross_street_not_on_corridor`, #39) **before** its SecondaryDistance/Direction is applied. If that outside corner is within a few hundred feet of a study end, the crash can physically sit inside the stretch and is wrongly left out.

Example: "Union City Blvd, 300 ft S of Whipple Rd" where Whipple Rd is 200 ft past the study end → the crash is ~100 ft inside the corridor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For excluded reports whose cross street meets the corridor street on the map (even outside the drawn stretch), place the corner, apply the reported offset along the corridor street, and run the normal C5 assignment (250 ft intersection / segment / outside study limits).
- [ ] Only if the offset point is still off the stretch does the crash keep `cross_street_not_on_corridor`.
- [ ] The Overpass fetch may need a wider margin along the corridor street to find nearby outside corners; measure the cost.
- [ ] Test: an outside corner 200 ft beyond the end with a 300 ft offset inward is kept; with an outward offset it stays excluded.

## Context
User discussion 2026-10-19 (Engineering session). 250 ft influence area confirmed (HSM / Caltrans HSIP). On Union City (study 51b98eedefd3) none of the 58 excluded corners appear in the downloaded map area, so the impact there is likely zero. Priority: low (user: backlog).

#36

title: [C2/C5] Grade separations (N7): roads over/under the corridor don't count
body:
## What this does
Rule N7 / #67 (user decision 2026-10-18): a road that passes over or under the corridor is not one of its intersections, and crashes on that road don't count.

**C2 network (`network.detect`)**
- A **grade separation** is a way that crosses the drawn line, within the study limits, without sharing a node with the corridor. Nodes of any way carrying the corridor's name count as corridor nodes, so short end pieces of the corridor street don't cause false hits. This was caught live on Dyer St, Union City.
- Two carriageways of the same road merge into one grade separation.
- `relation` = over / under / unknown, from `bridge` / `tunnel` / `layer` tags.
- Stored per corridor (migration 10). Corridors drawn before this are backfilled from the **cached** OSM response only; no new download.
- The corridor's road class is kept. On a **freeway corridor**, ramps and short freeway pieces are not intersections.

**C5 assign (`grade.py`)**
- A crash *on* the crossing road (CCRS PrimaryRoad names it, not the corridor) is excluded as `grade_separated_crossing`, counted and listed.
- A crash on the corridor that only uses the crossing as its reference point stays in. Example: `MAIN ST` / `RT 880`.
- **Freeway corridor:** only CHP IsFreeway crashes count. Others are excluded as `not_on_freeway` (the crossing road, ramp terminals). Ramp crashes are excluded as `ramp` unless the #34 item 9 include switch is on.
- **Arterial corridor:**
  - The IsFreeway rule is unchanged, so `freeway` still comes first.
  - With the include switch on, ramp crashes count and the freeway mainline above is still excluded, as `grade_separated_crossing`.

**Pull (no-GPS reports)**
- Reports on a crossing road are excluded and listed.
- Corridor reports referenced to a crossing are no longer excluded as side streets (#39).
- The pull cache key includes the grade separations, only when there are any, so cached pulls stay valid otherwise.

**Also**
- Names: FREEWAY / FWY / FRWY treated as one suffix.
- The spine's `corridor.grade_separations` is filled.
- Methods text says how grade separations are handled, and rule labels were added (including `cross_street_not_on_corridor`, missing since #36).
- Pain point 15 added to `knowledge/pain-points.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (#67)
- [x] C2 marks grade-separated crossings (bridge/tunnel/layer tags + no shared node), stores them, and feeds the spine.
- [x] They never count as intersections. The `NEAR_M` rule can't make one, because assign only uses network intersections. A near-placed crash at the crossing is a corridor crash, and `near` doesn't auto-place under the current gate.
- [x] Arterial: crashes on a grade-separated crossing are excluded as `grade_separated_crossing`, counted and listed.
- [x] Freeway corridor: IsFreeway only. Crossing road, ramp terminal and ramp crashes are excluded with a rule; ramps count when the switch is on.
- [x] Fixture tests: arterial under a freeway overpass, arterial over a local street, freeway with a diamond interchange. Each asserts the excluded count and rule.
- [x] Export / methods text.

## Checks
- pytest 199 passed, 2 skipped. Ruff clean.
- **Live, scratch DB, CCRS 2021–2025:**
  - **Crenshaw Blvd under I-405 (1.65 mi):** I-405 found as one grade separation ("over"), not an intersection. Ramp terminals stay at-grade intersections. 94 `freeway` + 1 `grade_separated_crossing` (`RT 405` without the IsFreeway flag).
  - **I-405 over Crenshaw (0.48 mi):** 0 intersections, Crenshaw found "under". 119 freeway crashes counted, 36 `not_on_freeway`, 12 `grade_separated_crossing` (crashes on Crenshaw below).
  - **The user's three studies:** no false grade separations.

## For the reviewer
- **Convention relied on:** PrimaryRoad = the road the crash happened on (CHP 555). It decides "on the crossing road" vs "on the corridor near it". Officers aren't always consistent, so this deserves a look in the Tester's statewide profile.
- **Changes `names.py`** (FWY suffix), which the PR #16 locator also uses. Unit tests pass, but the hidden-GPS validation wasn't re-run.

Closes #67

title: [Test] Statewide data test: every California city through tabs 1–2, Excel test report
body:
## Goal (user, 2026-10-19)
Run every California city through CrashIQ's data steps (tabs 1–2: crash pull and placement) and deliver a **professional test report as an Excel workbook**: how the testing was done, results per city, charts, and a conclusion on where it works and where it doesn't. Improvements get planned afterwards, from this report.

Owner: **Tester** session. It never changes app code. Real defects become `bug` issues with a failing test.

## How it runs (cost rule)
- Everything heavy runs as **Python scripts on the Mac**: CCRS queries, OSM downloads, and the app's own pull and placement code. No per-city work by hand, no AI steps, telemetry off.
- The session reads only the script's summary, never raw rows.
- TIMS: the user is signed in in the Tester browser panel. Download per county in as few clicks as possible (ask the user before each download), then compare with a script.
- Isolation (CLAUDE.md): own worktree, `data/tester.sqlite`, ports 8001/3101. Cache everything, so a rerun only redoes what changed.
- The workbook is **generated by the script** (openpyxl, native Excel charts), so rerunning refreshes it at no token cost. Output: `reports/testing/CrashIQ-statewide-test-<date>.xlsx`.

## Workbook sheets
1. **Summary:** test date, code version (git commit), data sources and years. Counts: agencies, cities, corridors, crashes tested. Pass/warn/fail counts. Charts: results by county, GPS rate by agency, top failure reasons. **Conclusion:** where it works and where it doesn't, each statement pointing to the sheet and cells behind it (code computes every number; the text only cites them).
2. **Method:**
   - how corridors were chosen per city (proposed: the longest major road, OSM primary/secondary, about 1 mile inside city limits);
   - years tested;
   - the pass/warn/fail rules;
   - what's excluded and why;
   - known limitations;
   - the exact command to reproduce the run.
3. **Cities:** one row per city: county, police agency, corridor tested (name and ends), crashes pulled, % with GPS, % placed by tier, % sent for review, excluded by rule (buffer, side street, freeway, grade separation), warnings, **result** and reason.
4. **Agencies:** statewide scan of how each reporting agency records crashes: GPS rate, street-name style, offsets present, blank fields, property-damage-only share, report versions, crashes piled on one point. Union City–type agencies flagged.
5. **TIMS vs CCRS:** by county and year: counts by severity, difference, likely reason (property-damage-only crashes, years not yet final, no location).
6. **Problems:** warn and fail cases grouped by cause, a few examples each, linked `bug` issues.
7. **Glossary:** every column and term in plain words.

## Pass / warn / fail (proposed, user to confirm on the first report)
- **Fail:** 0 crashes pulled while CCRS has reports naming the corridor in that city, or under 70% of crashes either GPS-located or placed.
- **Warn:** 70–90% located or placed, or more than 20% sent for review.
- **Pass:** 90% or more located or placed, and no silent drops.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Scripts in the repo (Tester's own folder, e.g. `tests/statewide/`) run end to end from one command; cached reruns are fast.
- [ ] The workbook has all 7 sheets, native charts, and freeze-panes and filters on the data sheets.
- [ ] Every number in Summary and Conclusion traces to a cell in the data sheets.
- [ ] The first run covers every incorporated city reachable through CCRS. Cities that couldn't be tested are listed with the reason, never skipped silently.
- [ ] `bug` issues filed for real defects, each with a failing test.
- [ ] Data discrepancies that matter to clients are added to `knowledge/pain-points.md`.
- [ ] PR with the scripts and the workbook; PM reviews and merges.

## Out of scope
Fixing what it finds (Engineering, via `bug` issues), and tabs 3–4 (charts and findings).

title: [Data] Placement checks (#53, part 1): road-name check, GPS flag, every corridor name
body:
**Stacked on #72 (#67).** The base is `feat/67-grade-separations` so the diff shows only #53. Retarget to `main` once #72 merges.

## What this does (#53 items)
| Item | Done |
|---|---|
| Flag GPS that disagrees with the stated road | GPS more than 400 ft (plus the reported offset) from the intersection the report names gets `gps_check: far_from_stated_intersection`. It's **counted where the GPS is, not moved**, and the profile caveat gives the count. Crenshaw: 1 (a ROSECRANS / CRENSHAW report whose GPS sits on a segment), the case the issue described. |
| Road-name cross-check for segment assignment | A GPS crash in the buffer or an influence area whose report names neither the corridor nor (at an intersection) that cross street is `excluded` as `not_on_corridor_street`. This applies the #39 rule ("only the corridor street and its own intersections") to GPS crashes. Blank road fields are kept, and placed crashes aren't checked (they were placed by those names). Crenshaw: 1 crash (134TH ST / ERIEL AVE). The tie rule (lower station) is now stated in the docstring and methods text. |
| IWP rows per report version | **Confirmed on live data:** CCRS has one row per Collision Id in every year 2016–2026. Only the latest version is published (versions go up to 1,326). IWP is unique by `InjuredWitPassId`. A stale v1 can't override v2 in the published tables. |
| Dedupe ties | The newest version wins even when it's the deleted one, so the crash is removed and older versions don't come back. Equal versions keep the first row read, counted as `version_ties_first_kept`. Live `IsDeleted` is never true (CHP removes the row instead), so this is a safeguard. |
| Exclude by provenance | T1 gets a "Crashes left out by placement method" row when the exclude-provenance rerun is used. Test: T1 rows add up to the assignment. |
| Fixture coverage (re-record + golden T1–T12) | **Not in this PR.** Part 2 follows: it's a large fixture change, kept separate so this one is reviewable. |

## Found along the way: corridor names change at city lines
OSM shows the Union City corridor's ways under two names. It's Union City Blvd in Union City and **Ardenwood Blvd** in Fremont, where Rancho Dr and Paseo Padre Pkwy sit. Fremont PD writes ARDENWOOD BLVD, so the pull never searched those reports.

The network now keeps every name and ref of the corridor's ways (migration 11, backfilled from the cached OSM response). They're used by the pull's name search, the road check and the grade rules. This also makes Nimitz Freeway = I 880 work on freeway corridors.

Union City study after a refresh: **21 → 30 intersection crashes**, 2 segment, 71 `cross_street_not_on_corridor`, 4 outside the buffer, 0 unplaced. The extra corridor names enter the pull cache key, so affected studies re-pull once. Pain point 16 and two lessons are recorded in `knowledge/`.

## Checks
- pytest 207 passed, 2 skipped. Ruff clean.
- Live checks ran on a backup copy of the local DB (`sqlite3 .backup`), not the shared file.

Refs #53 (part 1 of 2)

title: Bug: live CCRS injury codes (SuspectSerious, ...) not mapped to KABCO; A/B/C severity lost
body:
## What
Live CCRS `InjuredWitnessPassengers.ExtentOfInjuryCode` holds codes, not the text in the CHP data dictionary: `Fatal`, `SuspectSerious`, `SuspectMinor`, `PossibleInjury`, plus legacy `SevereInactive`, `OtherVisibleInactive`, `ComplaintOfPainInactive` (mostly 2016–2022). `ca_ccrs.KABCO` only knows the dictionary text, so only `Fatal` maps.

## Effect
On the user's Crenshaw study: 1 K, **0 A/B/C**, 131 U ("injured, level not reported"), 184 O. KSI counts only fatal crashes; T3 severity, KSI KPIs, findings and exports are wrong on every live study. Tests passed because the hand-built fixture used the dictionary text. Found while recording a live fixture for #53.

## Fix
Map both spellings: Fatal→K; SuspectSerious / SevereInactive→A; SuspectMinor / OtherVisibleInactive→B; PossibleInjury / ComplaintOfPainInactive→C (the standard SWITRS→KABCO crosswalk). A blank extent means no injury level for that person, not an unknown value. Cached pulls must be recomputed.

title: Fix: live CCRS injury codes → KABCO (A/B/C severity was lost)
body:
## Bug (#75)
Live CCRS `ExtentOfInjuryCode` holds **codes**, not the text in CHP's data dictionary:
- current KABCO codes: `Fatal`, `SuspectSerious`, `SuspectMinor`, `PossibleInjury`
- retired SWITRS levels that dominate older years: `SevereInactive`, `OtherVisibleInactive`, `ComplaintOfPainInactive`. In 2016, `SevereInactive` has 13,528 rows vs 11 for `SuspectSerious`.

`ca_ccrs.KABCO` only knew the dictionary text, so on live data **only `Fatal` mapped**. The user's Crenshaw study showed 1 K, **0 A / 0 B / 0 C**, 131 U. So KSI = fatal only, and T3, the KPIs, findings and exports were wrong on every live study. Tests passed because the hand-built fixture was written from the dictionary.

## Fix
- **Extent values matched with punctuation and spaces removed.** Both spellings map to KABCO, and the retired levels follow the standard SWITRS → KABCO crosswalk (severe → A, other visible → B, complaint of pain → C). Nuance N3.
- **A blank extent is no longer an "unknown injury value"**: it's an uninjured person or a witness.
- **`PULL_FORMAT` added to the pull cache key**, so every cached study re-pulls once and gets the corrected severity.
- **Recorded LIVE fixture** (`tests/fixtures/live/`, ~2 MB of public CCRS rows for the hand fixture's Crenshaw corridor) with `record_live_fixture.py`. Tests replay it through the real pull: Crenshaw stretch 2021–2025 is now **K 1, A 6, B 44, C 80, O 183**, with no unknown values.
- Lesson and pain point 17 in `knowledge/`.

## Checks
pytest 212 passed, 2 skipped. Ruff clean.

## Note for merging
- `knowledge/` will conflict with #74 (both add lessons and a pain-point row at the same place). Whichever merges second gets rebased; I'll do it.
- The live fixture was recorded with #74's corridor-name search. On `main` it replays 314 crashes, a subset; the severity test is pinned to the stretch.

Closes #75

title: [Data] #53 part 2: golden tables on live data, FakeCkan fix, one spelling per violation
body:
## What this does (#53, last item: "fixture coverage")
**Golden T1–T11 on LIVE data** (`tests/test_golden_live.py`): every profile number is recounted from the raw recorded CCRS rows by code that shares nothing with the app's cleaning (its own reading of CHP's injury codes, its own field parsing). It runs on two recorded corridors, 2021–2025:
- **Crenshaw Blvd**, LA County, GPS on most reports.
- **Union City Blvd**, the user's study. Union City PD records no GPS (#35), and the corridor is Ardenwood Blvd in Fremont.

The app still decides which crashes are in the study (assignment has its own tests). This checks that the tables count those crashes correctly from what CHP published. All tables match on both corridors.

**Fixture coverage:** a test pins that the live fixture keeps the cases the hand fixture lacked: a fatal, witness-only IWP rows, bicyclists, trucks, distances in miles (`M`), and `VC `-prefixed violations. The Union City fixture is recorded too.

## Two bugs found by it
1. **FakeCkan lost every no-coordinate row of live fixtures.** It built untyped SQLite columns, so `"County Code" IN ('1')` never matched the stored number 1, which PostgreSQL would match. Crenshaw replayed 314 of 1,602 crashes, and Union City replayed 0 while its golden checks "passed" on empty sets. Columns now take their CKAN types. The live-fixture test now asserts the replay returns all 1,602, and the pinned stretch severity moves to K1 A6 B44 C81 O185.
2. **One violation, several T5 rows.** CCRS writes `22350` and `VC 22350`; `21658A`, `VC 21658(A)` and `21658(a)`. `clean_violation` gives one spelling per Vehicle Code section; other codes (PC, ...) keep their prefix.

## Not in scope (noted for #52)
- PCF *category* (unsafe speed, right-of-way, ...): live CCRS has no category column, only the code A/C/D and the violation section, so #52 will need a section → category table.
- "Heavy truck" today = truck tractor only. 3+ axle trucks aren't counted. That's a definition for the user.

## Checks
pytest 247 passed, 2 skipped. Ruff clean.

Closes #53

title: Bug: real CCRS injury codes (SuspectSerious, SuspectMinor, PossibleInjury) all become U, so serious injuries are never counted
body:
## What's wrong
Live CCRS `InjuredWitnessPassengers.ExtentOfInjuryCode` holds codes, not phrases. 2024 statewide: `PossibleInjury` 117,616 · `SuspectMinor` 70,974 · `ComplaintOfPainInactive` 22,945 · `SuspectSerious` 15,354 · `OtherVisibleInactive` 8,694 · `Fatal` 4,075 · `SevereInactive` 1,922. `ca_ccrs.KABCO` only knows the spelled-out phrases from the synthetic fixture (`SUSPECTED SERIOUS INJURY`), so `severity()` returns **U** for every non-fatal injury crash. A/B/C are never assigned; KSI = fatal only in every real study. The values do show up in `cleaning.unknown_injury_values`, but nothing stops the study.

## Proof
`tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py::test_real_ccrs_injury_codes_map_to_kabco` (6 cases, strict xfail) — [file](https://github.com/redhawkliger/crashiq/blob/feat/73-statewide-test/tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py)

## Expected
SuspectSerious/SevereInactive → A, SuspectMinor/OtherVisibleInactive → B, PossibleInjury/ComplaintOfPainInactive → C, Fatal → K. (`*Inactive` look like the pre-2020 SWITRS levels; mapping them is N3, the user's call if unsure.) The fixture should be re-recorded from live data (#53).

Found by Tester, statewide data test #73. Priority: high (every severity number in tabs 3–4).

title: Bug: a hyphen in the OSM corridor name (Alvarado-Niles Road) stops every no-GPS report from being found (Union City)
body:
## What's wrong
OSM names the road `Alvarado-Niles Road`; Union City PD (0% GPS) writes `ALVARADO NILES RD`. `street_key` keeps the hyphen in the core, so the no-GPS search is `LIKE '%ALVARADO-NILES%'` against the squeezed column `ALVARADONILESRD` — never a match. Statewide run (#73): the app pulled 8 crashes; 58 no-GPS reports in Union City name the corridor and one of its study cross streets (e.g. 2459837 ALVARADO NILES RD & HARTNELL ST, 2474244 & SHERMAN DR).

## Proof
`tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py::test_hyphenated_corridor_name_finds_no_gps_reports` — [file](https://github.com/redhawkliger/crashiq/blob/feat/73-statewide-test/tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py)

## Expected
Hyphens (and other punctuation) are dropped on both sides of the LIKE, like spaces already are (`_SQ_DROP`). Check `same_core` too.

Found by Tester, #73. Priority: high (silent drop on the user's own study city).

title: Bug: one crash filed under two Collision Ids is counted twice
body:
## What's wrong
CCRS sometimes carries the same crash twice under different Collision Ids: same agency, Report Number, time and roads (e.g. CHP 9630-2023-00084 = Collision Ids 1975974 and 1975975, I-10 E/B & BOB HOPE DR, same GPS; Moreno Valley G232030005 = 2239535 v1 and 2543905 v2). 2023–24 statewide: 445 report numbers with 2+ Collision Ids and the same two roads (LAPD 77, LASD 49, Hesperia 27). The pull de-duplicates on Collision Id only and doesn't read Report Number.

## Proof
`tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py::test_same_crash_filed_under_two_collision_ids_counts_once` — [file](https://github.com/redhawkliger/crashiq/blob/feat/73-statewide-test/tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py)

## Expected
Read Report Number; collapse rows with the same agency + report number + same two roads (keep the highest version), log the count. Report numbers alone are **not** unique (SFPD reuses them for different crashes, knowledge/sources/ca-ccrs.md), so the road match matters. The exact rule may need the user's OK (one count per crash, N1).

Found by Tester, #73.

title: Bug: a 'NOT STATED' cross street is excluded as a side street named NOT STATED
body:
## What's wrong
CCRS 2024: SecondaryRoad is `NOT STATED` on 4,649 rows and `PRIVATE PROPERTY` on 644 (plus 1–2 letter junk). Santa Monica PD (8% GPS) has no usable cross street on 16% of its street crashes, Signal Hill (1% GPS) 15%, Riverside 16%. The no-GPS filter reads `NOT STATED` as a street, finds it isn't a study cross street and lists the crash as `cross_street_not_on_corridor` (the #39 side-street rule). The report says nothing about a side street.

title: Fix #84: empty Overpass answer is retried, never cached
body:
## Bug (#84, found by Tester #73)
Under load, overpass-api.de sometimes answers a valid corridor query with **0 elements and no remark**: 7 of 14 calls in the statewide run. `fetch_overpass` accepted that and cached it under the query key. The study then had no corridor street and no intersections, only the GPS crashes in the box, and gave no error.

## Fix
- **Empty answers are failures:** 0 elements counts as a failed attempt, so it's retried with back-off and never written to the cache. If every attempt is empty, a `NetworkError` says "Overpass returned no streets", which the API turns into the existing 502 message.
- **Old empty saves count as missing:** an empty answer cached before this fix is treated as a cache miss and downloaded again. The local DB has none (checked: 0 rows), but other copies might.

## Reproduced live
My own same-basis run for #80 (2026-10-20T04:34Z, Tester's UNIONCITY_1 line) got `osm_elements: 0` from Overpass. Both runs came back with no corridor street (332 rows, all freeway/buffer exclusions). The retry a minute later returned 312 elements.

## Tests
- The Tester's test, without the xfail: an empty answer raises and caches nothing. It's extended with empty-then-real (retried, cached) and a previously cached empty map (downloaded again).
- pytest 252 passed. Ruff clean.

Closes #84

title: Fix #82: 'NOT STATED' cross street is no longer called a side street
body:
## Bug (#82, found by Tester #73)
CCRS 2024: SecondaryRoad is `NOT STATED` on 4,649 rows and `PRIVATE PROPERTY` on 644, plus 1–2 letter junk. The no-GPS filter read `NOT STATED` as a street name, found it wasn't a study cross street, and listed the crash under `cross_street_not_on_corridor` (#39's side-street rule). The report says nothing about a side street.

**Open choice for the user (not made here):** whether `no_cross_street` crashes should go to the review list instead, since they are on the corridor but at an unknown place. PM, please put it to the user.

## What this does (#54, part 1)
| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| Rows thrown away after the join | Excluded reports are listed but **not looked up** in Parties/IWP: side street, grade separation, no cross street, private property. Their severity is `None` and `details: "not_looked_up"`. GPS rows farther than the box margin from the line stop before the lookups. Recorded Crenshaw replay: **id lookups 24 → 9, SQL calls 34 → 19**. |
| Parties/IWP batching | 500 ids per query (600 checked live). |
| Column lookups per resource | Live `package_show` and column lists are cached per process for 24 h. Before, every pull made 15+ metadata calls. SQL is never cached. |
| Cache key / TTL | `PULL_FORMAT` (from #75) already versions the cleaning. A pull whose window reaches last year expires after **30 days**, because CHP keeps revising preliminary reports; final years never expire. OSM expires after **180 days**, the old map is kept if the refresh fails, and an empty map never counts (#84). |
| Overpass `Retry-After` | Honoured on 429/503 (capped at 120 s). |
| Postgres-safe numeric cast | Not needed live: Latitude/Longitude are `numeric` columns in every CCRS year, so no cast runs. FakeCkan typed columns came with #78. |
| Call-count regression tests | `tests/test_pull_efficiency.py`. |

## Where the time actually goes (measured live, 2026-10-20)
Union City line (`tests/fixtures/live/line_unioncity.json`), 2016–2025:
- About **40 SQL calls in sequence, ~60–80 s**.
- One at a time, an indexed Parties lookup returns in **0.4–0.6 s** for 3 to 300 ids.
- With 4 queries in flight (while Tester's statewide run was also using data.ca.gov from this IP), the same lookups took 4–12 s. Requests queue on the server.

**So parallel queries were tried and set aside** (not in this PR). I'll re-time sequentially once Tester's run ends. The remaining lever is part 2: run the pull as a background job with progress, so the 1-minute wait isn't a frozen request.

## Choices made here (engineering defaults, easy to change)
- **30-day expiry** for recent windows and **180-day** OSM expiry. These are not recorded user decisions. Say if they should go to the user.

title: [Perf] #54 part 2: background pull with progress, memoized assignment, slim GET /crashes
body:
## What this does (#54, part 2)
| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| Background pull with progress | `POST …/crashes/pull?background=true`: a valid cached pull answers at once (200, as before). Otherwise the pull starts in a thread and answers **202** with `{"job": …}`. `GET …/crashes/pull/status` gives `{state, step, done, total}`, for example "Crash reports 2023 · 3 of 5" or "Parties and injuries 2024". Errors come back as `state: "error"` with the HTTP status and message (502 data.ca.gov / Overpass, 409 pull rules). Without `background`, the endpoint behaves as before. |
| Per-study lock | One pull at a time per study, whether in a request or a thread. A second background request joins the running job. |
| Compare-and-set on `cache_key` | The result is stored only if the study still has the same key when the pull ends. If the corridor or window was edited mid-pull, it pulls once more for the new study, then gives up with a clear 409. |
| Memoize assignment/profile | `for_study` reads only `cache_key`/`pulled_at` first and memoizes (pull, assignment) on pull key + time, radius, buffer, freeway switch and a network hash (16 entries). The profile, map, findings and exports no longer each reload the multi-MB pull and re-assign it. |
| Don't return the whole pull | `GET /crashes` leaves out each crash's party list, which the screens never read. `?full=true` returns it. |
| Frontend | The Crash profile screen uses the background pull and shows the current step under the existing "Pulling crashes…" message. Same layout, one muted mono line. "Pull fresh data" uses it too. |

## Checked in the app
Branch backend + built frontend on :8004, against a **copy** of the local DB. Opening the user's Union City profile (its old pull is invalid after `PULL_FORMAT`) showed "Crash reports 2021 · 1 of 5" while pulling. It finished (107 rows) and the profile appeared by itself: 32 crashes, KSI 1.

## Tests
- `tests/test_background_pull.py`: 202 + progress then the summary; a cached pull answers 200; progress names each step; two requests share one pull; a failed pull reports 502 + reason; a study edited mid-pull is pulled again and not stored stale; the assignment is memoized until an input changes.
- Slim vs full GET /crashes.
- Profile screen: the step shows, then the profile; a failed background pull shows the reason.
- pytest 275 passed, 2 skipped, ruff clean. vitest 45 passed, eslint clean.

## Not in this PR
- **Parallel data.ca.gov queries:** measured, they don't pay (requests queue server-side; see #93). Shelved.
- **Store crashes as rows instead of one JSON blob:** memoization removes the repeated parsing, which was the cost. A schema change can wait until a measured need.
- **Perf test at 20k crashes:** needs a synthetic 20k fixture. I'd do it when we have a corridor that big.

Closes #54

Any spelling of the corridor (`SOUTH CRENSHAW BLVD`, `CRENSHAW BLVD; MCDONALDS`, an address on it) groups under the corridor's name. The response also lists the decisions already made and where each one landed.
- **`POST …/review/decisions`:** for one crash or a whole group, place `{method: suggestion | intersection | map}` or exclude `{reason}` (a reason is required). Group "at suggestion" places only the crashes that have one.
- **`POST …/review/undo`:** reverts the last batch and restores any earlier decision for those crashes.
- **Decisions are an overlay, never written into the pull.** They're applied inside `for_study` on every read, so the profile, findings and exports all see them, and the assignment memo key includes them:
  - **Placed:** provenance **`user`**, assigned by the normal rules. A point off the buffer is still excluded by code, and the list shows that.
  - **Excluded:** rule `user_excluded`.
- **Re-pulls:** decisions are matched by Collision Id and survive a re-pull. A changed report version brings the crash back with reason `report_changed`, showing the old decision. If the crash now has GPS, the GPS wins.
- **T1:** new row "Crashes placed by you (included in Crashes)". The table still adds up: user-placed crashes are in Crashes, user exclusions in Excluded.
- **Excel / PDF:** a new "Review decisions" sheet lists each one with action, method, reason, where it was assigned, and whether it still applies. The methods text names `user_excluded`.
- Nothing is learned across studies; no alias table is fed.

**Frontend**
- **Entry:** on Crash profile, "N crashes are not placed yet. Review them →" opens the list in the data column (the same layout as the location drill-down).
- **Actions:** per group and per crash: At suggestion / At an intersection (a select) / On the map / Exclude (a reason field). "On the map" makes the profile map's next click the location (crosshair cursor). That's the only map change: an opt-in `onPick` prop.
- **Undo and outcomes:** an undo link, plus a "Decided" list showing where each placement landed, e.g. "→ West 132nd Street" or "→ not counted: outside the corridor buffer".

## Also fixed here
- **Memo bug from #98:** two pulls in the same second share `pulled_at`, so the memoized assignment could keep the old pull. Storing a pull now clears the study's memo entries.
- **`PULL_FORMAT` 2 → 3:** #80–#83 and #94 changed what a pull holds without bumping it, so saved pulls kept their old exclusions. On the local Crenshaw study, the 16 no-cross-street crashes only reached review after this bump. Every study re-pulls once.

## Checked in the app
Branch backend + build on :8005, against a copy of the local DB. Crenshaw (fb6e39a99490) re-pulled in the background and showed "16 crashes are not placed yet":
- **Grouping:** CRENSHAW BOULEVARD / NOT STATED (16) and 132ND ST / CRENSHAW BOULEVARD (1, suggestion `relaxed`).
- **On the map:** I clicked a point ~700 ft off the line. The crash showed as decided, and the code excluded it as outside the buffer, so T1 is unchanged.
- **Undo:** back to 17 open.
- **At suggestion:** counted at **West 132nd Street**, and the profile went from 191 to 192 crashes. Undone again afterwards.

## Tests
- **`tests/test_review.py` (12 tests):**
  - grouping and counts match T1
  - place at an intersection: `user` provenance, counted there, T1 `user_placed`
  - map placement assigned by the rules
  - off-corridor placement shows as not counted
  - exclusion needs a reason
  - group action + undo
  - undo restores the previous decision
  - suggestion with no suggestion is refused
  - decisions survive a re-pull
  - a revised report comes back as `report_changed`
  - unknown ids are refused
  - the export lists decisions
- **Profile screen:** open the list → exclude a group with a reason → profile reloaded, undo enabled; place at an intersection.
- pytest 287 passed, 2 skipped, ruff clean. vitest 47 passed, eslint clean.

Closes #97

## Goal

title: [Tab 3] A. Corridor strip diagram
body:
## What this does (#102)
"Where along the corridor crashes bunch up": a section on the Crash profile, in the data column under the key numbers.
- **The line:** the corridor runs A → B as a straight line, true to scale by station. Study intersections are ticks with short names ("W 135th St"), placed on two staggered rows so they never overlap. A name that doesn't fit is left to the hover title.
- **The dots:** one per placed crash, stacked at its station, most severe at the bottom, coloured like the map. Fatal and serious dots are slightly bigger. A stack taller than 24 ends in "+n", so drawn dots plus the "+n" counts equal T1 crashes.
- **Interaction:**
  - Hover a dot: type, date and hour, severity.
  - Click a dot or a tick: opens the existing location drill-down.
  - Toggle: colour by Severity (default) or Collision type.
- **Not drawn:** review-list and excluded crashes, with a one-line note of their counts from T1.
- **Exact numbers:** "Show table" gives location, distance from A and crashes, from T2.

**Data:** the assignment API now returns `station_ft` for intersection crashes (the intersection's station); segment crashes already had it. The frontend computes no statistic: it draws stations and colours.

## Colour finding (for PM / the user, not changed here)
The dataviz validator **fails the app's existing severity colours** on the dark surface:
- Serious injury `#FF8A3D` vs other injury `#FFB020`: ΔE 9.5 for normal vision (the floor is 15) and 6.7 for deutan.
- The grey for property damage is below the chroma floor; it's deliberate, but it fails as a category.

The strip keeps the map's colours for consistency and compensates with bigger K/A dots, a legend and the exact table. Re-stepping the severity colours is an app-wide design decision, so it's flagged separately rather than changed in this PR.

## Checks
- **Measured in the app** (Crenshaw, DB copy) at 1440 and 768 px:
  - 6 labels, **0 overlaps**, 0 outside the strip, no text over dots
  - 171 dots + "+4/+8/+8" = 191 = T1 crashes
- **Tests:**
  - `strip.test.js`: short names; no label overlap at 400, 600, 768 and 1440 px for Crenshaw and the dense 10-intersection Union City corridor
  - Profile screen: dots = T1 crashes, hover tooltip, colour toggle, Show table = T2, click → drill-down
  - Backend: every placed crash has a station (unit test, plus both live golden corridors)

title: [Tab 3] Severity colours: one legible K/A/B/C/O ramp app-wide (colour-blind safe)
body:
## Goal
Make the severity colours (K / A / B / C / O) clearly distinguishable everywhere: 3D map, strip diagram, severity bars, location ranking, exports. The user asked for visuals that are "clean, clear, legible" (2026-10-19). Today serious injury `#FF8A3D` vs other injury `#FFB020` is ΔE 9.5 for normal vision and 6.7 for deutan (validator floor 15), and the property-damage grey is below the chroma floor (found in PR #107).

## Approach
- One severity ramp defined once (design tokens) and used by every view; no per-view colours.
- An ordered ramp: fatal is the strongest (keep red), then serious, other visible, possible, then property damage as a quiet neutral that still reads as a category.
- It must pass the dataviz validator for normal, deutan, protan and tritan vision on the app's dark background. Keep the secondary encodings: bigger K/A marks, direct labels, tables.
- Same ramp in Excel/PDF exports.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The validator passes for every adjacent pair, normal and colour-blind, on the dark surface; the result is in the PR.
- [ ] Map, strip diagram, severity bars and exports all use the token; a test or lint check prevents hard-coded severity hex values.
- [ ] Before/after screenshots of the Crenshaw profile in the PR.

## What this does (#103)

**Data:** so the frontend only sorts and draws, T2 gains per-location `sev_k … sev_o` (summing to crashes; K + A = KSI) and `rate_to_critical` (rate ÷ critical rate). Both are new T2 columns, so they appear in the export too.
