title: [Design] One validated K/A/B/C/O severity ramp, app-wide and in exports
body:
## What this does (#108)
One severity ramp, defined once and used everywhere: 3D map, strip diagram, location ranking bars, severity summary, collision diagram, and the Excel and PDF exports.

| Level | Colour | Was |
|---|---|---|
| K Fatal | `#d9003b` | `#FF5A4E` |
| A Suspected serious | `#d37e01` | `#FF8A3D` |
| B Suspected minor | `#666800` | `#FFB020` (shared with C/U) |
| C Possible | `#19a0b8` | `#FFB020` (shared) |
| O Property damage | `#6f57ab` | `#8E9AA6` (grey) |
| U Injured, level not stated | `#8e9aa6` (neutral grey: an unknown, not a level) | shared amber |

**Where it lives:**
- **Backend:** `backend/crashiq/severity.py`; the exports use it.
- **Frontend:** `frontend/src/lib/severity.js` for the map layers, plus the `--sev-*` tokens in `app.css`.
- **Kept identical by a test.** The map's severity colour-by now shows K / A / B / C / O as separate categories, with U only when present. Before, B, C and U were merged as "Other injury".

## Validator results (dataviz `validate_palette.js`, OKLab ΔE×100, Machado CVD)
| Surface | Pairs | Lightness | Chroma | CVD (protan/deutan) | Normal vision | Contrast |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dark `#14181C` | adjacent | PASS | PASS | **PASS**, worst 11.4 | **PASS**, worst 19.4 | PASS ≥ 3:1 |
| White (exports) | adjacent | PASS | PASS | **PASS**, worst 11.4 | **PASS**, worst 19.4 | PASS ≥ 3:1 |
| Dark / white | all pairs | PASS | PASS | WARN, worst 7.5 (K ↔ B) | PASS, worst 19.4 | PASS |

**Why the all-pairs result is a WARN:** 7.5 sits in the 6–8 band, which the method allows only with secondary encoding. Those encodings are kept: bigger K/A marks on the map and strip, direct labels and legends, and "Show table" everywhere. A search over five-colour ramps found none that clears 8 on all pairs on both surfaces. The method's answer in that case is secondary encoding, not a forced palette.

**How the ramp was found:** I didn't pick it by eye. A hill climb from a hand-picked ramp kept only ramps where every adjacent check passes on both surfaces, and maximised the worst all-pairs colour-blind separation.

## Exports
- **Excel:** the T3 (and per-location T3) sheets colour each severity row's key cell.
- **PDF:** the severity table gets a colour swatch column.

## Lint
`tests/test_severity_colors.py`:
1. The backend, the JS module and the CSS tokens are identical.
2. No other frontend file contains a ramp colour, or builds its own severity map from literal hex (the old `SEV = { K: '#…' }` pattern).
3. The exports carry the ramp.

Theme colours that happen to share an old hex (traffic lamps, LOS colours, muted grey) aren't severity and stay.

## Before / after (Crenshaw, DB copy)
Before: three colours, with "Other injury 84" merged. After: Fatal 0 · Serious 4 · Minor 26 · Possible 58 · Property damage 103, each distinct on the map chips and the strip. I compared the two live servers side by side. I couldn't attach the screenshots through the CLI; PM, please check them visually as usual.

## Checks
pytest 295 passed, ruff clean. vitest 57 passed, eslint clean.

Closes #108

title: Bug: one wrong-county GPS crash in the corridor box sends the no-GPS search to the wrong county (Marina)
body:
## What's wrong
`crashes.pull` takes the county for the no-GPS name search from the GPS crashes inside the corridor box. If those are all from another county, the search goes there and every no-GPS report on the corridor that year is missed, silently.

Statewide run (#73), Marina (Monterey, county 27), Reservation Rd, 2021: the only GPS crashes in the box are two **Woodland PD** reports (Yolo, county 57): ids 2796970 and 2829517, `ELM ST & COURT ST` / `ELM ST & PENDEGAST ST`, which are Woodland corners, with GPS at 36.67, -121.78 in Marina. The pull searched county 57 for 2021 and missed every Marina no-GPS report that year (10 of Marina's 11 silent drops, e.g. 2747309 RESERVATION RD & IMJIN PW). Same in 2023, when county 57 was searched alongside 27.

Wrong-county GPS is common (Agencies sheet in the #73 workbook: GPS outside its own county).

## Proof
`tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py::test_wrong_county_gps_crash_does_not_redirect_the_no_gps_search` (strict xfail).

## Expected
The search area shouldn't rest on GPS crashes alone: always include the area found from the reports' street names (corridor street + a study cross street), and/or the county the corridor actually lies in. A GPS crash whose county disagrees with where its point is shouldn't define the area.

Found by Tester, #73.

title: [Test] Statewide data test: every California city through tabs 1–2, Excel test report (#73)
body:
Closes #73. Tester session; no app code changed (`backend/`, `frontend/` untouched).

## What it is
Every incorporated California city in CCRS (524) is run through CrashIQ's data steps (corridor → crash pull → placement → assignment) through the app's own API, in-process. The run writes an Excel workbook: `reports/testing/CrashIQ-statewide-test-2026-10-20.xlsx`.

## Run 1 (baseline), same basis (PR #86)
- **App code:** backend last changed in b590586 (tree 6f8d98257e56). The fixes merged since (#76 is in; #87/#89/#91 and the #82/#83 fixes came later) belong to the before/after rerun.
- **Crashes:** CCRS 2021–2025 by crash date, from a local mirror copied 2026-10-19 20:54. Preliminary records are kept and flagged.
- **Settings:** radius 250 ft, buffer 100 ft, freeway excluded.
- **Streets:** Geofabrik California extract dated 2026-10-18 (user OK for the download). Overpass rate-limited this machine. Against 28 real Overpass answers the extract gives a 99.92% road-way match, and all 28 corridors get the same corridor name and the same intersection list.
- **Corridors:** frozen in `tests/statewide/corridors_frozen.json`, which the rerun reuses unchanged.

| Measure | Run 1 |
|---|---|
| Cities | 524: 403 pass · 39 warn · 26 fail · 56 untested, each with a reason (campuses, parks, airports, OSM gaps such as Compton and Rosemead) |
| Corridor crashes located (GPS or auto-placed) | 96.4% of 36,195 · 2.1% review · 1.5% unplaced |
| Silent drops | 61 (Union City 48 and Saratoga 1: #80; Marina 11: #111) |
| Double counts among pulled crashes | 166 (#81) |
| TIMS counties within 2% (F+I, 2021–24) | 22 of 58 |

## Workbook sheets
Summary (every number is a formula over the data sheets; the conclusion sentences quote those cells), Method, Cities, Agencies (535 agencies), Fields (live coded values vs the CHP dictionary), TIMS vs CCRS, Problems, Run history + City by run (from `run_history.csv`, append-only, measure definitions versioned), Before-after (filled in by the rerun), Glossary. All data sheets have filters and frozen header rows; charts are native Excel charts.

## Bugs filed (failing tests in `tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py`)
#79 (fixed by #76), #80, #81, #82, #83, #84: all pass on current main and stay as regression tests. **#111** (a wrong-county GPS crash redirects the no-GPS search, Marina) is still open and kept as a strict xfail. Suite: 300 passed, 1 xfailed.

## Findings for the user (knowledge/pain-points.md rows 18–24)
- 61 local agencies filed under half their 2016–19 reports in a year since 2021 (Gardena, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Culver City, Palo Alto; LAPD at 28%). TIMS has the same gaps.
- Police GPS snapped to the intersection (Santa Ana 63% of reports placed > 250 ft away). Needs a user decision on which clue wins.
- CCRS runs 2.5–4% above TIMS on F+I, fatal and serious crashes. San Luis Obispo's +17% is state-park and campus crashes.
- Parties 2025 isn't published on data.ca.gov.

## Open user decisions (not settled here)
Pass/warn/fail thresholds (#73 proposal), the snapped-GPS rule, and a warning when an agency's reporting collapses.

title: Bug: corridor name starting with a direction (East Colorado Blvd) pulls 0 crashes (Pasadena)
body:
## Bug (found in the PM review of #112, statewide run 1)
A corridor whose OpenStreetMap name starts with a direction ("East Colorado Boulevard", "East Hobsonway") pulls **0 crashes**, even when CCRS has many reports naming the street without the direction.

## Evidence (CCRS mirror, Tester's run 1, frozen code b590586)
- **Pasadena:** test road "East Colorado Boulevard". The app pulled **0** crashes. CCRS 2021 alone has **48** Pasadena reports with PrimaryRoad `COLORADO BL` (no GPS) and 2 with `E COLORADO BL`. Pasadena has 8,751 crashes in 2021–25.
- **Blythe:** "East Hobsonway", 0 pulled. CCRS has 285 Blythe crashes.
- **Possibly related:** Solana Beach "South Coast Highway", where CCRS writes `SOUTH HIGHWAY 101`; that may be a route alias. Several small cities in the same list ("North Center Street", "West Manning Avenue").
- The run classed these as "untested: no CCRS report names this corridor". They are silent failures.

## Likely cause
The no-GPS SQL name prefilter (`_corridor_cores` / `_like` in crashes.py) squeezes the full core including the leading directional (e.g. `ECOLORADO`), so `LIKE '%ECOLORADO%'` never matches `COLORADOBL`. `same_core` in Python allows a directional missing on one side; the SQL prefilter doesn't.

## Fix (obvious mistake, no user decision needed)
- The SQL prefilter also searches the core **without** a leading directional (and with N/S/E/W abbreviations), so it's a superset. The Python matching then decides, as now.
- Check the GPS path for the same issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Failing test first: a corridor named "East Colorado Boulevard", fixture reports `COLORADO BL` and `E COLORADO BL` → both pulled.
- [ ] Same for West / North / South and the abbreviated forms.
- [ ] Locator re-validation unchanged (SF / LB), since `names.py` may be touched.
- [ ] Tester re-runs Pasadena and Blythe on the frozen corridors (same basis) and they're no longer 0.

title: Fix #113: corridor names starting with a direction pull 0 crashes (+ HTTP 414 on big cities)
body:
## Bug (#113, statewide run 1)
A corridor whose OSM name starts with a direction pulled **0 crashes**: Pasadena "East Colorado Boulevard", Blythe "East Hobsonway". The SQL prefilter searched the squeezed core with the direction (`EASTCOLORADO`), which never matches reports that write `COLORADO BL`. Python matching (`same_core`) already allowed the missing direction; SQL didn't.

## Fix 1: direction-free search core
`_search_core` searches the core **without** a leading direction for the corridor and its cross streets. That's a superset, since `COLORADO` is inside both `COLORADO BL` and `E COLORADO BL`, so Python still decides exactly as before. A core too short on its own (`1ST` from W 1ST ST) keeps its direction, so the search doesn't flood. `names.py` is unchanged, so no locator re-validation is needed.

## Fix 2, found while checking Pasadena: HTTP 414 (URI too long) on big cities
data.ca.gov takes the SQL in the URL, so Pasadena failed **on main** too, before reaching the names:
- **Area-by-street-names query:** repeated the 6-deep REPLACE chain for every corridor spelling × every cross street, 12 KB for 17 cross streets. It now squeezes each road column **once** in a subquery and compares short aliases. A cross list still too long is split and the counts added.
- **No-GPS name query:** same subquery form.
- **Parties/IWP id lookups (from #93):** 500 ids with the full column list could exceed the limit. Lookups now split by encoded URL length (`MAX_URL_SQL = 6000`), not only by id count.

`PULL_FORMAT` 3 → 4, so saved pulls refresh.

## Same-basis check (Tester's frozen corridors, run 1 code version 6f8d98257e56, 2021–2025, radius 250 / buffer 100, freeway off)
data.ca.gov pulled 2026-10-21T00:31Z.

| Corridor | Tester run 1 | main (c1df6ff) | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pasadena, East Colorado Blvd | 0 pulled, "untested" | **HTTP 414** (no result) | **1,212 kept**: 1,109 cross street off the stretch, 2 intersection, **101 unplaced** (review list) |
| Blythe, East Hobsonway | 0 pulled, "untested" | 0 kept | **36 kept**: 35 cross street off the stretch, 1 freeway |

**For the user / #17, not changed here:** the 101 unplaced Pasadena crashes aren't auto-placed because the locator rates `COLORADO BL` vs OSM `East Colorado Boulevard` as **relaxed**, not exact, and the gate auto-places exact only (PR #16 decision). Whether a missing leading direction counts as exact is a gate decision. Tester: please re-run Pasadena and Blythe on this branch to confirm against your independent count.

## Tests
- **Failing test first:** East Colorado Blvd, West Manning Av, North Center St and South Coast Hwy, each with reports written with and without the direction → all found.
- **Search core:** the direction is dropped, but not down to "1ST".
- **Id lookups:** stay under the URL limit for 1,200 ids × 26 columns.
- pytest 303 passed, ruff clean.

Closes #113

title: Fix #111: a wrong-county GPS crash can't redirect the no-GPS search
body:
## Bug (#111, Tester #73)
The county/city searched for no-GPS reports came only from the GPS crashes in the corridor box. In Marina (Monterey, 27), 2021, the only GPS crashes in the box were two Woodland PD reports (Yolo, 57; `ELM ST & COURT ST`). The pull searched county 57 and missed every Marina no-GPS report that year.

## Fix
- **The street-name area is always searched.** That's the area found from reports naming the corridor plus a study cross street (#35). It's found once per pull, and tried again each year until a year has such reports.
- **GPS crashes only add their area if their own report names the corridor street.** Woodland's `ELM ST & COURT ST` doesn't name Reservation Rd, so it no longer counts.
- The search area is the union of the two.
- **Cost:** one more query per pull, or up to one per year while none is found. The #93 call-count bound was raised from 20 to 25 to match.

`PULL_FORMAT` → 4. #114 also sets 4 for #113; whichever merges second keeps one value with both comments, a trivial conflict.

## Tests
- The Tester's strict-xfail test now passes; marker removed: 2023's GPS crashes all set to county 57, and the no-GPS Crenshaw report is still found.
- pytest 301 passed, 2 skipped. Ruff clean.

## Same-basis check (Tester run 1 corridor `MARINA_27`, Reservation Road, 2021–2025, radius 250 / buffer 100)
data.ca.gov pulled 2026-10-21T00:36Z.

| | Tester run 1 (6f8d98257e56) | main (c1df6ff) | This PR |

| Kept | 174 pulled, 11 silent drops | 231 | 231 |
| Intersection / segment / unplaced | – | 30 / 3 / 24 | 30 / 3 / 24 |
| Tester's listed silent drops still missing | 10 | **0 of 10** | 0 of 10 |

**Honest note:** on this corridor, current main already recovers the drops. #54 (part 1) drops GPS rows more than the box margin from the line before they're used, so the Woodland points no longer reach the area step. The flaw itself is still there whenever a wrong-county GPS crash sits close to the line. The test reproduces exactly that case, and it fails on main and passes here.

title: Measure: auto-place when names differ only by a leading direction (COLORADO BL vs East Colorado Blvd)?
body:
## Question
Should a no-GPS report whose street names differ from the map **only by a leading direction** ("COLORADO BL" vs OSM "East Colorado Boulevard") be auto-placed? Today it rates `relaxed`, and the gate auto-places only `exact` (tiers proven ≥ 98% on held-out data; docs/03, PR #16 decision 2). Pasadena after #114: **101** crashes stay unplaced for this reason alone.

## This is a user decision, so first measure
The gate is a user decision. Before asking, measure the narrow rule on the hidden-truth test (`backend/scripts/validate_geocode.py`, same split and seed):
- New tier or flag `exact_but_direction`: same core and suffix, and the only difference is a leading direction on one side.
- Report per city (SF, LB, and Riverside if cached): n, accuracy, Wilson 95% lower bound, plus the extra coverage it would add.
- Also count how often the corridor has **both** an East and a West part with the same core (East/West Colorado). There, dropping the direction could place a crash on the wrong half. Check those cases explicitly.

## Then
PM brings the numbers to the user: auto-place this narrow case only if its Wilson lower bound is ≥ 98% (the existing bar) and the East/West ambiguity is handled (e.g. never auto-place when both halves exist in the network).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A validation table in the PR or issue comment; no change to the gate in code until the user decides.

title: #116: measure 'exact except a leading direction' (no gate change)
body:
## Measurement (#116): "exact except a leading direction"
`validate_geocode.py --direction-tier`: a subset of the `relaxed` tier where, for each street, the report matches the map either exactly or with **only** a leading direction different (same core and the same suffix, e.g. `COLORADO BL` vs `East Colorado Boulevard`). Each case is also flagged when the map has **both** directional halves of that street (East *and* West Colorado). Held-out **test** half, seed 20261018, OSM network, run 2026-10-21.

| City | n | Accuracy | Wilson 95% low | Coverage gain | Exact tier (reference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| San Francisco (truth: DataSF) | 1 | 100% | 20.7% | 0.02% of 4,028 | 98.8% (low 98.3%) |
| Long Beach (truth: officer GPS) | **1,574** | **82.5%** | **80.5%** | **24.9%** of 6,326 | 88.9% (low 87.7%) |
| ↳ both halves on the map | 863 | 80.8% | 78.0% | 13.6% | |
| ↳ one half only | 711 | 84.5% | 81.7% | 11.2% | |
| Riverside (truth: officer GPS) | 6 | 50.0% | 18.8% | 0.2% of 2,609 | 57.4% (low 55.3%) |

## Reading
- **The bar is not met anywhere measurable.** The rule for auto-placement is a Wilson 95% lower bound ≥ 98% on held-out data (PR #16 decision 2). Long Beach, the only city with a real sample, gives 80.5%.
- **Long Beach's truth is noisy,** so look at the gap, not the absolute. Its officer GPS is itself only ~73% consistent with the reported streets (knowledge/lessons), which pulls every tier down, the exact tier included. Against the same truth, the direction-only case is **6.4 points below exact**: 82.5% vs 88.9%.
- **East/West ambiguity is real.** Where both halves exist on the map, accuracy drops further (80.8% vs 84.5% with one half).
- **San Francisco and Riverside barely have this case** (1 and 6 crashes), so they tell us nothing either way.
- **Pasadena (101 unplaced after #114):** these are already on the review list with a `relaxed` suggestion. The review list's group action "At suggestion" places a whole street pair in one click, with the engineer's eye on it, without lowering the bar.

## Proposal for the user (PM to ask)
Keep the gate as is: auto-place `exact` only. Leave this case to the review list's suggestion. Re-measure if a city with clean truth and many directional names (e.g. Pasadena with a second truth source) becomes available.

No gate change in code; this PR only adds the measurement.

Refs #116

title: Bug: 'NOT STATED' contains STATE, so every no-cross-street report names a 'State Street' corridor (Santa Barbara)
body:
## What's wrong
The no-GPS search and `_names_street` compare squeezed text by substring. The placeholder `NOT STATED` squeezes to `NOTSTATED`, which contains the core `STATE` of any **State Street** corridor. So every report with a blank cross street reads as naming the corridor. The street-name search area (#115) then spreads to every county with such a report next to a common cross-street name.

## Evidence (statewide run 2, #73, main 1c0739e)
Santa Barbara, corridor "State Street": 6,928 rows read, 6,683 without GPS, from counties 33, 37, 42 and 43 (Riverside, San Diego, Santa Barbara, Santa Clara). **6,136** have SecondaryRoad `NOT STATED` and are listed as side-street exclusions, e.g. `32456 HAUN ROAD | NOT STATED` (Menifee), `44217 LA PAZ STREET | NOT STATED`. "State Street" is a common corridor name across California.

## Proof
`tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py::test_not_stated_does_not_name_a_state_street_corridor` (strict xfail): a genuine `STATE ST & W 144TH ST` report is found (control), and `32456 HAUN ROAD | NOT STATED` is pulled too.

## Expected
Placeholders (`NOT STATED`, `UNKNOWN`, `PRIVATE PROPERTY`, blanks; the app's `NO_CROSS` set) never count as naming a street, in SQL and in Python. Check other short cores that are substrings of placeholders too (e.g. a street named "Private", "Known").

Found by Tester, #73 run 2.

title: [Test] Run 1 → Run 2 reconciliation, crash by crash (#73)
body:
Follow-up to #124 (PM review): a **Run 1 → Run 2 reconciliation**, crash by crash. Tester session; no app code changed.

## Method
On the 476 like-for-like corridors (same frozen line and a pull in both runs), every crash in either run's stored pull is matched by Collision Id and put in **exactly one** bucket (`tests/statewide/reconcile.py`, rules applied in order). The workbook's new **Reconciliation** sheet shows the waterfall with two add-up checks as formulas (kept run 1 + changes = kept run 2; same for located), and **Reconciliation by city** shows each city's buckets.

## Waterfall (kept = kept for the corridor, not excluded; located = kept with GPS or auto-placed)
| Bucket | Cause | Crashes | Δ kept | Δ located |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPS crash no longer pulled | **#54** (pull drops GPS rows beyond the corridor margin) | 11,441 | −11,441 | −11,441 |
| No cross street, kept for review | #82 / #94 (user decision) | 6,736 | +6,736 | 0 |
| Newly found, located | #80 #83 #111 #113 | 1,215 | +1,215 | +1,215 |
| Newly found, review | #80 #83 #111 #113 | 3,722 | +3,722 | 0 |
| Newly found, excluded (side street) | #80 #83 #111 #113 | 117,786 | 0 | 0 |
| 'NOT STATED' read as State Street | **#121** (open) | 6,211 | +100 | 0 |
| Refiled duplicate removed | #81 fix (#87) | 81 | −18 | −17 |
| Private property, own rule | #82 | 1,092 | 0 | 0 |
| Other (run-1 exclusions not re-read, etc.) | — | 2,073 | −22 | −11 |
| Unchanged | — | 149,434 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | | | **+292** (50,033 → 50,325) | **−10,254** (47,932 → 37,678) |

**Evidence for the largest bucket:** run 1's own assignment, re-run on run 1's stored pull, put all 11,441 of those GPS crashes **outside** the corridor (5,567 freeway, 5,039 outside the buffer, 806 outside the study limits, 29 grade-separated). They never counted for any corridor; they only inflated run 1's "located %". The PM's guess was #74 (GPS road-name rule), but that bucket is 0: the drop comes from #54's margin filter at pull time. The 4 GPS crashes run 1 *had* placed on a corridor and run 2 doesn't pull are all refiled duplicates whose twin is kept (San Ramon, Tulare, Santa Clarita, Lynwood); they're in the refile bucket.

## Located % on consistent denominators
| | Located % |

title: [Data] PCF section → SWITRS category crosswalk from CHP's own records (#52 1A)
body:
For #52 decision 1A. Tester session; no app code changed. Engineering loads the table.

## What
`data/reference/pcf_categories.csv` holds CHP's own PCF section → SWITRS category assignment, rebuilt from TIMS SWITRS crash records, with counts and agreement per key. Source, method and stats are in `data/reference/pcf_categories.md`.

- **Source:** TIMS Crashes exports, Los Angeles County (165,741) and Fresno County (14,697), collision dates 2021–2024, downloaded 2026-10-20 with the user's OK for those two queries. Only counts are stored, not the raw records.
- **Key:** section + subsection, which matters: 21453(a) → 12 Signals & Signs, (c) → 09 Auto right of way, (d) → 11 Pedestrian violation. Blank sections are keyed by the primary-collision-factor code (B → 22, C → 18, E → 24).
- **Agreement:** 629 keys. **262 mapped** (≥99%; all are 100% in practice) cover **95.8%** of the crashes; 349 are "unknown" (CHP itself assigns 00); **18 split**, listed with their year-by-year counts.

title: fix(#121): short street names match whole words; placeholders never name a street
body:
Closes #121

## Cause
Street names were matched as squeezed substrings. Squeezed, `NOT STATED` reads `NOTSTATED`, which contains `STATE`. The same habit put `MAIN` inside `MAINE AV` and `ROMAINE ST`, and `STATE` inside `INTERSTATE 5`, `ESTATES DR` and `MIRA VISTA TERRACE` (live CCRS 2024).

## Fix (`backend/crashiq/crashes.py`)
- **Placeholders first:** `NOT STATED`, `UNKNOWN`, `PRIVATE PROPERTY`, blank (the `NO_CROSS` set) never name a street. This applies in Python (`_names_street`) and in SQL (`sp_ NOT IN (...)`).
- **Short names (squeezed ≤ 6 letters) match as whole words.** A spaced column `' ' || UPPER(col), separators → space || ' '` is compared with `LIKE '% STATE %'`. That's plain LIKE, so the same SQL runs on data.ca.gov (PostgreSQL) and on FakeCkan / the Tester mirror (SQLite). Multi-word short names also match run together (`DELAMO` for Del Amo; one real Lakewood crash needed it). Python uses the same rule.
- **Longer names stay squeezed.** Measured on live CCRS 2024: CHP splits words the map writes as one (`MC FADDEN AV` 23 rows, `MC KINLEY` 6, `MAC ARTHUR` 3), and whole-word matching of CRENSHAW, WILSHIRE, ATLANTIC and EL CAMINO REAL loses nothing.
- **Route spellings stay squeezed,** as before (SR-1 = SR 1 = SR1).
- **No change** to `names.py`, so no locator re-validation is needed.
- `PULL_FORMAT` 6.

## Same basis
Tester's frozen corridors (`results/96234d3d7806`), Tester CCRS mirror (copied 2026-10-19) and local OSM extract, 2021–2025, radius 250 / buffer 100. Before: main 75075d7. After: this branch. App DB: fresh scratch copies; the Tester's files were only read.

**Santa Barbara, State Street:**
- Before: 6,781 pulled, 6,683 without GPS.
- After: 108 pulled, 10 without GPS.
- Located 101 → 101, intersection crashes 37 → 37, review list 101 → 1, silent drops 0.
- A live data.ca.gov pull at this commit gives the same 108.

**All 136 Tester corridors with a short name:**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Rows pulled | 107,705 | 82,455 |
| No-GPS rows read | 135,490 | 83,420 |
| On the review list | 5,080 | 4,280 |
| Located | 11,003 | 10,976 |
| Intersection crashes | 6,007 | 5,980 |
| Segment crashes | 451 | 451 |

- **Every one of the 27 fewer located crashes was a wrong-city crash** placed on another town's corridor (32 checked, listed in the session). For example, Marysville's 5th Street was placing Union City's `5TH ST & D ST` crashes as exact; Ferndale's Main St was placing San Francisco's `MAIN ST & MARKET ST`.
- **Longest SQL:** 5,989 URL characters (the split limit is 6,000); no HTTP 414.

## Tests
- The Tester's `test_not_stated_does_not_name_a_state_street_corridor` now passes; the strict xfail is removed.
- `test_short_names_match_whole_words_and_never_a_placeholder` and `test_sql_matches_short_names_as_words` (the SQL spaced column is checked in SQLite against its Python twin).
- pytest 319 passed; ruff clean.
- `knowledge/pain-points.md` row 24 added; lesson note extended.

## Not fixed here (found while checking; for PM)
The street-name area search (#111) still adds counties wherever the same pair of names exists. Santa Maria (Main St & Ray St) now pulls 6 Pleasanton crashes to its review list; Shasta Lake pulls 3 from Selma. Before this fix, junk counts filled the query's 20 county slots and hid those counties. It's a separate rule question: should a name-found county count when the GPS area already exists? No change made.

title: Bug: street-name area search adds distant cities with the same street names (Santa Maria pulls Pleasanton)
body:
## Bug (from Engineering's note on #131; PM ruling: correctness, not a user choice)
The street-name area search (#111, PR #115) adds **any** county or city where the corridor street and a cross street both appear in no-GPS reports, even far away. **Santa Maria**, Main St & Ray: the pull now brings **6 Pleasanton crashes** (~250 miles away) onto Santa Maria's review list. They aren't counted, but a wrong-place crash on the review list is still wrong, and the user might place it.

## Why it's a bug, not a choice
A study corridor is in one place. A report from an agency whose area can't contain the corridor can't be on it. The name search exists to find the corridor's own area when there's little or no GPS (Union City, #35), not to add distant areas that share street names.

## Fix
- The street-name area is a candidate only if it's **geographically plausible**: its jurisdiction or city boundary (or, if unknown, the GPS extent of that agency's own crashes) intersects or borders the corridor's box plus margin.
- With GPS crashes in the box, their areas stay as now; name-found areas are added only if they pass the plausibility check (this keeps the Marina #111 protection).
- Keep a log line for each candidate area that was rejected and why.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Failing test first: Main & Ray-style names in two distant counties → only the corridor's own area is searched.
- [ ] #111's Marina test and #35's Union City test still pass.
- [ ] Same basis: Tester re-runs Santa Maria and a sample of common-name corridors (Main, 1st, Broadway) on the frozen list; no distant-city crashes on any review list.

title: [Tab 3] Pedestrians and bicyclists first: KSI share, danger comparison, markers, ranking, night split
body:
## Goal (user, 2026-10-20)
Pedestrian and bicycle crashes are what reviewers (ATP, HSIP, cities) look at first, because they are where people are killed or seriously hurt. Today tab 3 shows them as a small text list near the bottom (#105). Make vulnerable road users (VRU: pedestrians, bicyclists, and motorcyclists shown alongside) a first-class part of the Crash profile.

## Build
1. **Move up, with a headline:** a VRU section directly under the trust strip. Headline sentence from the tables, e.g. "12 pedestrian and 7 bicycle crashes; they are 25% of everyone killed or seriously injured." The key figure is the **VRU share of KSI** (and of all crashes), computed in the backend.
2. **"How dangerous is it?":** share of pedestrian crashes, bicycle crashes, and all other crashes that are KSI, side by side (aligned bars, direct labels). Code computes every share; show n for each.
3. **Always-visible markers:** pedestrian and bicycle crashes get a distinct marker (an outline ring or small icon) on the strip diagram and the 3D map, on top of the severity colour. They're visible without filtering, and the legend explains it. Must not break the severity encoding or the colour-blind check (#108).
4. **Location ranking column:** a pedestrian + bicycle count (and KSI) per location in the ranking (#103), plus a sort "by pedestrians and bicyclists".
5. **Pedestrian context:** pedestrian action (T15: in crosswalk, not in crosswalk, …) and **lighting split (daylight / dark with or without street lights / dusk-dawn)** for pedestrian crashes. Night-time pedestrian crashes are a classic pattern.

Out of scope: VRU over-representation tests (Findings, later); e-scooters unless CCRS has a reliable code (check and report).

## Rules (as for all tab 3 views)
Numbers only from API tables (add a T-table or columns as needed, with golden recounts from raw rows on the live fixtures). Plain-language titles, ⓘ citations, the severity ramp from tokens, exact numbers behind "Show table", no decoration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The VRU section sits right under the trust strip; the headline's numbers equal their table cells (test).
- [ ] The danger comparison equals the recount from raw rows on both live fixtures (golden test).
- [ ] Markers are visible on the strip and the map; the legend explains them; colour-blind check still passes.

title: fix(#132): a search area must have its own GPS crashes near the corridor
body:
Closes #132

## Rule
A county (or city) is searched for no-GPS reports only if **at least 3 of its own GPS crashes lie within 5 mi of the corridor box**. CCRS publishes no jurisdiction boundaries, so where an area's crashes are shows where the area is.
- **One grouped query per pull:** `_areas_near`, GPS crashes per area in the widened box.
- **Street-name areas (#111):** checked as the issue asks.
- **GPS-found areas: also checked (agreed with PM).** Santa Maria still pulled Pleasanton after the first version: one Pleasanton report with GPS inside Santa Maria's box made county 1 a "GPS area".
- **No GPS within 5 mi for any area:** nothing to judge by, so nothing is rejected, and the log says so (`area_unchecked`). This keeps the all-no-GPS case working (`test_area_found_from_street_names_when_no_gps_in_the_box`).
- **Logging:** each rejected area is logged once in `cleaning.area_rejected` (area, how it was found, the reason).
- `PULL_FORMAT` 11.

## Tests
- `test_street_name_area_far_from_the_corridor_is_not_searched`: Main & Ray-style names in a distant county; failed first.
- `test_one_stray_gps_crash_does_not_make_a_distant_county_a_search_area`: the Santa Maria case.
- The #111 Marina test (`test_wrong_county_gps_crash_does_not_redirect_the_no_gps_search`), the #35 Union City tests and the pull-efficiency query cap still pass.

title: Bug: no-GPS reports from neighbouring cities sharing a street pair fill the review list (Buena Park, Palm Springs)
body:
## Bug (from Engineering's same-basis run for #132 / PR #141)
No-GPS reports from **neighbouring cities in the same county** that share the street pair land on a corridor's review list. **Buena Park** and **Stanton** each hold ~220 Huntington Beach and Westminster crashes; **Palm Springs** holds La Quinta (169) and Palm Desert (55). They aren't counted, but the user would have to reject hundreds of wrong-place crashes by hand, and might place one by mistake.

## Why it's a bug
CCRS gives every report its **City Name / City Code**. A no-GPS report filed in a city the corridor never enters can't be on the corridor. The corridor can cross city lines (Union City Blvd → Ardenwood Blvd in Fremont, #74), so the rule must follow the line, not the study's "home" city.

## Fix
- The corridor's cities = the incorporated cities whose OSM boundary the drawn line (plus the buffer) intersects, plus "unincorporated county" where the line leaves city limits.
- A no-GPS report is a candidate only if its City Code is one of those. GPS crashes are unaffected (placed by their GPS).
- Reports dropped by this rule are counted in the pull log (`no_coords_other_city`) with the city names. They're not shown on the review list.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Failing test first: a corridor wholly inside city A; same street pair reports in neighbouring city B → B's no-GPS reports not pulled; A's still are.
- [ ] A corridor crossing A → B keeps both (Union City / Fremont live fixture).
- [ ] Same basis: Buena Park, Stanton and Palm Springs review lists drop the other-city crashes; Union City, Marina and Santa Barbara unchanged.

title: Bug: San Jose PD's CCRS GPS is written as degrees-minutes-seconds; those crashes land ~30 km away and are lost
body:
## What's wrong
San Jose PD (NCIC 4313) writes most of its CCRS GPS as degrees-minutes-seconds in a decimal field: `37.142677` means 37°14′26.77″ = **37.24077**. CrashIQ reads it as decimal degrees, so the point lands ~30 km south-east, in the hills. The crash falls outside any San Jose corridor box, and the no-GPS name search skips it because it has coordinates. It disappears without a count.

## Evidence (Tester, #88 portal survey, 2026-10-20)
- **DMS digit signature** (minutes and seconds digits both < 60 in latitude and longitude): **85–88%** of SJPD GPS points 2021–2024 (13% expected by chance); **2025: 56%** (possibly fixed partway through 2025).
- **Against San Jose's own open data** (Crash Locations layer, TCR `24-011-0126` = CCRS Report Number `2024-240110126`), 491 linked 2024 crashes: CCRS GPS as written sits a **median 34 km** from the city's point; read as DMS, **median 80 m** (63% within 250 ft; the city's points are intersection-level).
- Example: report 2024-240190382, BASKING RIDGE AV & CHELSEA CROSSING: CCRS (37.142677, -121.454889); city (37.24078, -121.76354); DMS → (37.24077, -121.76353).
- No other agency with ≥ 200 GPS points shows ≥ 95% DMS signature statewide, but a per-agency, per-year check is cheap.

## Proof
`tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py::test_gps_written_as_degrees_minutes_seconds_is_not_lost` (strict xfail): the Crenshaw fixture's GPS re-encoded as DMS. 0 of the corridor's 121 GPS crashes are found today; expected ≥ 90%.

## Fix
The rule is a **user decision** (the PM is taking it to the user). Recommendation: detect the DMS signature per agency and year. For each crash, convert if the converted point agrees with the report's streets (within the existing GPS-check distance of the named intersection or road); otherwise treat it as no GPS (name search). Provenance `gps_dms_corrected`, counted in the pull log.

Found by Tester, #88.

title: [Test] #88 part 1: placement accuracy by agency, San Jose GPS bug (#143), open-data sources
body:
Part of #88 (does not close it: the TIMS crash-by-crash match waits on the user's download decision). Tester session; no app code changed.

## 1. Placement accuracy by agency: the hidden-GPS test, statewide
`tests/statewide/accuracy_by_agency.py`. Covers every local police agency (not CHP, not multi-city sheriffs) with ≥200 street crashes with GPS in 2021–24: **158 agencies, 144 tested**, the rest listed with a reason. Up to 400 crashes each: the GPS is hidden, the app's own `locate.place` runs on the city's network from the OSM extract, and each result is scored against the hidden point. Correct = within 250 ft (PR #16). Workbook sheet **Accuracy by agency**.

- **Officer GPS is a weak check on offsets.** It usually sits at the intersection even when the report says the crash was hundreds of feet away. Concord: 92% right at the chosen intersection, 73% after applying the stated offset. So the sheet reports matcher accuracy at the intersection, point accuracy, and both on **self-consistent GPS only** (within 400 ft of an intersection of the streets the report names; agencies run 68–90%).
- **9 agencies' GPS can't serve as a check** (<50% self-consistent). San Jose is at 0.2% because of #143 below.
- **Exact tier**, self-consistent GPS: median 92.2% at the intersection (10th percentile 84.8%), 70% of crashes. This is below PR #16's 98%, which used SF's own geocodes as truth; officer GPS is a noisier answer key.
- **Relaxed tier** (held for review by the gate): median **91.5%**. Across 84 agencies with enough of both, relaxed minus exact has a **median of −0.05 points** (10th percentile −10, 90th +6). Examples:

| Agency | GPS self-consistent | Exact: share / accuracy | Relaxed: share / accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Long Beach | 77% | 46% / 96.5% | 37% / 97.7% |
| Torrance | 93% | 60% / 99.2% | 34% / 100% |
| Stockton | 77% | 16% / 96.6% | 66% / 86.1% |
| Fresno | 82% | 6% / 100% | 80% / 86.1% |

That's **evidence for the user's gate decision, not a decision.** In most agencies relaxed is as good as exact; in some (Stockton, Fresno) it is 10+ points lower, and there it carries most crashes. The next run stores raw counts so the tiers can be pooled with Wilson bounds.

## 2. New bug #143: San Jose PD's GPS is degrees-minutes-seconds
85–88% of SJPD GPS points 2021–24 carry the DMS signature (13% by chance; 2025: 56%). Against San Jose's own open data (n=491), as written the points sit a median **34 km** away; converted, **80 m**. Those crashes vanish from San Jose corridors. Strict-xfail test included; the fix rule is with the user.

## 3. Sources for unplaced crashes: portal survey
`tests/statewide/portal_survey.json`, workbook sheet **Sources for unplaced**. Measured only; nothing enters the app.

- **San Jose:** TCR `24-011-0126` = CCRS `2024-240110126`. **83%** of SJPD 2024 crashes link, 84% of those without GPS. Terms: 'as is' disclaimer only.
- **Pasadena:** `Accidno` = CCRS Report Number. **64%** link, all without GPS (Pasadena PD has GPS on 0.4% of reports). Licence 'custom' with no text.
- **SF** and **LA** as before; LAPD's dataset has stopped updating. **San Diego** has a report number but only block addresses (PDDL). **LA County 2017–21** is mostly CHP crashes that already have GPS.
- Copies of CHP/TIMS data, and cities with nothing found (Oakland, Sacramento, Long Beach, Fresno, …), are listed. Every source's terms need checking before any product use, as for TIMS (#126).

## 4. Knowledge
Pain points 26 (GPS in the wrong format) and 27 (San Jose's own data has 5,594 crashes for 2024 vs 2,453 in CCRS, 44%); a duplicate row 24 renumbered. Lessons on the GPS-as-truth limits and on spotting systematic GPS errors.

## Pending
TIMS geocodes for unplaced crashes, by reason group (no cross street / relaxed held by the gate / other). Needs the two approved TIMS files on disk: the browser can't save them, and both page-transfer routes were blocked by the session's safety check. The user's decision is pending.

title: fix(#142): a no-GPS report must be filed in a city the corridor enters
body:
Closes #142

## Rule
**A report without GPS counts only if CHP filed it in a city the corridor enters.** The corridor's cities come from OpenStreetMap:
- `network.corridor_cities`: the admin-level-8 boundaries containing points every 300 ft along the line and on both buffer edges.
- One Overpass `is_in` per point, behind a `make pt` marker; cached like every OSM answer (180 days).
- Where a point is in no city, the corridor is in **unincorporated county**: CCRS `Unincorporated` is allowed, plus the county's own name (San Francisco is a city-county, level 6).
- **Safety net for a missing OSM boundary:** any city with 2 or more of its GPS crashes along the corridor is also allowed.

**Matching names:**
- CHP and OSM spellings are normalized: accents dropped, `Saint` = `St`, `City of` stripped, and either name may be the start of the other when both are at least 6 letters. That covers Carmel / Carmel-by-the-Sea, Angels Camp / Angels, La Canada / La Cañada.
- Reports filed under campuses, park districts, airports and harbors (`Uc Santa Barbara`, `Pismo Dunes Pk Dist`, `Sf Intl Airport`…) are **never judged**, and neither are blank cities.
- If OSM can't answer, `corridor_cities` is None and **nothing is dropped**; the log shows `corridor_cities: null`.

**Logging and display:**
- Dropped reports are counted in `cleaning.no_coords_other_city`, with `cleaning.other_cities` by name.
- They are never on the review list.
- The "Where these crashes come from" panel shows the count, with the city names on hover.
- The PDF method text has one sentence on the rule.

**Plumbing:** `ensure()` looks the cities up before each pull, using `app.state.overpass`, so the same transport and cache as the corridor. GPS crashes are unaffected. `PULL_FORMAT` 12.

## Tests
- `test_no_gps_report_from_a_city_the_corridor_never_enters_is_dropped`: a Hawthorne corridor and Gardena reports for the same corner. They're dropped and counted; Hawthorne's own report stays; with no city list, nothing is dropped. Failed first.
- `test_a_corridor_crossing_into_the_next_city_keeps_both_cities` (golden, live Union City fixture):
  - Union City + Fremont gives assignments identical to no filter.
  - Union City alone drops Fremont's no-GPS reports.
- `test_city_names_chp_and_osm_spell_differently_still_match` and `test_corridor_cities_from_osm_boundaries`: parsing, the unincorporated case, and an OSM failure giving None.
- pytest 338 passed, with outside network blocked (no test reaches Overpass). vitest 64 passed; ruff and eslint clean.

## Tester harness, flagged for the Tester
`tests/statewide/osm_local.py` gains `is_in()` and answers the new query from the extract's `areas` rings. Without it, the harness's local OSM would refuse the query. The app would then retry and give up, so the filter would be silently off in the statewide runs. Spot checks:
- Buena Park → [Buena Park]; Stanton → [Stanton]; Union City → [Union City]; Santa Barbara → [Santa Barbara]
- Marina → [Marina] + unincorporated Monterey County
- Palm Springs' frozen Route 111 line → unincorporated Riverside County only. That stretch really is outside city limits; a point downtown returns Palm Springs.

## Same basis
- **Corridors:** Tester's frozen corridors (results/96234d3d7806), all 136 short-name corridors plus Union City and Marina.
- **Data:** Tester CCRS mirror and local OSM extract, 2021–2025, radius 250 / buffer 100.
- **Before:** main with #141. **After:** this branch. Every corridor got its city list; no errors.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Rows pulled | 51,541 | 26,934 |
| On the review list | 3,192 | 1,857 |
| Located | 10,976 | 10,922 |
| Intersection crashes | 5,838 | 5,786 |
| Segment crashes | 468 | 467 |
| Silent drops (Tester's independent check, v2) | 8 | 8 |

| Corridor | Pulled | Located | Review list |
|---|---|---|---|
| Buena Park | 4,127 → 393 | 240 → 235 | 424 → 8 |
| Stanton | 1,858 → 494 | 75 → 75 | 348 → 61 |
| Palm Springs | 770 → 40 | 22 → 22 | 241 → 0 |
| Union City | 347 → 347 | 159 → 159 | 1 → 1 |
| Marina | 231 → 231 | 58 → 58 | 24 → 24 |

**The 54 fewer located crashes were all filed in a city the corridor doesn't enter** and had been placed by name match:

title: Bug: reports filed under an unincorporated place's own name (Kensington) are dropped as 'another city' by the #142 filter
body:
## What's wrong
CCRS files crashes in some unincorporated places under the place's own name; CCRS even marks some of them incorporated (Kensington, Broadmoor, Bear Valley Springs, …). When a corridor runs through such a place, OSM reports it as unincorporated county land. The #142 filter then allows only the OSM cities plus UNINCORPORATED / the county name, and drops those reports as filed in another city.

## Evidence (statewide run 3, #73, main 3a9a57e)
Kensington, Arlington Avenue: corridor cities from OSM = Berkeley + unincorporated Contra Costa County. The pull drops **11 'Kensington' reports** (`other_cities: {'Kensington': 11, …}`), e.g. 2677748 ARLINGTON AV & WESTMINSTER, 2681500 ARLINGTON AV & SUNSET AVE, all no-GPS, on the corridor, at its own intersections. Run 2 (before #142) pulled them.

## Proof
`tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py::test_unincorporated_place_name_is_not_another_city` (strict xfail): a no-GPS corridor report with City Name 'KENSINGTON', corridor cities {Hawthorne, outside: LA County} → dropped (`other_cities: {'KENSINGTON': 1}`).

## Expected
A report city with **no OSM city boundary** (admin level 8) is not 'another city' when part of the corridor is unincorporated: treat it like UNINCORPORATED. Only names that are real OSM cities the corridor doesn't enter should be dropped.

## Also seen (edge case, for the PM)
Calistoga, Silverado Trail: the test corridor lies outside Calistoga's limits, and 1 Calistoga PD report at a corridor intersection is dropped. That's arguably correct; it's listed here so the rule is decided deliberately.

Found by Tester, #73 run 3.

title: [Test] Statewide run 3: same corridors at main 3a9a57e, reconciliation run 2 → 3, new bug #147 (#73)
body:
Run 3 of the statewide test (#73). Tester session; no app code changed.

## Same basis
Frozen corridors, the same CCRS mirror (2026-10-19 20:54), the same OSM extract (2026-10-18) and the same settings. Only the code differs: **run 3 = main 3a9a57e**, which adds #121 (#131), #129/#134, #130/#137, #132 (#141) and #142 (#145) since run 2. #143 (San Jose DMS) is not fixed yet, so San Jose is labelled "affected by #143".

**City filter checked live:** every city logs the cities its corridor enters, and the filter was on for all 479 corridors (none off). A corridor with the filter off would be marked untested, not passed.

## Headline (like for like)
- On the **43,263 crashes kept in both runs**, located is **88.3% in run 2 and 88.3% in run 3**: placement is unchanged.
- **As measured:** 88.25% located in run 3, from 43,280 crashes kept for the corridor.
- On-corridor crashes with a location: **82.0%**, up from 65.0% in run 2.

| Rule | Run 2: pass / warn / fail | Run 3: pass / warn / fail |
|---|---|---|
| Run-1 rule | 266 / 85 / 123 | **333 / 75 / 65** |
| Run-2 rule | 263 / 80 / 134 | **328 / 73 / 75** |

Unplaced corridor crashes: 1,731 with no cross street (was 6,843) and 2,706 relaxed matches held by the gate (was 3,878).

## Reconciliation, run 2 → run 3
Crash by crash on 479 corridors; the waterfall adds up exactly. Kept 51,361 → 43,280; located 38,658 → 38,195.

- **#142 other-city reports dropped:** 188,435 crashes; −7,986 kept, −472 located. **All 472 located ones were run-2 "exact" placements of reports filed in another city on the same street pair.** Examples: a Pasadena report "WASHINGTON BL & MENTONE AV" was placed on Culver City's Washington Blvd; Hesperia's "Main St & Locust Av" came from Placerville. These were wrong placements that #142 correctly removed. It also shows the exact tier's main failure mode: **the same corner name in another city.**
- **#121 junk removed:** 6,234 crashes (−100 kept). **#132 rejected areas:** 38 crashes. Other: 24.

## New bug #147
The #142 filter drops reports filed under an **unincorporated place's own name**. Kensington lost 11 genuine Arlington Av reports, which run 2 had. Strict-xfail test included.

## Silent drops (v2 = 52) are mostly my check's own false positives
- **Re-filed duplicates whose twin was kept**, so #81 is working: Fountain Valley, Paramount, Orinda, Aliso Viejo.
- **Different streets that substring matching wrongly counted:** OLD MIDDLEFIELD WY ≠ W Middlefield Rd (Mountain View, 22 drops, the same in run 2), LINCOLNOCEAN AV, ARROWN HWY, …
- **Real:** Kensington (#147), and Calistoga, where the corridor lies outside the city (edge case, noted on #147).
- **Proposal for run 4:** silent_drops_v3 = exact street match after normalising, and duplicate-aware. That is a new column; v2 stays as recorded.

## Corridor check (new)
**78 of 479 frozen corridors lie mostly outside their own city**: 55 entirely, 23 partly. Examples: Sacramento (unincorporated Natomas), Escondido, Santa Rosa, Clovis, Manteca. Cause: the picker took the longest road with *any* node inside the city. The app's results on those corridors are still valid tests, but they aren't tests of that city's agency. They're flagged on the Cities sheet ("Corridor inside its own city %"). **Re-picking them would break the same basis, so it's the PM's or user's call** (e.g. a corridor-list v2 with a one-time re-baseline).

title: [Test] Silent-drop check v4: v3 + the report's own offset, independent of the app (#73)
body:
Silent-drop check **v4**, per the PM's method call after #149. It is a new column, and v3 is kept beside it. Tester session; no app code changed.

## What v4 does
v4 takes v3's drops and removes reports whose **own stated offset** places them past the end of the study stretch.
- **Independent of the app.** The cross-street point is the OSM node nearest the frozen corridor line, from the local extract, not the app's intersections. The offset comes from CCRS SecondaryDistance, SecondaryDirection and SecondaryUnitOfMeasure, converted here (F → ft, M → ×5280). The station math is in `tests/statewide/checks.py`; nothing comes from the app's offset code.
- **A tolerance band, not a hard cut.** A report counts as expected unless it lands **more than 250 ft** past either end of the stretch the study cross streets span (or the study radius, if that is larger).
- **Conservative.** These never clear a report:
  - an offset over a mile (typos such as 52,800 ft or 317 "miles");
  - a missing direction;
  - a cross street that can't be found in OSM.
- **Auditable.** Each result stores `v4_cleared` (crash id, cross street, direction, stated offset, computed distance past the end). The workbook lists them all on a new **Silent drops v4 cleared** sheet.
- New columns: `silent_drops_v4` and `result_v4` per city, and `silent_drops_v4` plus `pass/warn/fail_v4` in the run history. HARNESS goes to 5.

## Checked on run 3's stored data
| | v3 | v4 |
|---|---|---|
| Kensington (#147) | 9 | 9 |
| Calistoga | 1 | **0**: 2754373 cleared (PICKETT, N, 2,059 ft stated, **957 ft past the stretch end** computed along the corridor) |
| **Total** | 10 | **9** |

v4 matches the recorded real count for run 3 (9). The 957 ft is the along-corridor part of the 2,059 ft offset (the corridor runs NW–SE). My #147 comment's "about 2,060 ft beyond" was the full offset, not the along-corridor distance.

## Tests
`tests/tester/test_statewide_harness.py` gains 4 tests:
- units and unusable offsets;
- station movement along, against and across the corridor;
- the tolerance band;
- the nearest cross-street node.

Suite: 349 passed, 2 skipped, 2 xfailed. Ruff is clean.

Refs #73.

title: fix(#147): unincorporated places filed under their own name count where the corridor is unincorporated
body:
Closes #147

## Fix
Where part of the corridor is unincorporated, a report filed under a name that is **no incorporated city** counts like `Unincorporated`. That covers Kensington, Broadmoor and Bear Valley Springs, which CHP files under their own names and CCRS even marks incorporated. A report filed under a real city the corridor never enters is still dropped.

**"Real city"** comes from the new `data/reference/ca_cities.csv` (method in `ca_cities.md`):
- CCRS City Names marked incorporated in 2021–2024 that OpenStreetMap also has as a city: 479.
- Plus Compton, a real city missing only from the Tester's OSM extract: 480 in all (California has 482).
- The list errs toward keeping reports: a city missing from it is kept, never wrongly dropped.

title: Bug: a corridor name with 'of' (Avenue of Flags) never matches CHP's spelling, so its no-GPS reports aren't pulled
body:
Found by the statewide test, run 4, corridor list v2 (#73): **Buellton, Avenue of Flags**.

Silent-drop check v4 found crash **2752702** (Buellton PD, 2021-03-18, AVENUE OF FLAGS & 1ST ST, 34 ft S, no GPS). It names the corridor and a study cross street (1st Street), but the app never pulled it. The pull log shows `no_coords_read: 0`.

**Cause:** `names.street_key('Avenue of Flags')` gives core `AVENUE FLAGS`, because the word OF is dropped as a filler word. The SQL prefilter then searches for `AVENUEFLAGS` inside the squeezed road text, and CHP's `AVENUE OF FLAGS` squeezes to `AVENUEOFFLAGS`, so it never matches. Other California streets with the same shape include Avenue of the Stars (LA, core `AVENUE STARS`) and Avenue of the Americas. Any corridor whose name has OF, THE or AT inside it is affected.

**Failing test:** `test_corridor_name_with_of_matches_chp_spelling` in tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py (strict xfail). It runs the Crenshaw fixture with no GPS, corridor 'Avenue of Flags', and crash 9200001 PrimaryRoad 'AVENUE OF FLAGS'. The crash isn't pulled; written as 'AVENUE FLAGS', it is.

title: Bug: a numbered corridor with a direction (East 4th Street) misses CHP's 'E 4TH ST' and '4TH ST', so its no-GPS reports aren't pulled
body:
Found by the statewide test, run 4, corridor list v2 (#73): **Dorris, East 4th Street**.

Silent-drop check v4 found crash **2508053** (Dorris PD 4700, 2023-02-28, MAIN ST & 4TH ST, no GPS). It names the corridor and a study cross street (Main St; the study intersection is 'South Main Street / US 97 / West 4th Street'), but the app read 0 rows.

**Cause (`crashes._search_core`):** a core that is too short without its direction keeps the direction, so 'East 4th Street' searches for `EAST4TH`. CHP writes the direction abbreviated (`E 4TH ST` → `E4TH`) or leaves it out (`4TH ST`), and neither contains `EAST4TH`. **Even 'E 4TH ST' is missed** (fixture check). Numbered streets with a direction are common: W 1st St, E 4th St, N 2nd St, and so on.

The no-direction form ('4TH ST') at an intersection where East and West 4th meet is the harder case. Whether to pull it is a rule question. The abbreviated 'E 4TH ST' is plainly the same street.

**Failing test:** `test_numbered_corridor_with_direction_matches_abbreviated_direction` (strict xfail). It runs the Crenshaw fixture with no GPS, corridor 'East 4th Street', and crash 9200001 PrimaryRoad 'E 4TH ST'. It isn't pulled.

title: fix(#154, #155): Avenue of Flags keeps OF; East 4th Street searches the bare number
body:
Closes #154
Closes #155

## #154: Avenue of Flags
`names.street_key` dropped OF and THE everywhere as filler, so 'Avenue of Flags' became `AVENUE FLAGS`, and the prefilter never found CHP's `AVENUE OF FLAGS`.
- **Key:** `AVENUE/AVE/AV OF (THE)` now keeps OF and leaves THE out, because CHP writes it both ways (Buellton: AVENUE OF FLAGS and AVENUE OF THE FLAGS). So 'Avenue of Flags', 'AVE OF FLAGS' and 'AVENUE OF THE FLAGS' give one key, `AVENUE OF FLAGS`; 'Avenue of the Stars' gives `AVENUE OF STARS`.

- **Elsewhere OF is still noise:** '100 FT NORTH OF THE BRIDGE' gives `FT NORTH BRIDGE`, as before.
- **Search:** the SQL prefilter searches the name after "of" (`FLAGS`, a whole word since #121); Python decides.

## #155: East 4th Street
A short core used to keep its direction (`EAST4TH`), because before #121 a bare `4TH` matched inside 14TH and 24TH. Since #121, short names match as whole words.
- **Search:** the prefilter now searches the bare core (`4TH`), which covers CHP's `E 4TH ST` and `4TH ST`.
- **Python decides, unchanged:** `same_core` already accepts `E 4TH ST` and the no-direction `4TH ST` for East 4th Street (the existing relaxed tier), and rejects `W 4TH ST`.

title: fix(#143): San Jose PD GPS written as degrees-minutes-seconds is converted and checked against the report's streets
body:
Closes #143

User decision 2026-10-21 (docs/03, option A).

## What
1. **One query, two boxes.** The GPS query now also reads the corridor box's **degrees-minutes-seconds image** (`dms_encode` of its corners), joined with OR, so no extra calls. San Jose's 37.142677 is the DMS image of 37.24077.
2. **Which agencies.** A point from that image is considered only if its **agency-year clearly carries the DMS signature**: ≥ 75% of a sample of up to 1,000 of its GPS points have minutes and seconds < 60 in both coordinates (`_dms_share`, one small query per agency-year, cached per pull).
3. **Converted point kept** (`dms_decode`) only if it lands within the **GPS-check distance (400 ft + the report's offset)** of the study intersection the report names, or of the corridor line when it names the corridor. Provenance `gps_dms_corrected`, the as-written pair kept in `gps_as_written`.
4. **Otherwise no GPS:** the row joins the no-GPS path (name rules, city filter, review list).
5. **Pull log:** `gps_dms_corrected` and `gps_dms_unconfirmed` (distinct crashes), plus `gps_dms_agencies`, e.g. `4313 (2024)`.
6. **Downstream:**
   - Assignment, the GPS check and review overlays treat `gps_dms_corrected` as GPS.
   - T1 `located_gps` includes these crashes, so T1 still adds up, and a new row `located_gps_dms` breaks them out.
   - The trust strip shows "(n converted)" next to GPS; the provenance label is in the drill-down.
7. `PULL_FORMAT` 15.

## Why 75%, not a simple majority
Measured on the Tester's CCRS mirror, 2021–25, all agencies with ≥ 20 GPS points (about 300–340 a year):
- **Ordinary agencies:** most show the DMS digits on **30–40%** of their points, not the 13% pure chance would give, because GPS values cluster. A few small agencies reach 50–67%.
- **San Jose PD (4313):** **85–88%** in 2021–24 and **55%** in 2025.
- A 50% cut would flag about six innocent agencies a year. **75% flags San Jose PD 2021–24 and nothing else.**
- SJPD 2025 (55%) is *not* "clear", so it isn't converted, consistent with "only where the signature is clear" (docs/03). The street check would also guard a wrong conversion.

## Check against San Jose's own data (not committed)
- **Source:** San Jose's open crash layer (GIS 553, TCR `24-004-0754` = CCRS Report Number `2024-240040754`), read live 2026-10-21. Its terms aren't confirmed for product use (#88), so no rows are stored.
- **Linked:** **494** of SJPD's 592 CCRS 2024 GPS points.
- **As written:** a median **34.2 km** from the city's point.
- **After conversion** (425 with DMS digits): median **35 m**, 75th percentile 283 m, 90th percentile 1.0 km; 64% within 400 ft, 89% within 1 km. The city's points are often intersection-level.
- **Not converted:** 69 of the 494 carry no DMS digits (e.g. 37.2198) and fit no other clean format (decimal minutes is off by about 1 km). They stay unconverted and are lost, as today. That's listed in pain-points row 26.

## Tests
- The Tester's `test_gps_written_as_degrees_minutes_seconds_is_not_lost` now passes; its strict xfail marker is removed.
- `test_dms_encode_decode_round_trip`, using San Jose's own example report.
- `test_gps_written_as_dms_is_converted_and_kept_near_its_streets`: the whole Crenshaw fixture DMS-encoded. Every GPS crash is either converted back to within 2e-5° of its true point or sent to the no-GPS path; none are lost.
- `test_dms_needs_the_agency_signature`: an ordinary agency is never converted.
- **Results:** pytest 358 passed; the pull-efficiency query cap is unchanged; vitest 64; ruff and eslint clean.

## Same basis
- **Corridor:** the Tester's only San Jose corridor, Monterey Road (results/781a88aa53f3).
- **Data:** Tester CCRS mirror and local OSM, 2021–2025.

| Monterey Road | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Located | 21 | 22 |
| Intersection crashes | 3 | 4 |
| Pulled | 353 | 354 |
| Tester's silent drops (v2) | 0 | 0 |

- **Pull log:** `gps_dms_corrected` 1, `gps_dms_unconfirmed` 1, agencies 4313 (2022), 4313 (2024).
- **Why the effect is small:** SJPD puts GPS on only about 24% of its reports (592 of 2,453 in 2024); most of its crashes come in through the no-GPS name search already. The effect is larger on corridors where SJPD's GPS reports cluster.

title: [Test] Fatal crashes first: count unplaced fatal crashes, measure FARS matching (measure only)
body:
## Goal (user, 2026-10-21)
Fatal crashes get extra weight: **every fatal crash should be placed**, even when the CCRS report has no GPS and no usable cross street. Measure first, then propose.

## Measure (Tester; measure only, nothing into the app)
1. **How many fatal crashes are unplaced:** in the test corridors (frozen list v1, latest run) and statewide (CCRS 2021–2025), count fatal (K) crashes with no location, by reason (no cross street, gate-held relaxed match, other) and by agency.
2. **FARS match:** NHTSA's Fatality Analysis Reporting System (public domain, US DOT) has every US fatal crash with its own LATITUDE/LONGITUD, date, time, county, city and route.
   - Download the California accident files for the years available (2021–2023 final; 2024 if published). **This needs the user's OK in your session**, one batched request with file names, source (nhtsa.gov / static.nhtsa.gov) and sizes.
   - Link CCRS fatal crashes to FARS by county + date + time (± tolerance) + number killed, with roads as a tie-break. Report the link rate and the ambiguous cases.
   - For unplaced CCRS fatal crashes: how many FARS gives a usable point? A usable point fits the report's road names (within the GPS-check distance of the named road or intersection) and isn't a degenerate point (county or city centroid, many crashes on one point).
3. **Residue:** list the fatal crashes neither CCRS nor FARS can place (expected to be few), with city, date and roads, as candidates for a human-confirmed public-source lookup (news etc.). No web lookups in this step.

## Output
A **Fatal crashes** sheet in the statewide workbook plus a summary on the tracker: unplaced fatal count, FARS link rate, FARS-placeable count, residue list. Same basis as the statewide runs.

title: [Test] Fatal crashes first: unplaced fatal crashes and the FARS link, measure only (#166)
body:
Closes #166. Fatal crashes first, **measure only**: nothing goes into the app. Tester session; same basis as run 5 (backend tree e03af4bc6080, CCRS mirror 2026-10-19, OSM extract 2026-10-18).

## FARS data
The user OK'd the four NHTSA national files in the Tester session on 2026-10-21: FARS 2021–2024 National CSV from static.nhtsa.gov, 137 MB in total. FARS 2025 isn't published.
- Only the California rows of `accident.csv` are kept, in `data/cache/fars/` (gitignored). The national files were deleted.
- FARS is public domain (US DOT).
- Correction: the 2021 and 2022 files begin with a byte-order mark, so my first filter missed them, and I had already deleted the originals. I re-downloaded those two approved files, applied the fix, and deleted them again.

## 1. Unplaced fatal crashes
| | Crashes |
|---|---|
| CCRS fatal crashes 2021–2025 | 19,459 |
| **without GPS** | **4,381 (22.5%)**: LAPD 1,200, San Diego PD 286, Victorville 246, Sacramento PD 197, SFPD 152 … (Fatal crashes sheet) |
| without GPS *and* without a cross street | 90 |
| Test corridors (run 5): fatal crashes kept | 303: 276 placed, **27 unplaced** (16 relaxed matches held by the gate, 11 no locator match) |

"Statewide unplaced" here means "CCRS has no GPS". Many of those have a cross street that the app's name matching may place; only the test corridors show what the app actually does.

## 2. FARS link
Link rule: county (CCRS county → FIPS 2n−1) + date + time within 60 min (FARS unknown time matches any) + number killed. Roads break a tie. A FARS case is year + ST_CASE, because case numbers restart every year. Keying on ST_CASE alone first mixed years up; that's now fixed and covered by a test.
- **94.7%** of 16,278 CCRS fatal crashes in 2021–24 link to exactly one FARS crash. 767 aren't found and 89 are ambiguous. 61 FARS crashes match two CCRS records (refilings).
- **A usable FARS point** is a real point (not an unknown code, not shared by 3+ crashes) with a road the report names within 400 ft plus the report's offset (local OSM).
  - Of the no-GPS fatal crashes: **3,379** get one. 58 fall off the report's roads, 13 are unusable, 204 aren't found, 20 are ambiguous, and 707 are from 2025.
  - On the test corridors: **22 of the 27 unplaced** get one.

## 3. Residue (no web lookups)
**295** fatal crashes in 2021–24, plus **707 from 2025** waiting for FARS 2025. They're listed on the **Fatal residue** sheet (city, date, roads, why no point), for a later human-confirmed lookup.

## Output
- Workbook: **Fatal crashes** and **Fatal residue** sheets.
- Tracker: a **Fatal crashes first** section, live.
- Pain points 28 (one fatal crash in five has no GPS) and 29 (CCRS and FARS don't line up one to one).

Tests: 5 new FARS-link tests, covering the county mapping, the link, the road tie-break and ambiguity, and the year+case key. Suite: 366 passed.

For the user, per the issue: the proposal (FARS as a checked source with `fars` provenance, fatal crashes first on the review list, human-confirmed lookup for the residue) comes after they've seen these numbers.

title: Bug: a route number in a location's name (CA 41, US 395) makes the validator reject the screen's own finding
body:
Found by the statewide Findings run (#176) on run 5 (backend e03af4bc6080, frozen list v1).

**19 code-written findings in 14 cities were rejected**, every one with the same reason: the route number in the location's OSM name. The validator reads every number in the finding's text and requires a cited table cell for it. The location label comes from the T12 row, but its digits aren't a cited *number*, so it rejects:
- Atascadero: "Rear End crashes are over-represented at Mercedes Avenue / CA 41: 9 of 26 crashes here (34.6%) vs 19.1% across the corridor intersections." → `number 41 in the text is not backed by a cited table cell`
- Bishop (US 395 / US 6), El Segundo and San Francisco (CA 1), Gilroy (SR 152), Fontana (Route 66), Hercules (SR 4), Santee, Ukiah, La Quinta, Rosemead, Santa Clarita, Dinuba, La Cañada Flintridge.

**Cost:** these findings are written by code from T12 and every figure in them is cited, but they never reach the user. They're signals at state-highway intersections, which are often the most important locations on a corridor. The non-negotiable rule (no uncited numbers) isn't at stake: the digits are part of a road name, not a figure.

**Failing test:** `test_route_number_in_location_name_does_not_reject_the_finding` in tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py (strict xfail). It builds a T12 row and the screen's own finding text for "Mercedes Avenue / CA 41" and expects `findings.validate` to return no reasons. Today it returns `['number 41 in the text is not backed by a cited table cell']`.

title: [Test] Verify Findings: golden T12 from raw rows, statewide Findings run, bug #179 (#176)
body:
Closes #176. Tester session; measure only, no app code changed.

## 1. Golden T12 (closes the gap from #78)
`tests/tester/test_golden_t12.py` recounts the over-representation screen from the **raw recorded CCRS rows** on both live fixtures (Crenshaw, Union City), with code that shares nothing with `signals.py`:
- target crash sets read from CHP's own fields;
- p\*, the HSM variance, the method-of-moments beta prior;
- P(true share > p\*) from the beta density integrated by Simpson's rule (no continued fraction). That integral is checked against Monte Carlo: 0.5844 vs 0.584.

**Result: T12 matches exactly.** That covers which rows are flagged, every count and share, the probability, the strength and the method. There are 8 flagged rows across the two fixtures; both the beta-prior method (4) and the binomial fallback (4) are exercised.

## 2. Statewide Findings run (same basis)
`tests/statewide/findings_run.py` runs Findings on all 479 frozen-v1 corridors with **run 5's own backend code** (cbb69bc, from a temporary checkout) over run 5's stored pulls. Current main has #169 in the backend, so running it there would change the basis.

| | |
|---|---|
| Corridors screened / locations screened | 479 / 7,725 |
| T12 rows flagged | 847, of which **367 use the binomial fallback** (labelled a confidence, not a probability) |
| Corridors with at least one finding | 233 |
| Findings shown | 741 |
| **Findings the validator rejected** | **19 (expected 0)**: bug #179 |

## 3. Bug #179
Every rejection is a route number in the location's name. Example: "…at Mercedes Avenue / CA 41: 9 of 26 crashes…" is rejected for "number 41". This affects 14 cities, including Bishop (US 395), El Segundo and San Francisco (CA 1), and Fontana (Route 66). These findings are code-written, fully cited, and never reach the user. There's a strict-xfail test in `tests/tester/test_ccrs_agency_bugs.py`.

title: feat(#174): fatal crashes placed at their linked FARS point when it fits the report's streets
body:
Closes #174. User decision 2026-10-21 (docs/03, "Fatal crashes: FARS as a source").

## What
- **Store:**
  - Migration 13: `fars_accident` (California rows; key year + ST_CASE) and `fars_source` (file, rows and load date per year).
  - Loader: `backend/scripts/load_fars.py`. `--download <years>` reads the official NHTSA national CSV zip and keeps `accident.csv` rows with STATE 6; `--csv` loads files already on disk.
  - The byte-order mark at the start of the 2021–22 files is handled.
  - Yearly refresh and the link rule are documented in `data/reference/fars.md`. Nothing from FARS is committed except a small test fixture.
- **Link** (`crashiq/fars.py`), the Tester's verified rule from #166 / PR #172:
  - same county (CCRS county code → FIPS 2n−1) and date, same number killed
  - time within 60 min (FARS unknown time matches any)
  - roads break a tie (route numbers or the same street, via the app's own name matching); still more than one = ambiguous, never used
  - a case is year + ST_CASE
- **Usable point:** inside California (not FARS's 77/88/99 unknown codes) and not shared by 3+ FARS crashes.
- **Placement** (`placement.place_fatal_from_fars`, before the street-name locator): for each fatal crash (killed > 0, not excluded) with no GPS, or with GPS that fails the street check:
  - the linked point is used if it passes **the same street check as DMS-converted GPS** (`crashes.point_fits_streets`): within 400 ft + the report's offset of the study intersection the report names, or of the corridor when it names only the corridor
  - provenance `fars` and `fars_case`; replaced GPS is kept in `gps_replaced`
  - otherwise nothing changes (the review list)
  - non-fatal crashes are never touched
- **Counts:**
  - pull log `cleaning.fars`: tried / placed / linked_point_off_streets / no_point / ambiguous / unlinked / no_fars_year
  - T1 `located_fars` (T1 still adds up)
  - trust strip segment "FARS"; provenance label in the drill-down
  - Excel sheet "FARS-placed fatal crashes" with the FARS case; FARS in the credits
- `PULL_FORMAT` 17.

## Tests
- `tests/test_fars.py` (9):
  - county → FIPS; BOM and other states skipped on load
  - the link: time window, deaths, unknown time, road tie-break, ambiguous → not used
  - the ST_CASE year reset; no FARS year
  - unknown and shared points not used
  - placement: a point on the report's streets is placed; a point 2 km off is not; a non-fatal crash is never placed
- **Golden:** `test_fars_link_agrees_with_the_testers_rule`. On every fatal crash (2021–24) in both live fixtures' raw rows, using the real FARS rows of those days (`tests/fixtures/live/fars_fatal_days.csv`, 72 rows, public domain), the app's link equals the Tester's `fatal.link` crash by crash: 25 linked, 1 unlinked. None of the fixtures' study-stretch fatal crashes are unplaced, so the placement itself is covered by the unit tests above and the same-basis run.
- pytest 378 passed, vitest 66; ruff and eslint clean.

## Same basis
- **Corridors:** the 19 run-5 corridors (`results/e03af4bc6080`) holding the Tester's 27 unplaced fatal crashes.
- **Data:** Tester CCRS mirror and local OSM; FARS 2021–24 California rows (the Tester's copies).
- **Comparison:** this branch with an empty store vs with FARS loaded.

| Fatal crashes (19 corridors) | Without FARS | With FARS |
|---|---|---|
| Unplaced (review list) | 27 | **15** |
| Placed by FARS | 0 | **12** |
| GPS / exact | 11 / 3 | 11 / 3 |

All other crash counts are unchanged, except located +12 (intersection +8, segment +4) and review −12.

**Why 12, not the Tester's expected 22.** The Tester's "fits" check asked whether a road the report names runs within 400 ft of the FARS point. The app requires the point to be near **the study intersection the report names, or this corridor**.
- **Far away:** most of the 13 linked points that fail lie **1 to 7 miles from the corridor**, so the crash happened elsewhere on the same roads:
  - Chico, four RT 32 crashes: 4.7–7.4 mi
  - El Cajon: 1.5 mi
  - Paramount and Winters: about 1 mi
  - San Bernardino, two RT 18 crashes: 0.7–0.9 mi
- **Near miss:** Tulare (544 ft from its named corner, no offset given).
- **Not linked:** 6 are 2025 (no FARS yet), 2 unlinked, 1 unusable point.

The 13 stay on the review list, as decided. **For the PM/user:** FARS is evidence that most of them aren't on the study stretch at all. #175 could show "FARS puts this crash X mi away" on the review list.

- **Source required:** placing a fatal crash with no `source` (link or note, ≤ 500 chars) returns 422 "A fatal crash needs a source…".
  - Migration 14 adds `crash_decision.source`; it's in the decisions signature, undo keeps it, and the overlay carries it as `user_source`.

title: [Tab 3] #106 Collision diagram per study intersection (N10)
body:
Closes #106. User decision N10 (docs/03, 2026-10-21), as specified in docs/06 N10 revision 2.

## What
- **`backend/crashiq/diagram.py` computes every placement:**
  - DemandIQ's layout: arms, control symbol, street names on the arms, north arrow.
  - Each crash goes on the at-fault party's approach (CCRS `DirectionOfTravel`; party 1 when none is marked), in that approach's quadrant (SB upper left, NB lower right, EB lower left, WB upper right), in fixed slots so nothing overlaps.
- **Symbols** (HSM Ch. 5 / ITE, NCDOT, Peel, Seattle):
  - rear-end, angle, left-turn broadside, head-on, sideswipe same/opposite
  - fixed object, pedestrian (dotted, P), bicycle/e-bike/e-scooter (B), backing, parked, out of control, other
- **Marks:**
  - severity at the impact point: **filled = fatal, hollow ring in the KABCO colour = injury, crossbar = property damage only**
  - arrowheads hollow by day, **filled in the dark**
- **NCDOT stacking:** identical crashes (same type, approach, side of the other party, surface + light code) share one symbol with a row of crash numbers, marked with the most severe among them.
- **Numbers and list:** crashes are numbered in date order. New table **T21@<intersection>** (crash, date/time, approach, type, severity, HSM code) is the key.
- **Crashes that can't be drawn** are listed with why: no party data (CCRS Parties 2025 isn't published), no direction, or no room.
- **One renderer source:** the output is a list of **drawing steps**. The app draws them as SVG (`IntersectionDiagram.jsx`, a new component; the Findings screen's existing `CollisionDiagram` is untouched) and the PDF draws the same steps with ReportLab, so both always match.
- **Drill-down** (study intersections only): the diagram, the not-drawn note, a legend built from the backend's own symbols, and the crash list behind "Crash list (numbers on the diagram)". It's drawn like a printed sheet (white paper) in both themes.
- **PDF:** a "Collision diagrams" section, one per study intersection with crashes, each followed by its numbered list and the code legend.

## Tests

  - light code and night
  - stacking (numbers "1, 3"); date numbering; the worst mark shows; fatal filled; everything inside the frame
  - no-party-data crashes listed, not drawn
- **Golden** (both live fixtures, every intersection): T21 numbers every counted crash exactly once, 1..n in date order; drawn + not drawn = all; severities equal the raw-row recount.
- **API/PDF:** the drill-down returns the diagram and T21 for an intersection, no diagram for a segment; the PDF has "Collision diagrams".

title: Bug: a missing year of CCRS Parties/IWP silently undercounts road users, trucks, movements; disclose it
body:
## Bug (disclosure)
When a year's CCRS **Parties** (or InjuredWitnessPassengers) table is missing, the pull records it (`parties_missing_years`, `iwp_missing_years`), but **no screen, table caveat or export says so**. Every Parties-based number then silently undercounts that year: road users (T10, T19, T20: pedestrians, bicyclists, e-bikes, e-scooters, motorcyclists), heavy trucks, movement of the at-fault party (T16), broadside split (T17), and the collision diagram (#106 lists them as not drawn, the only place it shows).

Seen: until 2026-10-22 data.ca.gov had no Parties_2025, and the frozen test mirror (2026-10-19) still lacks it. CHP published Parties_2025 and Parties_2026 on 2026-10-22, so live pulls get it now, but the gap will recur for every new year.

## Fix
- A profile caveat whenever `parties_missing_years` or `iwp_missing_years` is non-empty: "CHP hasn't published party (or injury) details for 2025 yet: road users, trucks, movements and the collision diagram leave out those years' N crashes."
- The same note on each affected table (ⓘ) and in Excel/PDF (methods and the T-table notes).
- The diagram's not-drawn reason says "no party data for this year in the pull", not "not published", so it stays correct after CHP publishes.
- Severity: if IWP is missing for a year, those crashes' injury level is U and the caveat says so.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests with a fixture missing Parties for one year: the caveat appears on the profile, the affected tables and the exports; with no year missing, no caveat.
- [ ] Cached pulls made before a year was published get refreshed (the existing 30-day expiry covers recent windows; confirm, or bump PULL_FORMAT).
