body:
Closes #178. Run 6 of the statewide test (#73). Tester session; no app code changed.

## Basis
Same frozen corridors (v1 and v2), the same **frozen CCRS mirror (2026-10-19)**, OSM extract and settings. Code: **main 6c42616** (backend tree 8261077cc6bd), with #174 FARS (#182) and the #179 fix (#184).
- #185 (fatal-first review) merged after run 6 started, so it isn't in this run.
- FARS 2021–2024 (California rows, from the files the user OK'd for #166) is loaded into the Tester databases with the app's own `load_fars.py`.
- **Completeness guard: passed.** 524/524 frozen-v1 cities and 78/78 v2 corridors.

## Fatal crashes on the test corridors, before vs after FARS
Each run is read with its own code over its own stored pulls (`tests/statewide/fatal_outcomes.py`). Workbook sheet: **Fatal before-after**.

| Outcome | Run 5 | Run 6 |
|---|---|---|
| placed, GPS | 133 | 128 |
| placed, exact name match | 58 | 10 |
| **placed, FARS point** | — | **62** |
| **placed, total** | **191** | **200** |
| excluded `fars_off_corridor` (FARS puts it elsewhere on the report's roads) | — | 36 |
| excluded, other rules (freeway, limits, buffer, street) | 85 | 62 |
| **unplaced** | **27** | **5** |

**Crash by crash:**
- 44 moved from an exact name match to their FARS point. 41 of them stay at the same study location.
- 13 unplaced crashes are now placed by FARS.
- 9 unplaced crashes are now `fars_off_corridor`.
- 22 crashes that were already excluded (outside limits or buffer) are relabelled `fars_off_corridor`.
- **5 that run 5 counted on the corridor are now excluded as `fars_off_corridor`.** This follows the agreed rule (a FARS point is treated like GPS: within the 250 ft radius or the 100 ft buffer, or out). For the user: in **Dana Point** (PCH & Golden Lantern) and **Fontana** (Foothill & Sierra), the FARS point is only **~60 ft** from where the name match put the crash at a study intersection the report names, but 230–285 ft off the line, so the crash now leaves the corridor. In **Palm Desert**, FARS puts the crash 7.4 mi from the name-match spot, which suggests the name match was wrong there. A possible rule for the user: count a FARS point that lies within the GPS-check distance (400 ft + offset) of the study intersection the report names.

## Other run-6 numbers
- v4 check: 338 / 77 / 61 (run 5: 337 / 77 / 62). Missed reports v4: 0. On-corridor located: 82.08%.
- **Reconciliation 5 → 6** adds up. The only change is `fars_174`: 22 crashes, +22 located. On the 43,297 crashes kept in both runs, located goes 88.2% → 88.3%.
- **Findings** on run 6's code: 237 corridors, 755 findings, **0 rejected** (run 5: 19). **#179 re-verified**: all 14 affected cities now show the findings they had blocked. Comment posted on #179.

## Corrections
- **There were no silent worker stops**, in run 5 or run 6. Every worker finished. My checks were wrong: `ps | grep "python …"` doesn't match macOS's `…/Python`, and a `pgrep` waiter matched its own command. #164's "one worker stopped silently" was wrong too.
- **My reruns overlapped the still-running workers** on the same Tester databases for 13 cities. Checked:
  - all 13 have the same outcome line in both runs;
  - each city's two pulls are **identical crash by crash** (crash id, location source, exclusion);
  - every result file points at a study with its stored pull. Measures only read those studies, so the extra study rows feed nothing.
- **Fix:** `run_cities.py` now logs a heartbeat every 60 s (city, elapsed, peak memory) and an **EXIT line** (finished / signal / exception) per worker. A run is waited on by its EXIT lines, not by process names.

## Mirror refresh (proposal; the PM or user decides)
CHP refreshed CCRS today. **Proposal:**
- A new mirror date is a **basis change**. It's recorded in the run history (`mirror_date` already exists) with a one-line reason.
- Run N on the old mirror and run N+1 on the new one, **with the same code**, so the reconciliation isolates the data change from code changes. Then normal runs continue on the new mirror.
- Like-for-like headlines compare only runs on the same mirror. The tracker labels the mirror on each run.

New **pain point 30:** Parties_2025 is published as a file but not loaded into data.ca.gov's query service (`datastore_active = False`, checked 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-22). So 2025 crashes have no party details through the API.

title: Bug?: fatal crashes ~60 ft from a study intersection excluded as fars_off_corridor (Dana Point, Fontana); Palm Desert link
body:
## Suspected bug (from run 6, PR #190)
5 fatal crashes that run 5 placed on their corridor are excluded in run 6 as `fars_off_corridor`:
- **Dana Point, Fontana:** the FARS point is ~60 ft from the study intersection the report names, but > 230 ft off the drawn line. `assign()` tests the intersection radius (250 ft) **before** the line offset, so a point 60 ft from a study intersection should be an intersection crash. That it's excluded suggests the FARS point is compared against a different node, the named intersection isn't the study node, or the radius is measured differently for FARS points.
- **Palm Desert:** FARS puts the crash 7.4 mi away. Is the CCRS↔FARS link wrong (two fatal crashes the same day and county?), or is the road-name consistency check too loose?
- Also check the other 2 of the 5 (Tester's run-6 data, PR #190).

Investigate each with evidence (CCRS record, FARS ST_CASE, distances to the study node, the line, and the named intersection). Fix if it's a bug, with a failing test first. If it's a legitimate geometry case (e.g. the drawn line is off the road), report it; a rule change would go to the user.

title: fix(#191): FARS only for fatal crashes with no usable location
body:
Closes #191.

## Finding: two code bugs, all five crashes explained
The PM's reading of the distances is right: Dana Point's FARS point is 285 ft from Golden Lantern and Fontana's 252 ft from Foothill, both just outside the 250 ft radius. But **none of the five should have reached the FARS step at all.** In run 5 each already had a usable location:

| Crash | Run 5 | Run 6 (before this fix) | Why it changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dana Point 2486955 (RT 1 PCH & Golden Lantern) | exact, at Golden Lantern | FARS 285 ft off → `fars_off_corridor` | the FARS step ran **before** the street-name locator |
| Fontana 2558597 (Foothill & Sierra) | exact, at Foothill | FARS 252 ft from the corner, 231 ft off the line → excluded | same |
| Twentynine Palms 2573645 (Larrea & RT 62) | exact | FARS 407 ft off → excluded | same |
| Palm Desert 4567942 (Country Club & El Dorado, 549 ft off) | exact, on its segment | FARS **7.4 mi** east → excluded | same |
| Atwater 2700880 (Juniper & Augusta) | **GPS**, 34 ft from W Avenue 2 / E Juniper | FARS 611 ft off → excluded | GPS was judged by a **stricter** check than the assignment's (the report must name the corridor; it names Juniper, the cross street) |

The decision (docs/03) is FARS for a fatal crash with **no usable location**. An exact locator placement, or GPS the assignment accepts, is a usable location.

**Palm Desert's link is correct.** Riverside County has exactly one FARS fatal crash that day: 2023-63406 at 03:39 (CCRS 03:38), 1 killed, on Country Club Dr. FARS geocodes it near Country Club Dr & Monroe St, 7.4 mi east (FARS city code 2646). CHP's report says Palm Desert, Country Club Dr & El Dorado Dr. The sources disagree on the place. The road check passed because **one** of the report's roads, Country Club Dr (miles long), runs past the FARS point. With this fix the crash keeps its exact placement and FARS isn't consulted.

## Fix (\`placement.py\`)
1. The FARS step now runs **after** the street-name locator, on fatal crashes still unplaced (including no-cross-street ones, which skip the locator).
2. A fatal crash's GPS is replaced only when **the assignment's own check** rejects or flags it (\`not_on_corridor_street\`, or \`gps_check\` far from the stated intersection). The stricter test is no longer used for this.

\`PULL_FORMAT\` 18.

## Tests (failing first)
- \`test_fatal_crash_the_locator_places_exactly_keeps_that_place\`: CRENSHAW BL & MARINE AV with a FARS point on Crenshaw 2.5 mi away. It used to become \`fars\`; now it stays \`exact\`.
- \`test_fatal_crash_whose_gps_the_assignment_accepts_keeps_its_gps\`: the Atwater shape, GPS at an intersection whose cross street the report names. It used to become \`fars\`; now it stays \`gps\`.
- pytest 403 passed, run with outside network blocked; ruff clean.

## Same basis
- **Corridors:** the five run-6 corridors (\`results/8261077cc6bd\`) plus the 19 FARS corridors from #182.
- **Data:** Tester CCRS mirror and local OSM, FARS 2021–24 loaded.
- **Comparison:** main vs this branch.
- **The five:**
  - Dana Point, Fontana, Twentynine Palms → **exact, at their intersections**
  - Palm Desert → **exact, on its segment**
  - Atwater → **GPS, at its intersection**
- **Three other GPS fatal crashes** (Compton ×2, Huntington Beach) keep their own GPS. It places them outside the corridor, where FARS also had them, so they're now excluded under the normal rules.
- \`fars_off_corridor\`: 17 → 9. FARS on the stretch: 13 = 13. Unplaced: 5 = 5. Nothing else changed (51 fatal crashes).

## For the user (rule question, not built)
Should a FARS point have to fit **both** roads the report names (corridor + cross street), not just one? Palm Desert shows one long road (Country Club Dr) can match a point miles away. After this fix it only matters for crashes the locator can't place. It's the PM's call to take to the user.

title: Parties/IWP download fallback when a year isn't in the data.ca.gov datastore (Parties_2025)
body:
## Goal (user decision, docs/03 2026-10-22; proposal on #188)
When a CCRS Parties (or IWP) year isn't queryable in the data.ca.gov datastore (`datastore_active = False`) but its file is downloadable, the server downloads it once and serves lookups from a local cache.

## Build (per Engineering's proposal on #188)
- Detect datastore-inactive resources at pull time.
- Background download (ranged GET; ~211 MB, ~40 s), parse into SQLite with only the needed columns (~51 MB), keyed by resource id + last_modified. Refresh weekly at most.
- Lookups by Collision Id from the cache; pull log `parties_source: file_cache (date)`. The #189 caveat clears for that year once the cache has it.
- Network failures: the pull still completes with the caveat; never block a study.
- Don't commit the cache; document where it lives and its size.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests with a fake inactive resource plus a small file: lookups from the cache, the caveat cleared, refresh rules honoured, failure keeps the caveat.
- [ ] Live check: Parties 2025 for the Crenshaw and Union City studies; the collision diagram draws 2025 crashes.
- [ ] Tester run 7 measures 2025 road users before/after.

title: feat(#196): Parties/IWP download fallback when a year isn't in the data.ca.gov datastore
body:
Closes #196

## What
When a CCRS Parties or InjuredWitnessPassengers year is published on data.ca.gov as a CSV but not loaded into the datastore (`datastore_active = False`; Parties_2025 today), the server reads it from CHP's file. This follows the user decision of 2026-10-22 (docs/03) and the proposal on #188.

- **Detection:** at pull time from `package_show`, CSV resources only (`ccrs_files.inactive_resources`). Crash tables are always read from the datastore.
- **Download:** in the background, one per resource. The file is parsed into `data/cache/ccrs_files/<resource id>.sqlite` (gitignored; `CRASHIQ_FILES_DIR` moves it). The copy keeps only the 9 columns the app reads, indexed by Collision Id, plus a `meta` table with the resource id, URL, `last_modified`, download date and row count. It is written to a temp file and then renamed.
- **Refresh:** at most weekly, and only when `last_modified` changed (CHP re-dates every file daily). The old copy keeps answering until the new one is complete.
- **Never blocks a pull:**
  - While the file isn't ready, the year stays missing. The #189 caveat adds "CHP has published the file; CrashIQ is downloading it…".
  - Once the copy exists, the waiting pull counts as stale (`files_pending`), so the next view re-pulls and the caveat clears.
  - A failed download is logged in `file_errors`, keeps the caveat, and is retried after 60 minutes.
- **Pull log:** `parties_source` / `iwp_source` per year (`datastore` or `file_cache (date)`).
- **Live data.ca.gov only.** FakeCkan, recorded fixtures and the Tester's mirror never start a download. A harness opts in by setting `app.state.ccrs_files` to a `FileCache`. **Tester, for run 7:** set it in the harness, or the before/after shows no change.
- **No PULL_FORMAT bump:** pulls missing 2025 already refresh daily (#189), and other pulls are unaffected.
- **Docs:** `data/reference/ccrs_files.md` (location, size, refresh rules); pain point 30 → Built.

## Tests (no network)
`tests/test_ccrs_files.py`:
- A fake inactive Parties_2025 plus a small CSV built from the fixture (BOM, every column, stray header spaces): the profile tables are identical to the datastore path, the caveat is cleared, and only the needed columns are kept.
- A failed download keeps the caveat, says "downloading", and leaves no half-written copy. No retry within the hour; a retry after it.
- A waiting pull goes stale when the file arrives.
- Refresh rules: under a week with a newer date, not refreshed; a week old with the same file, kept; a week old with a newer date, downloaded again, with the old copy answering meanwhile.
- Only CSV resources count; FakeCkan never downloads; live data.ca.gov gets one cache in the settings folder.

Full suite: 409 passed, 2 skipped, with the network blocked. ruff clean.

title: fix(#195): the FARS point must fit both roads the report names
body:
Closes #195

## What
Per the user's decision of 2026-10-22 (docs/03), a fatal crash's FARS point is used only when it fits **every** road the report names (placeholders like "NOT STATED" are ignored):
- **At the named intersection:** the point is within the GPS-check distance (400 ft, plus the reported offset) of the study intersection the report names. Both roads meet there. Or:
- **On the named roads:** the OSM roads at the point carry every named road, matched by name, ref, alt_name or old_ref (`fars.on_named_roads`). Before this change, one road was enough.

Otherwise the crash stays on the review list with the FARS hint (case, point, miles from the corridor). The hint's wording changes from "not on any road the report names", which is now wrong when the point sits on one of them, to "the map doesn't show both roads the report names there. Check it before placing." PULL_FORMAT 19.

## Tests
`tests/test_fars.py`:
- A point on only one of two named roads → review list with the hint.
- A point on both → placed.
- A point at the named study intersection → placed.
- A placeholder cross street → one road is enough.

The full suite passes with the network blocked (406 passed); ruff and eslint are clean.

## Same-basis check: the Tester's 79 corridors with fatal crashes
- **Basis:** tree 5e9ec19d57dc, with the Tester's CCRS mirror, the local OSM extract and FARS 2021–24 loaded.
- **Code compared:** main 63e2541 vs this branch.
- **Reading:** each DB read with its own code.

| Fatal crashes (154) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| placed (exact / GPS / FARS) | 53 / 37 / 16 | 53 / 37 / 15 |
| FARS point off the corridor (`fars_off_corridor`) | 9 | 9 |
| excluded by the normal rules (limits, buffer, freeway) | 36 | 36 |
| review list (unmatched) | 3 | 4 |

**One crash changed: Tulare 2801885** (RT 63 / PROSPERITY, 2021-03-25).
- **The point:** FARS case 2021-61564 lies 120 ft from study intersection `osm-2090793238` on Mooney Blvd. OSM leaves that cross street unnamed ("Unnamed road"), so the point can't be confirmed on Prosperity.
- **What happens now:** the crash goes to the review list, first in the fatal section, with the hint (0.0 mi from the corridor).
- **Is the rule wrong here?** The placement before this PR was probably right. The rule worked as written; the OSM name gap is what blocks it.

**Question for the user (via PM), not built:** when the road at the point has no name in OSM, should it count as "can't tell" (accept the point if the other named road matches) rather than as a mismatch? Today it's a mismatch, which is the conservative reading of the decision. It affects 1 of 154 fatal crashes on this basis.

title: [Test] Citywide geocoding coverage: per city, crashes filed vs on the map vs review vs unplaceable, with accuracy
body:
## Goal (user, 2026-10-22)
The client-facing test: **for every California city, of all crashes its police filed in CCRS, how many can CrashIQ put on the map, and how accurately?** For example: "Fremont PD filed 2,889 street crashes 2021–25; police GPS on 1.6%; CrashIQ places N% from street names; M% go to review; K% can't be placed (no cross street); accuracy X% where it can be checked."
Today we have this per 1-mile test road (Cities) and per agency GPS rate (Agencies), but not **citywide**.

## Method (Tester; measure only)
For every local agency (and CHP areas separately), all **non-freeway** CCRS crashes 2021–2025 from the mirror (+ the Parties cache where relevant):
1. **Police GPS usable:** GPS present and consistent with the report's streets (after the #143 DMS correction).
2. **CrashIQ placed:** run the app's own locator on the rest, against the city's local OSM network (not a corridor): exact tier (auto-placed under the 98% gate), FARS for fatal.
3. **Review list:** relaxed / held by the gate, by reason.
4. **Can't be placed:** no cross street / no usable clue.
5. **Accuracy:** hidden-GPS test where the agency's GPS is usable as truth (#144 method); city open data where linkable (SF, San Jose, Pasadena); otherwise "can't verify", stated plainly.
- The headline per city: **on the map (police GPS + CrashIQ) %**, review %, can't-place %, and accuracy (with its basis).
- Use the app's own code at a stated commit; same-basis rules; completeness guard.

## Output
- A **Citywide coverage** sheet (one row per city/agency) plus a California map coloured by "on the map %", in the workbook and on the tracker.
- Sorted lists: worst 25 cities, and the cities where the police record little GPS but CrashIQ still places most (the value CrashIQ adds).
- Bugs found → `bug` issues with failing tests.

title: [Test] Measure 'unique pair' relaxed matches (one possible intersection): accuracy vs exact, coverage gain (Lancaster Avenue J)
body:
## Question (evidence for the user's gate decision; measure only)
Lancaster's citywide sample: 9,403 crashes, 38.7% on the map, **41.9% to review**, mostly "relaxed" matches. Reports say `AVENUE J`; OSM has `East Avenue J` / `West Avenue J` (2,587 crashes). The relaxed tier is held by the 98% gate (docs/03, #116).
Many of these may be **unambiguous anyway**: if the report's street pair (in any directional variant) meets at **exactly one** place on the city network, e.g. `AVENUE J & 20TH ST W` can only be `West Avenue J & 20th Street West`, placing it isn't a guess. That's different from the risky case #116 measured (both halves exist *and* the pair could match either).

## Measure
1. A new tier, measured only: **relaxed match whose street pair has exactly one candidate intersection** on the city network ("unique pair").
2. Accuracy by the #144 method (hidden police GPS, self-consistent truth only) for every agency where GPS is usable; report n, accuracy, Wilson 95% lower bound, by agency and pooled. Also SF / San Jose / Pasadena open data where linkable.
3. Coverage gain: how many review-list crashes statewide (and in Lancaster) it would place.
4. Compare with the exact tier on the same truth.

## Then
PM brings the numbers to the user. Auto-placement only if the user decides (the bar is the existing 98% lower bound, or what the user sets).

title: Placement tier unique_pair: street pair meets at exactly one intersection (behind the 98% gate)
body:
## Goal (user decision in principle, docs/03 2026-10-22)
A new placement tier, `unique_pair`: the report's two streets (allowing differences only in a leading/trailing direction or suffix) meet at **exactly one** intersection on the city network → place there. Example: `AVENUE J & 20TH ST W` → West Avenue J & 20th Street West (Lancaster).

## Build
- In `locate`: after exact, before relaxed. Enumerate candidate street variants for both names, intersect, and accept only if exactly one node (or one cluster within NEAR_M) results. Two or more → stays relaxed (review), as now.
- `Gate()`: `unique_pair` auto-places only when enabled in config. Default **off** until Tester's #201 measurement shows it meets the 98% Wilson lower bound and the user confirms; when off, the crash goes to review **with the unique-pair suggestion** (one click).
- Provenance `unique_pair`; T1 and export counts.
- Locator re-validation (SF/LB/Riverside): add the tier's row to `validate_geocode.py` output.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests: Avenue J case (unique → placed when enabled); East/West ambiguity (two candidates → review); disabled gate → review with suggestion.
- [ ] `validate_geocode` reports the unique_pair tier: n, accuracy, Wilson low.
- [ ] No change to exact placements (same-basis check on Tester's corridors).

title: feat(#203): unique_pair placement tier (gate off until #201 and the user)
body:
Closes #203

## What
A new placement tier, **`unique_pair`**. The report's two streets meet at exactly one intersection on the city network, allowing only what the report leaves out: a leading or trailing direction, or a suffix. A part the report writes must match, or be absent from the map. The tier runs after exact and before relaxed. This builds the user's decision in principle (docs/03, 2026-10-22).

- **Why Lancaster went to review:** `street_key` drops a trailing direction, so `20TH ST W` and `20th Street East` share one key. `AVENUE J & 20TH ST W` therefore matched both West Ave J & 20th St W and East Ave J & 20th St E, and went to review as ambiguous.
  - The network now keeps each way's trailing direction per node (`Network.trail_at`).
  - `names.directions()` reads the report's directions.
  - Result: a single match, West Avenue J & 20th Street West.
- **Gate:** auto-placing tiers now come from `backend/crashiq/config/placement.json`, which is `["exact"]`.
  - `unique_pair` is added only after the Tester's #201 measurement clears the 98% Wilson bar and the user confirms. Until then the crash goes to review with the unique-pair suggestion (one click).
- **Counts:**
  - Provenance `unique_pair`.
  - New T1 row `located_unique_pair` ("Placed where the report's two streets meet at only one place"), also in the export. It is left out of `located_other`.
  - New quality-strip entry: "one possible corner".
- **`validate_geocode.py`:**
  - The tier is in the per-tier table.
  - A summary line with n, accuracy, Wilson 95% low and coverage gain, also written to `summary.json` as `unique_pair`.
  - A new arm, "A+ exact + unique_pair".
- **Exact placements can't change.** `unique_pair` runs only when exact found no single intersection. When exact was ambiguous and `unique_pair` can't resolve it, the same "exact: streets meet in more than one place" review comes back as before.

## Tests
`tests/test_unique_pair.py`, on a small Lancaster-style grid:
- Avenue J & 20th St W → `unique_pair` at West Ave J, in either order.
- East/West left open on both streets → review (two candidates), unchanged.
- A direction the report writes must exist.
- Exact placements are unchanged.
- `directions()` returns the directions as written.
- Gate off by default → suggestion with tier `unique_pair`; gate on → placed with provenance `unique_pair`.

`test_locate`, Long Beach `ATLANTIC AV & ATLANTIC PL`: same node as before, but the tier is now `unique_pair` instead of relaxed (only the left-out "North" differs).

The full suite passes with the network blocked (419 passed). Vitest: 69 passed. ruff and eslint are clean.

## Same-basis check
I ran 8 of the Tester's corridors (tree 5e9ec19d57dc, Albany through Bell Gardens), not all 79: the PM asked not to compete with the Tester's CPU this morning.
- **Basis:** the Tester's CCRS mirror and the local OSM extract, at `nice 19`, comparing main and this branch.
- **Exact placements:** 180 before, 180 after, 0 changed.
- **Changed:** 2 of 2,005 crashes. Atwater `BUHACH RD / JUNIPER AV` and Banning `W RAMSEY ST / 16TH ST` were relaxed suggestions and are now `unique_pair` suggestions, at the identical point.
- **Not changed:** no crash placed or unplaced differently.
- **Full run:** I can do all 79 corridors when the Tester is idle.

## Seen, not changed
An exact match can contradict a trailing direction the report writes. Example: `E AVENUE J & 20TH ST W` lands exactly at East Ave J & 20th St (East), because the exact key ignores the trailing W. I left it alone, since exact placements are out of scope here. Flagging it for the Tester's #201 measurement.

title: Bug: exact tier ignores a stated trailing direction (20TH ST W placed at 20th St East)
body:
## Bug (found by Engineering in #203 / PR #204)
The **exact** tier, which auto-places under the 98% gate, can contradict a trailing direction the report states. `E AVENUE J & 20TH ST W` is placed at **East Ave J & 20th Street East**, because exact matching ignores the `W`. That's a wrong automatic placement, not a review item.

## Fix (obvious mistake)
- When the report states a trailing (or leading) direction on a street, the exact tier must not match a network street with the **opposite** direction. Missing direction on either side is still allowed, as now.
- If that leaves no exact candidate, fall through to unique_pair / relaxed (review), as usual.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Failing test first: the Lancaster example goes to West 20th, or to review, never to East.
- [ ] Count statewide how many existing exact placements change (Tester), and re-run `validate_geocode` (SF/LB): exact accuracy should hold or rise.

title: fix(#205): no tier matches the opposite of a stated trailing direction
body:
Closes #205

## What
The street key drops a trailing direction. Because of that, `E AVENUE J & 20TH ST W` was auto-placed by the **exact** tier at East Avenue J & 20th Street **East**.

The fix: every tier now keeps only intersections where any trailing direction the report writes is on a way through the node, or that way has none.
- **Left out on either side:** still allowed, as before.
- **Applies to every tier, not only exact:** the relaxed tier made the same mistake, as a suggestion on the review list.
- **Near tier:** it picks a node on one street that the other street only passes close to. There the other street's direction can't be checked, so it doesn't block the match.
- **When nothing is left:** the crash falls through to the later tiers or review, as usual. The Lancaster example now goes to review: East Ave J never meets 20th St W.
- **Leading directions:** these are part of the exact key already ("EAST AVENUE J" never matches "WEST AVENUE J"), so only trailing directions needed the fix.

## Tests (failing test first)
- `test_exact_never_lands_on_the_opposite_stated_direction`:
  - `E AVENUE J & 20TH ST W` → review, never node 4 (East).
  - No direction stated → node 4, as before.
  - `20TH ST E` → exact.
  - It fails on main.
- `test_near_tier_still_works_with_a_stated_direction` guards the near-tier exception (it fails with a strict check).
- Full suite: 421 passed with the network blocked; ruff clean.

## Re-validation (validate_geocode, test half, main vs this branch, `nice 19`)

| | exact n | exact accuracy | Wilson low | changed crashes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF main | 3,632 | 98.8% | 98.3% | |
| SF this PR | 3,635 | 98.8% | 98.3% | 4, all correct before and after |
| LB main | 2,825 | 88.9% | 87.7% | |
| LB this PR | 2,825 | 88.9% | 87.7% | 2: one fixed, one wrong suggestion now review |

SF:
- 3 crashes moved from unique_pair to exact: CONSERVATORY DR WEST / JFK DR, and HAIGHT ST / BUENA VISTA AV W and E.
  - On main, exact matched both the East and West corners and returned ambiguous; unique_pair then found the right one.

LB:

Exact accuracy holds in both cities; the only change in correctness is the fixed LB crash.

**Left for the Tester (acceptance item):** count statewide how many existing exact placements change.

**For #201 (seen in passing):** the unique_pair tier is large in Long Beach: 2,437 crashes, 38.5% of the test half, accuracy 83.5%, Wilson low 82.0%. LB's own exact tier scores 88.9% on the same truth. In SF it is 4–7 crashes, all correct. This is still behind the gate.

title: [Test] Statewide coverage: every CCRS crash 2021-25 in two bins, by district, county, city and road type (#199, draft)
body:
Refs #199 (draft; the user asked for the numbers as soon as they exist). Tester session; measure only, no app code changed.

## Headline: every CCRS crash 2021–2025, all roads
**2,057,508 crashes**, every non-deleted CCRS crash 2021–25 and each in exactly one bin (completeness checked: the merged count equals the mirror's count).

| | Crashes | **Bin 1: on the map** | **Bin 2: difficult** |
|---|---|---|---|
| All crashes | 2,057,508 | **85.3%** | 14.7% |
| Fatal | 19,459 | **94.5%** | 5.5% |
| Fatal + serious injury (KSI) | 95,637 | **85.5%** | 14.5% |

**Where bin 1 comes from:** police GPS checked against the report's roads 71.1%; CrashIQ from street names (exact, under the gate) 14.2%; FARS 0.1%; converted degrees-minutes-seconds GPS 1,989 crashes.
**Bin 2:** review 7.6% (a likely match the gate holds, mostly *relaxed* = 110,884) and can't place 7.1% (no cross street, or the named streets don't meet on the map). **The reason is recorded per crash.**

**On the map % is a share of what CCRS holds, not of every crash that happened.** CCRS is incomplete (pain points 26–30: LAPD 67–77%, San Jose 44%, collapsing agencies). There's a Source completeness column per agency.

## Roll-ups (workbook sheet "Statewide coverage", first; tracker top section with a county map)
| Caltrans district | Crashes | On the map | Fatal on the map | KSI on the map |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 19,824 | 94.4% | 95.6% | 93.6% |
| 2 | 19,447 | 88.4% | 94.0% | 89.8% |
| 3 | 171,757 | 92.1% | 97.1% | 93.0% |
| 4 | 345,954 | 89.6% | 95.9% | 90.6% |
| 5 | 86,845 | 88.6% | 96.6% | 88.5% |
| 6 (incl. all of Kern) | 155,057 | 86.6% | 96.9% | 92.1% |
| 7 | 574,680 | 80.1% | 91.3% | 74.0% |
| 8 | 277,695 | 85.2% | 92.8% | 87.1% |
| 9 (excl. eastern Kern) | 3,216 | 93.9% | 95.0% | 88.0% |

| 11 | 128,737 | 83.3% | 94.5% | 84.4% |
| 12 | 149,328 | 79.8% | 92.7% | 85.7% |

| Road type | Crashes | On the map | Police GPS | CrashIQ placed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Freeway | 652,058 | 94.7% | 94.6% | 0.1% |
| County road (outside cities) | 305,500 | 96.6% | 95.2% | 1.4% |
| State highway off the freeway | 150,877 | 87.1% | 81.5% | 5.5% |
| **City street** | 949,073 | **75.0%** | 45.5% | **29.4%** |

City streets are where it's hard, and where CrashIQ's street-name placement does most of the work. Examples:
- **San Francisco:** 91.2% (police GPS 32.0% + CrashIQ 59.2%).
- **Sacramento:** 81.4% (29.7% + 51.6%).
- **Los Angeles:** 69.5% (review 23.5%).
- **Lancaster:** 41.6%. Review 39.9%: reports say "AVENUE J", the map has East/West Avenue J. That's the unique-pair case in #201.

The lowest cities with 1,000+ crashes (La Habra 12.8%, Madera, Dinuba, Signal Hill, Tulare) are listed for the next step. La Habra in particular needs a look before anyone quotes it.

## Accuracy, with its basis
- **Exact street-name placement:** 98.8% at the right intersection on San Francisco's own records (claim C1).
- **Elsewhere:** against an agency's own police GPS where that GPS is usable as truth (#88; a lower bound).
- **Police GPS in bin 1** is checked for consistency with the report's roads, not graded.
- **Otherwise:** "can't verify".

## Method and basis
`tests/statewide/coverage.py`:
- **Inside a city:** the city's own OSM street network. The app's own locator runs on it under the app's gate (exact only), plus FARS for fatal crashes.
- **Outside cities:** police GPS is checked against the OSM roads around the point. The 617 crashes there without GPS get a network of just the roads they name.
- **Road type:** CCRS IsFreeway; a route number in a road name; inside a city or not.
- **KSI:** a death, or an IWP SuspectSerious / SevereInactive injury.
- **Districts:** `data/reference/caltrans_districts.csv`, from Caltrans's Local Assistance contacts page.
- **Code basis:** app code at main **5f54c02** (#197). That's **before #204 (unique_pair, gate off) and #206 (exact vs stated direction)**. The per-city count of exact placements that change under #206 is a follow-up.
- **Data:** CCRS mirror 2026-10-19, OSM 2026-10-18, FARS 2021–24 in the Tester database.

**Files:**
- `reports/testing/coverage-2026-10-22.json`: every roll-up (527 city names, 535 agencies, 58 counties, 12 districts, road types, district × road type).
- Per crash: `data/statewide/coverage_crashes.csv` (gitignored, 2.06 M rows: bin, outcome, reason, and place in every roll-up).

**Run notes:**
- An agency-based first version was wrong for sheriffs and CHP, which serve many cities. It now runs city by city.
- The run was split into shards and merged; the merge rebuilds every roll-up from the per-crash files.
- 59 crashes with a NULL city name were first missed, then added. The completeness check is how they were caught.

title: [Test] Step 2: the difficult bin (14.7%): what's in it, why, and which fixes gain most at what accuracy
body:
## Goal (user, 2026-10-22: "Start" step 2)
Understand the **difficult bin** from #207 (302,202 crashes, 14.7% of CCRS 2021–25) and rank the fixes that would move the most crashes into "on the map" **without losing accuracy**. Measure only: the user picks fixes from the ranking.

## Part A: what's in the bin (from `coverage_crashes.csv`, at current main)
For each reason, total and by Caltrans district, county, top 25 cities, road type, agency, severity (fatal / KSI):
- relaxed match held by the gate (incl. the unique_pair subset, #201)
- named streets don't meet on the map
- police GPS off the report's roads (+ what the names say)
- no cross street (NOT STATED etc.)
- near / fuzzy match held by the gate
- streets meet in more than one place
- no street map for this place (campuses, parks…)

## Part B: why (root causes, from samples)
For the two big reasons (**don't meet**, **GPS off the roads**), audit a random stratified sample (e.g. 300 each) and classify the root cause with evidence. Candidate causes:
- a misspelling or abbreviation the normalizer misses
- a route number vs a street name (alias)
- the street is missing from OSM, or named differently (check TIGER)
- the streets don't actually intersect (nearby or parallel)
- a private road or parking lot
- a freeway ramp
- the GPS is right and the names are wrong, or the reverse
- the 400 ft GPS check is too strict

## Part C: candidate fixes, what-if (each on the app's code paths where possible)
For each fix: **crashes gained** (statewide, by district) × **accuracy** (the #88/#144 hidden-GPS method on self-consistent truth, plus SF/San Jose/Pasadena open data), with the Wilson lower bound:
1. **unique_pair** auto-placement (#201; the tier exists, gate off)
2. **OSM + TIGER street network union** (decided earlier, not built; #17)
3. an **alias / abbreviation table** learned from the audit (any table needs user approval before use, per CLAUDE.md)
4. **disambiguation clues** for "meet in more than one place": offset direction, direction of travel, agency jurisdiction
5. **GPS-off cases:** trust the GPS when it is near *one* of the named roads, or at a known intersection?
6. **no cross street:** what's possible (FARS for fatal is done; the rest likely stays on review)

## Output
A **Difficult bin** sheet and tracker section, plus a **ranked fix table** (gain × accuracy × effort note) for the user. Same basis (mirror 2026-10-19, OSM 2026-10-18, stated commit); completeness guard.

title: Bug: leading abbreviations not expanded (AVE M ≠ Avenue M, ST/MT/FT ≠ Saint/Mount/Fort): up to 5,106 difficult crashes
body:
Found by the Tester in the #211 Part B audit (root causes of "named streets don't meet on the map").

**Bug:** `names.street_key` doesn't expand a street-type or title abbreviation at the **start** of a name, so the report's name and OSM's name get different cores and never match, in any tier (exact, relaxed or unique_pair). Suffix abbreviations are expanded (`FOOTHILLS BL` = `Foothills Boulevard`); leading ones are not:

| Report | OSM | `same_core` |
|---|---|---|
| `AVE M` | Avenue M | False (`AVE M` vs `AVENUE M`) |
| `AV J` | Avenue J | False |
| `AVE Q-8` | Avenue Q-8 | False |
| `ST TROPEZ CT` | Saint Tropez Court | False |
| `MT VERNON AVE` | Mount Vernon Avenue | False |
| `FT STOCKTON DR` | Fort Stockton Drive | False |
| `BL DE ORO` | Boulevard de Oro | False |
| `AVE OF THE STARS` | Avenue of the Stars | True (special-cased) |

**Size (#199 basis, CCRS mirror 2026-10-19):** up to **5,106 difficult crashes**, 19 of them fatal and 257 serious injury, name either road this way. By leading word: AVE 2,712, MT 890, ST 848, AV 721, FT 19. For AVE/AV alone it's 3,414, mostly in the Antelope Valley lettered-avenue grid: Lancaster 1,184, unincorporated 936, Palmdale 123; plus Indio 247 and Coachella 212. It's an upper bound, since some of these crashes may still fail for another reason.

**Failing test:** `tests/tester/test_names_leading_abbrev.py` (strict xfail; it passes once this is fixed).

**Not a learned alias:** these are fixed abbreviations of the same kind the normalizer already expands as suffixes, not a table learned from data, so the CLAUDE.md approval rule for aliases shouldn't apply. Engineering/PM should confirm.

title: GPS rules: apply the report's offset to intersection-snapped GPS; treat default/dispatch points as no GPS

## Goal (user decision, docs/03 2026-10-22)
1. **Snapped GPS → apply the report's offset.** If police GPS lies at (within ~50 ft of) the intersection the report names, and the report states a distance > 50 ft and a direction, place the crash at that intersection plus the stated offset, along the named road in the stated direction. Provenance `gps_offset_applied`. Assignment then runs as normal (an offset can move a crash out of the 250 ft influence area into a segment).
2. **Default / dispatch points → no GPS.** A GPS point shared by many crashes of one agency (a pile; thresholds from Tester's agency scan) that doesn't fit the report's streets is treated as no GPS, and the crash goes to street-name placement. Provenance records it.
3. Both are counted in T1 / pull log, and disclosed in methods.

- [ ] Failing tests first for each case, plus no-change cases (GPS fits and no offset; GPS already at the offset point).

title: fix(#212): a leading AVE/AV, ST, MT, FT, BL is the start of the name (AVE M = Avenue M)
body:
Closes #212

## What
- **Street key:** a leading street-type or title abbreviation is now the start of the name, as suffix abbreviations already were. When a name follows it (also after a leading direction):

  | Leading word | Becomes |
  |---|---|
  | `AVE`, `AV`, `AVN` | `AVENUE` |
  | `ST` | `SAINT` |
  | `MT` | `MOUNT` |
  | `FT` | `FORT` |
  | `BL`, `BLVD` | `BOULEVARD` |

  So `AVE M` = Avenue M, `W AVE J` = West Avenue J, `ST TROPEZ CT` = Saint Tropez Court, `MT VERNON AVE` = Mount Vernon Avenue.
- **What keeps its meaning:**
  - A word with nothing after it but a suffix: `W ST` is West Street, `N AVE` is North Avenue.
  - `ST HWY` / `ST RTE`: a highway, not Saint.
  - `FT` after a number or before a direction (`100 FT NORTH OF …`): feet. An existing test caught this.
- **Pull prefilter:** the name search also tries CHP's short spellings of a corridor core (`AVENUE J` → `AVE J`, `AV J`; `SAINT X` → `ST X`; …). Before, a corridor on Avenue J missed every no-GPS report written `AVE J`. The route-spelling flag is now set only for route numbers. PULL_FORMAT 20.
- **Not a learned alias:** these are fixed abbreviations of the same kind as the existing suffix table, not learned from data. So, in my reading, the CLAUDE.md approval rule for aliases doesn't apply. **PM to confirm, as the issue asks.**

## Tests
- The Tester's `tests/tester/test_names_leading_abbrev.py` passes; its strict xfail is removed.
- New guards in `test_names.py`: `W ST`, `N AVE`, `W AVE J`, `100 FT NORTH OF THE BRIDGE`, `ST HWY 1`, `ST JOHNS AVE`.
- Pull search words: `AVENUE J` → `AVE J` / `AV J`; routes are unchanged.
- Full suite: 429 passed with the network blocked. ruff clean.

## Re-validation (validate_geocode, test half, main vs this branch, `nice 19`)

| | exact n | exact correct | accuracy | Wilson low | review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF main | 3,635 | 3,590 | 98.8% | 98.3% | 195 |
| SF this PR | 3,643 | 3,597 | 98.7% | 98.3% | 186 |
| LB main | 2,825 | 2,512 | 88.9% | 87.7% | 781 |

- Overall: the Wilson low bound holds at 98.3%; rounded accuracy is 98.8% → 98.7%.

**LB:** 24 crashes leave review.
- 11 exact, all correct.
- 13 unique_pair suggestions, 11 correct (gate off).
- Mostly ST LOUIS AV and ST JOSEPH AV.

- **Basis:** the Tester's 79 corridors (tree 5e9ec19d57dc) plus Lancaster, Palmdale, Indio and Coachella (5447e864597e), on the CCRS mirror and the local OSM extract. Main vs this branch, `nice 19`.

title: test(#219): agency GPS quality profile + 'GPS right, names wrong' re-check
body:
Closes #219. Measure only; no app code.

## Findings
1. **Nine in ten police GPS points fit the report's own streets:** 90.0% of 1,554,835.
2. **The biggest problem is GPS that fits but sits at the intersection while the report places the crash farther along the road:** 78,095 crashes, 5.0%. Each is within 50 ft of where the two named roads meet, with a stated offset over 50 ft.
   - These are on the map today, at the intersection rather than the stated point; #218 rule 1 targets them.
   - Highest: Vacaville, South Gate and Glendale at about 38–40%, Vallejo, Woodland and Pomona at about 35–36%, Santa Ana 11.0%.
3. **More than a mile from the named roads:** 1.8% statewide.
   - Falling: 3.2% in 2021 → 1.1% in 2025.
   - San Jose PD is the outlier at 27.2%, alongside 63.2% of its GPS in degrees-minutes-seconds format (#143).
4. **Shared default / dispatch points are rare but real:** 1,755 crashes (0.1%) on 50 points.
   - The biggest are statewide CHP defaults: one point near Auburn holds 333 crashes from 59 CHP areas (2021–22), and two downtown Sacramento points hold 256 (2025 only) and 225.
   - There are also whole-degree points (34, −118), a placeholder (38.12346, −121.12346), and the CSU Northridge PD campus point.
   - Coordinates with 2 decimals or fewer: 547 more.
5. **Other off-road within a mile:** 2.9%. Highest: Thousand Oaks 18.3%, Santa Barbara 12.0%, Irvine 11.1%.

## "GPS right, names wrong"? No evidence for it as a pattern
284 difficult crashes were checked: police GPS off the report's roads but within a mile of them, 84 from the #211 audit sample and 200 at random.

In the **random sample of 200**:
- **2 (1%)** show the GPS at an intersection whose streets resemble both report names but aren't spelled the same (RANDAL AVENUE ↔ Randall Avenue; SEDCO HEIGHTS DR ↔ Sedco Heights Road). That's the only class where the GPS is right and the names are (slightly) wrong.
- **119 (60%)** agree with both: freeway crashes with the GPS on the freeway at a distance from the named cross street, or GPS at about the stated offset.
- **5** have the GPS *at* the named intersection. The **Tester's harness** missed these, because it clips each city's network to the city boundary and the intersection sits in a county pocket just outside (Fontana CHERRY AVE & HUNTER ST: GPS 19 ft away).
- **18** put the GPS at a different intersection. Nothing says the GPS is the right one.
- **49** put the GPS off any intersection: parking lots, driveways, house addresses.
- **7** sit on default points.

So the user's doubt holds. The audit's "near one road / within a mile" groups are mostly freeway crashes, offsets and wrong or off-street GPS, not wrong names.

## #215 question: is "street outside the city's clipped map" a harness artefact? Yes
Of the 71 such audit cases still difficult, **39 have the named street within the city's bounding box plus ~1 km**: county pockets and boundary streets the clipped network leaves out. Most of the rest name a city whose name CCRS uses for a county road nearby (Fresno: Millerton Rd, Academy Ave), plus a few name variants. A corridor study fetches the streets around the corridor, so it doesn't hit this.

**Proposal for run 8 (testing method, PM's call):** use the city's box plus 1 km, not the clipped outline, for both the locator and the GPS check. Label the old figure as harness-only.

title: fix(#218): report offset beats snapped GPS; default points and coarse GPS are no location
body:
Closes #218

## What
This implements the user's decision of 2026-10-22 (docs/03). The thresholds live in `backend/crashiq/config/gps.json` and come from the Tester's statewide scan (#219, posted on #218).

**1. Snapped GPS → the report's offset wins.**
- **When:** police GPS is within 50 ft of the study intersection the report names, and the report states more than 50 ft and a direction.
- **What happens:** the crash moves to that intersection plus the distance, along the named road that runs in that direction.
  - The primary road first, since CHP measures the distance along it.
  - Otherwise the cross street: "CRENSHAW BLVD | 132ND ST, 206 ft E" on a north–south Crenshaw is on 132nd.
  - If neither road runs that way, the GPS stays where it is.
- **Provenance:** `gps_offset_applied`. It still counts as GPS everywhere (`crashes.GPS_SOURCES`), and the original point is kept as `gps_as_reported`. Assignment then runs as usual.

**2. Default points and coarse GPS are not a location.**
- **Pile point:** an exact 5-decimal point shared by ≥10 crashes naming ≥5 street pairs, under 50% of which fit it, pooled across agencies. The point is ignored for the crashes it doesn't fit.
- **Coarse GPS:** ≤2 decimals in latitude or longitude, using the Tester's definition (trailing zeros don't count). Always ignored.
- **Where the point is kept:** on the crash as `gps_ignored` {lat, lon, reason, shared_by}. The report then takes the normal no-GPS path (names, city, cross street) and the locator places it.
- **Where pile points come from:**
  - Inside the corridor box: found from the pull itself.
  - Statewide: the Tester's 50 points (1,828 crashes), in `data/reference/gps_piles.json` with a `.md`.
- **Reaching piles elsewhere, as the PM asked:** a second name query per year reads reports that name the corridor, in the area, whose GPS sits on a listed point or is coarse. Before, these were silently missed: they were never in the box and never in the no-GPS query.
  - The query matches rounded latitude IN (…) and longitude IN (…) separately, then matches exactly in code.
  - It stays under half of `MAX_URL_SQL` (tested).
- **Fit check for piles inside the box:** a crash counts as not fitting only when it names a study intersection, or the corridor on the stretch, and the point is far from it. Anything the corridor can't judge counts as fitting.
  - The first same-basis run caught this: two real corners just past the study limits were taken for defaults (Balfour Rd & Brentwood Bl; La Cadena Dr & Barton Rd), and 12 of their reports dropped.
  - Fixed in the second commit, with a test that fails without the fix.

**Counts and disclosure:**
- **Pull log:** `gps_offset_applied`, `gps_default_ignored` (and `_by_agency`), `gps_coarse_ignored`, `gps_ignored_found_by_name`.
- **T1:** `located_gps_offset` (within `located_gps`) and `gps_ignored`.
- **Methods:** a sentence in the PDF method paragraph, and a "Police GPS vs the report's description" entry in Methods & references.
- **Labels:** frontend provenance labels.
- **PULL_FORMAT 22.**

## Tests
`tests/test_gps_rules.py`, 10 tests on the Crenshaw fixture:
- **Snapped GPS:** 300 ft N moves to the segment. An offset across the primary road goes along the cross street.
- **No-change cases:** GPS already at the offset point; an offset ≤50 ft; no offset.
- **Piles:** a pile of 12 crashes over 6 street pairs is ignored, and each is placed at its own corner.
  - Not a pile: 4 street pairs; a busy snapped intersection; a busy corner just past the stretch.
- **Coarse GPS** is ignored.
- **Config:** the defaults are the Tester's thresholds; the query fits the URL limit.

**Existing tests whose expectations change (commented in the code):**
- 21 fixture crashes sit at a named corner with a stated offset and now move. As a result the top screening finding on the Crenshaw study moves from West 135th Street (12 of 21) to West 147th Street (5 of 8).
- Fixture crash 9300001 was built as "GPS far away". Its point is 33.95, −118.4 (2 decimals), so under the coarse rule it's no GPS. It's now found and placed by its names, Crenshaw / 135th in Hawthorne. The pull count goes from 125 to 126.
- The CKAN call budget in `test_pull_efficiency` goes from 25 to 30, for the new name query (one per year).

Full suite: 442 passed with the network blocked. Vitest: 69 passed. ruff and eslint clean.

## Same-basis check (82 corridors, main 2d7461b vs this branch, nice 19)
Basis: the Tester's 79 corridors plus Lancaster, Palmdale, Indio and Coachella, on the CCRS mirror and the local OSM extract.

**Snapped GPS moved by the report's offset: 568 crashes.**

| Agency (NCIC) | 1969 | 3300 | 1956 | 1962 | 1955 | 3024 | 3015 | 1944 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crashes moved | 133 | 81 | 54 | 42 | 40 | 32 | 31 | 24 |

- 133 stay at an intersection.
- 58 move from an intersection to a segment.
- 80 move from an intersection to excluded: 56 outside the buffer, 24 outside the study limits.
  - Example: `CLARA ST | GARFIELD AV, 294 ft W` is on Clara, 294 ft off Garfield.
  - Example: `ATLANTIC AV | PATATA ST, 515 ft S` is past the study limits.
  - Each was counted at the intersection before.

**GPS not used: 76 crashes.**
- 52 coarse and 24 on the Tester's listed default points. No dynamic pile is left after the fix.
- 64 of them were newly found by name. For example, freeway crashes at Seal Beach, Westminster, Selma and Lodi with GPS on the statewide CHP default near Auburn or in downtown Sacramento.
- Where they end up:
  - 59 are on the corridor but off the study stretch, so they're excluded and listed.
  - 12 are placed and counted.
  - 3 go to the review list.
  - 2 are placed and excluded by the normal rules.

**Pull totals:**
- 25,670 → 25,733 crashes: 65 new.
- 2 gone, both coarse freeway crashes that don't name the corridor (I-10 / 22nd St, Banning; I-15 / Oak Hill Rd, San Bernardino). They were listed as excluded "freeway" before, never counted.
- Counted crashes: 6,672 → 6,597 (81 out, mostly the offset moves above; 6 in).

**Locator re-validation (validate_geocode, test half): unchanged.**

| | exact n | accuracy | Wilson low |
|---|---|---|---|
| SF | 3,643 | 98.7% | 98.3% |
| LB | 2,836 | 89.0% | 87.8% |

**Not run here:** the Tester's citywide sample, where Santa Ana is expected to be high.

title: OSM + TIGER/Line street network for placement (user decision; TIGER downloads approved)
body:
## Goal (user decision, docs/03 2026-10-22)
Build the **OSM + TIGER/Line** street network for placement and the street-name checks, so streets missing from or named differently in OSM can be matched. The user approved the TIGER downloads (US Census, public domain).

## Build
- **TIGER source:** Census TIGER/Line "ROADS" (or "EDGES") per California county (58 files), current vintage. Download from census.gov at build or refresh time, and cache like the Parties file cache (#197): keyed by vintage, refresh yearly. Document size, location and attribution.
- **Union:** add TIGER segments and names to the network. Where a TIGER street coincides with an OSM way (geometry within a few metres), use it only as an **extra name** for that way; otherwise add it as a new way. Keep provenance (`osm`, `tiger`, `both`) per way and name.
- **Use in the locator** (all tiers) and the GPS street check. Placements that rely on a TIGER-only name or way get a visible tag.
- **Re-use** the PR #16 experiment code where it helps (TIGER ≈ OSM; the union added +1–2 pts at the same accuracy).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Failing tests first: a street present only in TIGER gets matched; a duplicate street isn't double-counted; an OSM-name vs TIGER-name pair at one way matches either.
- [ ] Re-validation (`validate_geocode`, SF/LB/Riverside, osm vs both): exact and unique_pair accuracy and coverage. The SF low bound stays ≥ 98.0% or it's reported.
- [ ] Tester's run 9 measures the statewide gain and accuracy (#211 estimated up to ~18,100).

title: [Test] Draft street alias table from the difficult bin, for the user's entry-by-entry approval
body:
## Goal (user decision, docs/03 2026-10-22)
Draft a **street alias / spelling table** from the #211 audit for the user to approve **entry by entry** before the app uses it (CLAUDE.md: nothing is learned without user approval).

## Tester (measure and draft only)
- Mine the difficult bin (CCRS 2021–25) for report street names that don't match the network, where evidence ties them to a specific map street: police GPS self-consistent on that street; a unique cross-street pair; a frequent repeated spelling.
- Propose entries as `report name (normalized) → map street`, scoped by city or county (aliases are local). For each entry: crashes it would place, evidence (example crashes, GPS agreement %), and accuracy on hidden GPS where possible.
- Exclude anything ambiguous (one report name → two map streets in scope).
- Output: `data/reference/street_aliases_DRAFT.csv` with a status column (all `proposed`), plus a short review sheet for the user sorted by impact. The app doesn't read the DRAFT file.

## Then
PM walks the user through the top entries; approved ones move to the live table that Engineering wires into the locator.

title: test(#230): draft street alias table (912 proposed, for user approval; not read by the app)
body:
Closes #230. Measure and draft only: **the app doesn't read `data/reference/street_aliases_DRAFT.csv`**; every entry needs the user's approval (CLAUDE.md).

## Summary

- **912 entries proposed**, which would place **4,635 difficult crashes** with the app's current gate. On hidden GPS they are right at the intersection 3,724 of 3,792 times (98.2%, 95% low 97.7%).
- By kind: 161 entries (2,287 crashes) are standard abbreviations spelled out (JR = Junior, EXPWY = Expressway, RT = Route, PW = Parkway, TRL = Trail, HW = Highway): one name-cleaner rule would fix them in every city, so they are better approved as rules than as entries. 751 entries (2,348 crashes) are local spellings or names (HAWTHORN BL = Hawthorne Boulevard, FAIRMONT AV = Fairmount Avenue): the real alias table.
- 465 of the 912 entries (2,850 crashes) have no crash with GPS to check them: they rest on the street evidence alone (marked "no GPS to check"); the rest are checked as above.
- 12,762 candidates excluded: only N crashes point to one street 12,588; hidden GPS right only N/N 630; ambiguous 42; agreement N% 26; route number mismatch 16.
- The long tail: 11,689 candidates rest on a single crash (one-off misspellings such as MAONOLIA, HYPE PARK DR). A table can't cover them; the fuzzy tier holds them for review today.
- 139 candidates are one pattern, a route number after the name ("PACIFIC COAST HWY - SR1", "BEACH BL - SR39") or a direction in brackets ("(N)"): better fixed once in the name cleaner (a rule, like #212) than city by city.

Review sheet for the user (top 40 by impact): `reports/testing/alias-review-2026-10-22.md`. Column guide: `data/reference/street_aliases_DRAFT.md`. Excluded candidates with reasons: `reports/testing/alias-2026-10-22/alias_excluded.csv`.

## What
Builds the user's decision and download approval of 2026-10-22 (docs/03): the placement network is OpenStreetMap joined with Census TIGER/Line roads.

- **TIGER cache** (`sources/tiger_files.py`): EDGES and FEATNAMES per California county, downloaded in the background the first time a study needs that county.
  - Kept as a trimmed SQLite copy (`data/cache/tiger/<vintage>/<fips>.sqlite`, gitignored; `CRASHIQ_TIGER_DIR` moves it): named road segments only, with their points, bounding box and names.
  - Vintage 2026 (`config/tiger.json`); a new vintage downloads into its own folder.
  - A county still downloading leaves the network OSM-only, logs `network.tiger_pending`, and the next view pulls again (like #197). A failed download is retried after an hour.
  - Live data.ca.gov only; fakes and harnesses opt in with `app.state.tiger`.
- **Which counties:** padded county boxes, `data/reference/ca_county_boxes.json`, built from CCRS GPS by `backend/scripts/build_county_boxes.py`. No extra download.
- **Union** (`union.py`):
  - A TIGER segment that runs along OSM ways only adds its names to them (`tiger:name`; way source `both`). "Runs along": ≥ 80% of its 10 m samples within 12 m, in the same direction (±20°), with the last 15 m at each end left out. A street is never added twice.
  - Otherwise the segment is a new way (`tiger`), joined at an OSM node within 12 m or spliced into the OSM way there.
  - Name provenance is kept per street key and per node (`Network.key_source`, `src_at`).
- **Where it's used:**
  - **Locator, all tiers.** A placement that needs a TIGER-only name or road is tagged `placed_on: tiger`, counted in T1 (`located_tiger`) and listed in every table's sources line.
  - **The pull's name filters and the GPS street check.** These use TIGER's names for the corridor and for each study intersection. The names are stored with the pull (`network_alt`), so the assignment uses the same ones.
  - **The FARS road check.**
- **Why the filters matter:** the pull drops a no-GPS report whose cross street isn't one of the study's intersections by OSM's name, before the locator ever sees it. Test: a report naming the cross street by TIGER's other name is `cross_street_not_on_corridor` on OSM alone; on the union it is kept and placed at West 135th Street, tagged `tiger`.
- **Route names:** TIGER's route spellings (`State Hwy 39`, `State Rte 1`, `US Hwy 101`, `I- 5`) now read as routes.
- **Docs and deps:** methods text in the PDF paragraph and Methods & references (TIGER source added); `data/reference/tiger.md`; `pyshp==3.1.6` pinned. PULL_FORMAT 23.

## Tests (failing first; acceptance cases)
- `test_union.py`:
  - a TIGER-only street gets matched;
  - one meeting the corridor between OSM nodes is spliced in, in order;
  - a TIGER copy of an OSM street isn't added twice;
  - an OSM name and a TIGER name on one way both match (and the TIGER name is tagged);
  - far TIGER is left out;
  - a cross street beside a divided road's far carriageway doesn't name it (the SF regression below; fails without the direction check).
- `test_tiger_network.py`:
  - the county cache, built from tiny TIGER-shaped zips made in the test with pyshp: download once, roads only, names;
  - a failed download leaves no copy and waits;
  - the end-to-end pull above;
  - a county still downloading leaves the network OSM-only, with the re-pull hook;
  - FakeCkan never downloads.
- Full suite: 455 passed with the network blocked. Vitest: 69 passed. ruff clean.

## Re-validation (validate_geocode, test half, `--network osm` vs the new `--network union`, nice 19)

| | exact n | exact accuracy / Wilson low | exact + unique_pair coverage | exact + unique_pair accuracy / low | review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SF** OSM | 3,643 | 98.7% / **98.3%** | 90.5% | 98.7% / 98.3% | 186 |
| **SF** union | 3,662 | 98.7% / **98.3%** | 91.0% | 98.7% / 98.3% | 179 |
| LB OSM | 2,836 | 89.0% / 87.8% | 83.6% | 86.4% / 85.5% | 757 |
| LB union | 3,186 | 89.0% / 87.8% | 85.4% | 86.2% / 85.2% | 661 |
| Riverside OSM | 2,259 | 57.0% / 55.0% | 89.6% | 56.4% / 54.4% | 193 |
| Riverside union | 2,283 | 56.8% / 54.8% | 90.3% | 56.2% / 54.2% | 190 |

**The SF low bound holds at 98.3%,** above the 98.0% bar.

**Union network size:**

| | TIGER segments | coincide with OSM | added | spliced | street names (OSM → union) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF | 18,073 | 17,505 | 568 | 83 | 2,731 → 2,958 |
| LB | 14,001 | 12,768 | 1,233 | 145 | 1,610 → 2,109 |
| Riverside | 12,172 | 11,483 | 689 | 65 | 3,606 → 4,007 |

**For the user/PM: placements that need a TIGER-only name or road are less accurate than each city's average.**

| | TIGER-only placements | right |
|---|---|---|
| SF | 111 | 101 (91%) |
| LB | 499 | 421 (84%) |
| Riverside | 99 | 48 (48%) |

They are tagged and counted, so they can be gated separately: auto-place, or review with a suggestion. Today they follow their tier (exact / unique_pair auto-place). I haven't built a separate gate; that's a user decision if wanted.

**The first validation run caught a regression before the fix in the second commit:** SF exact 3,643 → 3,598, with 66 crashes going to "streets meet in more than one place". TIGER's centerline of a cross street ran beside a divided road's far carriageway (Masonic at Geary). The direction check fixed it.

**Not done here:** the statewide gain and accuracy is Tester's run 9 (#211 estimated up to ~18,100 crashes). It needs `app.state.tiger` set in the harness, and downloads the corridors' county files. So far this run downloaded SF, Los Angeles and Riverside (copies: 3.5, 76 and 43 MB).

title: Tier verified_typo: fix small typos automatically when only one street fits and the cross street confirms (gate off; measure first)
body:
## Goal (user, 2026-10-22: "1 yes")
Fix one-off typos (e.g. `MAONOLIA` → Magnolia) automatically **when it isn't a guess**, so a human doesn't have to check ~11,700 crashes. Plain fuzzy matching is too loose (75–89%: Westmont vs Westmore).

## Tier `verified_typo` (Engineering builds behind the gate, default OFF)
A report name with no exact/unique_pair match is corrected to map street M only if **all** hold:
1. Small edit: ≤ 2 character edits (or a transposition) from M, after normalization.
2. No rival: no other street in the city/area network within the same edit distance (or within distance+1).
3. The cross street confirms it: with the corrected name, the street pair meets at exactly **one** intersection (the unique_pair test).
4. Where the crash has police GPS, it agrees (fits the corrected streets).
Provenance `verified_typo`; counted in T1; shown in methods.

## Tester measures (after run 9)
Accuracy on hidden self-consistent police GPS (#144 method), SF/San Jose/Pasadena/LAPD open data where linkable; n, accuracy and Wilson low, vs exact on the same truth. Coverage gain statewide by district. Also report how many of the ~11,700 single-crash typos it resolves, and what's left.

PM brings the numbers to the user; it auto-places only on the user's OK.

title: feat(#233): tier verified_typo behind the gate (off)
body:
Closes #233

## What
Tier **`verified_typo`**: the user's "1 yes" of 2026-10-22, as relayed on #233. **I don't see it recorded in docs/03 yet. PM, please record it before anyone switches the tier on.**

The tier is behind the gate and **off**: `verified_typo` is not in `config/placement.json` `auto_tiers`, so a match is a one-click suggestion on the review list.

A report name with no exact or one-place match is corrected to map street M only when all of these hold:

1. **Small edit:** at most 2 character edits from M (optimal string alignment, so swapping two neighbouring letters counts as one).
   - 1 edit for names of 4 letters.
   - **None under 4 letters, on either side.** The existing rule "short names are too risky" (`OAKK` → Oak) stays.
   - **Digits are never changed:** 15TH is not a typo of 16TH. Routes aren't corrected either.
2. **No rival:** no other map street within the same number of edits or one more.
3. **The cross street confirms it:** the corrected pair meets at exactly one intersection, with the #205 direction checks.
4. **GPS agrees:** where the crash has police GPS, the corner is within 400 ft plus the stated offset.

**Where it sits:** it's tried after exact / unique_pair / relaxed / near and **before plain fuzzy**. Typos that used to become a fuzzy suggestion now become a `verified_typo` suggestion when they pass the checks above.

**Counts, methods, config:**
- Provenance `verified_typo`.
- T1 `located_verified_typo`, plus a frontend provenance label.
- Methods & references entry, and a PDF method sentence saying it's a suggestion until measured and approved.
- Thresholds live in `config/placement.json` under `verified_typo`.

**`validate_geocode`:**
- Reports the tier: n, accuracy, Wilson low and coverage, in the printout and in `summary.json`.
- New arm "A++ exact + unique_pair + verified_typo".
- The locator is now given **the crash without its coordinates**. In the hidden-GPS cities (LB, Riverside) the crash's `lat`/`lon` are the truth, and the new GPS check would have seen them. Condition 4 is therefore not exercised in validation; it applies in the app and in the Tester's harness where real GPS exists.

## Tests
`tests/test_verified_typo.py`:
- `MAONOLIA` → Magnolia.
- Rivals as close or one edit further (Westmont / Westmore) → no correction.
- Digits are never corrected.
- 4 letters allow 1 edit; 3 letters are never corrected.
- A corrected pair that meets twice → no correction.
- Police GPS must agree.
- Exact names are untouched.
- Off by default (suggestion) and on with the gate.

`test_locate`: `OAKLANDD AVE` is now `verified_typo` instead of `fuzzy`; the short-name rule is unchanged.

Full suite: 465 passed with the network blocked. Vitest: 69 passed. ruff clean.

## First numbers (validate_geocode, test half, nice 19; the real measurement is the Tester's after run 9)

| | n | accuracy | Wilson low | coverage gain | exact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF | 27 | 96.3% | 81.7% | +0.67% | unchanged 3,643 at 98.7% / 98.3% |
| LB | 57 | 78.9% | 66.7% | +0.90% | unchanged 2,836 at 89.0% / 87.8% |

The tier is well below the 98% bar in LB. That is what the gate is for: it stays off until the user decides.

**Limit for corridor studies:** the pull drops a no-GPS report whose cross street isn't a study intersection by name before the locator runs. So in corridor studies this tier only sees typos in names the pull already matched loosely. It mainly shows in citywide placement (validate_geocode, the Tester's harness). If the user turns it on, the pull's cross-street filter would need the same check; I'd do that then.

No PULL_FORMAT bump: the gate is off, so nothing placed changes. Cached pulls keep their old suggestion labels until the next refresh.

title: Bug: OSM + TIGER loses correct OSM placements (TIGER copies near OSM streets: tiger_road holds, second meeting points)
body:
Found by the Tester in run 9 (#229 OSM + TIGER, PR #232).

**Bug:** with TIGER on, correct OSM placements are lost. On the agencies' own open data (validate_geocode test halves, main, OSM-only vs `--network union`, same code otherwise):

| | Auto-placed by OSM alone, lost with TIGER | ...of which right with OSM | Gained with TIGER | ...right |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| San Francisco (DataSF) | 35 | 33 | 11 | 11 |
| Los Angeles (LAPD 2024) | 66 | 63 | 22 | 19 |

Statewide (run 9 coverage, every CCRS crash 2021–25, OSM + TIGER only where the city's OSM network is): thousands of crashes that OSM alone places are held. In San Francisco alone, 250: 140 "streets meet in more than one place" and 110 flagged `tiger_road`.

**Two mechanisms, both in the union:**
1. **`tiger_road` on an OSM intersection.** A TIGER copy of an OSM street that `union` doesn't recognize as the same street (not within `coincide_m` along `coincide_share` of its length, e.g. ~25–40 m off) is added as a TIGER-only way and spliced into the cross street near the OSM intersection. Within `CLUSTER_M` (80 m) the locator treats both as one intersection and can pick the TIGER node. `_tiger(..., road=True)` is then true, so the gate holds a crash OSM places exactly. Examples, San Francisco: EMBARCADERO & SANSOME ST, KEZAR DR & LINCOLN WY, SAN BRUNO AV & DIVISION ST.
2. **A second meeting point.** The TIGER copy diverges from OSM, so the same street pair meets again more than 160 m away (2 × `CLUSTER_M`), and the crash goes to review as "streets meet in more than one place". Examples, San Francisco: JOHN F SHELLEY DR & MANSELL ST (meeting points 0, 23 and 393 m apart), 19TH AV & WINSTON DR (0, 14, 25, 236, 240 m).

**Failing test** (mechanism 1, a synthetic network through the app's own `union`): `tests/tester/test_union_tiger_regression.py`, strict xfail. OSM alone auto-places it; with a TIGER copy of the cross street 37 m off, the placement is held as `tiger_road`.

**A fix should probably** (Engineering's call):
- prefer an intersection node that OSM alone supports when the cluster has one, and not flag `tiger_road` when OSM keys alone meet there;
- not count a TIGER-only copy of a street OSM already has (same name, nearby, roughly parallel) as a second meeting point.

Accuracy split, as asked on #232 (Engineering's 91/84/48% mixed both kinds):

| | tiger_name (TIGER name on an OSM street; auto under its tier) | tiger_road (TIGER-only road; held), if auto |
|---|---|---|
| San Francisco open data | 59 of 60 right (98.3%) | 40 of 42 (95.2%) |
| LAPD open data | 54 of 61 (88.5%) | 66 of 72 (91.7%) |

Statewide hidden-GPS numbers follow in the run-9 report.

title: fix(#243): switch the OSM + TIGER union off until it stops losing OSM placements
body:
Refs #243 (step A: switch off; the fix itself is step B).

## What
Run 9 shows the OSM + TIGER union (#232) **losing correct OSM placements** on open-data truth: SF −35 auto (33 of them right), LA −66 (63 right). This is a regression, so the union goes off now.

- **The switch:** `config/tiger.json` `"union": false` (new key, default off).
- **What off means:**
  - The network is OSM only.
  - No TIGER names reach the pull's name filters or the GPS / FARS checks.
  - The locator runs on plain OSM.
  - Nothing is downloaded: `tiger_for()` returns None, even when a harness sets `app.state.tiger`.
- **Methods text follows the switch:** the PDF method paragraph says "The street network is OpenStreetMap."; the Methods & references entry is marked `planned`, with the reason.
- **PULL_FORMAT 26,** so pulls made on the union are redone.

## Tests
- New: with the switch off, a TIGER cache present is neither used nor downloaded. The report naming TIGER's cross-street name stays `cross_street_not_on_corridor`, and the network log says `osm`.
- The union tests run with the switch on (fixture), so the code stays tested for step B.
- Full suite: 473 passed with the network blocked. ruff clean.

## Step B (#243, next)
- OSM nodes take precedence.
- A TIGER copy of an already-named OSM street never adds nodes or meeting points.
- Merge tolerance and direction checks.
- A TIGER-only road may add a meeting point only if no OSM pair meets within ~200 m.
- Proved on SF/LA open data before/after: no correct OSM placement lost.

title: D1: place freeway crashes by the user's method (crossing + offset, ramp terminal, gore)
body:
## Goal
Place D1 (freeway) crashes in the difficult bin (24,076: mainline 16,793, ramp 2,528, freeway-to-freeway 1,683) the way the user locates them by hand. Gated (off by default) until Tester measures it and the user approves.

## The user's method (2026-10-23, in PM chat), three worked examples
| # | Record | User's pin | Police GPS, distance from pin |
|---|---|---|---|
| A mainline | 1456564 Lawndale, `I-405 N/B (SAN DIEGO FREEWAY)` / `ARTESIA BLVD.`, S 200 F, IsFreeway True | 33.873296, -118.342525 | 237 ft |
| B ramp | 2327267 Stockton, `NB I5 OFF RAMP` / `FLORA ST`, N 10 F | 37.957310, -121.311389 | 93 ft |
| C fwy-to-fwy | Martinez, `I-680 S/B TO SR-4` / `SR-4`, N 1320 F, IsFreeway True (1428399 / 1895421) | 38.001344, -122.078158 | 2,066 / 883 ft |

Rules as the user described them:
1. **IsFreeway = True** means the crash is on the mainline. The secondary road crosses over or under the freeway; start at that crossing, then go the stated distance along the stated-direction lanes.
2. **Ramp** in PrimaryRoad (OFF/ON RAMP): start where the ramp meets the secondary road (ramp terminal). Distances under the ~400 ft margin are placed at the terminal itself.
3. **`<fwy> TO <fwy>` with IsFreeway True:** treated as mainline before the connector. The user measured from the **gore** (where the connector splits from the mainline), not from the SR-4 crossing.

## Open points (PM to confirm with user; build both as options, Tester measures)
- Example A: record says **S** of Artesia; the user said "north". Confirm direction is read as written (S).

title: fix(#243): OSM first in the OSM + TIGER union: no correct OSM placement lost (SF/LA)
body:
Closes #243

Includes the Tester's failing test from #244 (same commit; its strict xfail is removed here because it passes). The union stays **switched off** (`config/tiger.json` `union: false`, #245); this PR is the fix that would let it be switched back on.

## What: OSM first, TIGER adds only what OSM lacks
Run 9 found the union losing correct OSM placements on SF/LA open data. Fixing it took four same-basis runs; each run exposed one more way TIGER interfered.

1. **A loose TIGER copy of a named OSM street** (25–40 m off, outside `coincide_m`) was added as a TIGER-only way and spliced near the OSM corner. The locator could then pick its node, flag `tiger_road`, and the gate held the crash.
   - Now a TIGER segment running along an OSM way of the same name adds nothing: within `copy_m` = 60 m, same direction (±20°), for half its length.
   - Within an intersection's cluster, the locator takes a node where the streets meet on OSM alone.
2. **A diverging copy made a second meeting point** more than 160 m away. A TIGER way now never joins where it would make two streets meet that OSM already has meeting, anywhere in the network. That's stricter than the suggested ~200 m, and it also covers the 393 m cases.
3. **TIGER names merged onto the wrong OSM way:**
   - TIGER's "Market St" along OSM's Clayton Street.
   - "Griffith Park Dr" along OSM's Griffith Park Road, while OSM's Griffith Park Drive is elsewhere.

   Now a TIGER name is never added to an OSM way when another OSM way carries it (core and street type). A TIGER-only road under a name OSM already has here is not added either: TIGER's Hill St in Santa Monica beat OSM's South Hill Street downtown.
4. **A TIGER name that only repeats the way's own name with a direction** ("N Whitley Ave" on Whitley Avenue) became a different key. The node where Whitley Ave and Whitley Ter merge then looked like a second corner, 145 m from the real one. Such names are no longer added.

New union counts in the log: `copy_of_osm_street`, `join_refused_osm_meets`, `names_refused_osm_has`, `same_name_as_osm_street`. `validate_geocode` rows carry `tiger_road`.

## Tests
- The Tester's `test_union_keeps_the_osm_placement` passes; its xfail is removed.
- New tests, which fail without the fix:
  - a diverging copy adds no second meeting point;
  - a loose copy adds nothing;
  - another OSM street's name is never given to a way, including the same core with another street type;
  - a TIGER road under a name OSM has elsewhere isn't added;
  - a directional copy of a way's own name isn't added.
- Full suite: 481 passed with the network blocked. ruff clean.

## Proof (validate_geocode, open-data truth, test halves, `--network osm` vs `--network union`)
Crash by crash. "Auto" means exact or unique_pair and not `tiger_road`, as the gate decides.

| | OSM auto (right) | union auto (right) | **lost** | **flipped** | gained (right) | tiger_road held |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SF (DataSF) | 3,655 (3,608) | 3,655 (3,608) | **0** | **0** | 0 | 1 |
| LA (LAPD) | 5,743 (4,813) | 5,745 (4,814) | **0** | **0** | 2 (1) | 0 |

- Lost = auto under OSM, not under the union. Flipped = auto in both, right under OSM and wrong under the union.
- Run 9 found SF −35 and LA −66. The run-by-run lost counts went:
  - run 1: SF 7, LA 25;
  - run 2: SF 0, LA 1;
  - run 3: SF 0, LA 0, with 1 flip;
  - this run: 0 / 0.
- Accuracy: SF exact 3,651 → 3,652 at 98.7% (Wilson low 98.3%, unchanged); LA exact 2,302 → 2,303 at 82.3%.

**What's left of the union's gain:** almost nothing on these two cities. OSM first means TIGER now only adds streets and names OSM doesn't have at all. Whether to switch the union back on is for the user; the numbers above are what it would do. With `tiger_only_auto` still false, TIGER-only roads would stay suggestions.
