title: feat(#246): D1 freeway crashes placed by the report, behind the gate (off)
body:
Closes #246 (build; the Tester measures, and the user decides whether it auto-places)

## What
Freeway (D1) crashes placed by the report, as the user described it on 2026-10-23 (docs/03 D1; `knowledge/methods/freeway-crashes.md`). Every field is read as written: the compass direction is literal, and "X TO Y" names a connector.

**`backend/crashiq/freeway.py`** works on the raw OSM elements (highway, ref and oneway tags).

| Kind | Report | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| **Mainline** | `I-405 N/B` / `ARTESIA BLVD.` / S 200 F, IsFreeway | where the reference street crosses the lanes of the stated travel direction, then the stated distance along those lanes toward the stated compass direction |
| **Ramp** | `NB I5 OFF RAMP` / `FLORA ST` / N 10 F | the terminal where a ramp joined to that route and direction meets the reference street; under 400 ft at the terminal, else along the ramp |
| **Connector** | `I-680 S/B TO SR-4` / `SR-4` / N 1320 F | from where the connector reaches the second freeway, the stated distance along the connector |

- **Connectors:** a route usually has a connector to each direction of the other. A connector counts only if the stated direction follows it for most of the distance. The spot is used only when those walks agree.
- **Never a guess:** a description that fits more than one place (crossings or terminals more than 600 ft apart), or no place, returns nothing.
- **Gate:** new tier `freeway_offset`. Not in `config/placement.json` `auto_tiers`, so it is a one-click suggestion on the review list until it's measured and approved.
  - With the gate on, the report beats the officer's GPS (D1 rule 4): a GPS point more than 400 ft from the report's spot moves there, and `gps_as_reported` is kept.
  - With the gate off, GPS is left as it is.
- **Freeway corridors only.** Arterial corridor studies are untouched; there, freeway crashes stay excluded unless "include ramps" is on.
- **Counts and methods:** T1 `located_freeway`, the quality strip, a provenance label, and a Methods & references entry.

## Tests (`tests/test_freeway.py`)
The OSM fixtures are cut from the local OSM extract (2026-10-18), 900 m around each crash: `tests/fixtures/overpass_d1_*.json`, 117–187 KB each.

| Example | Truth (as the user set it) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A 1456564 Lawndale | computed: 200 ft **S** of the Artesia crossing, on the NB lanes | 180–220 ft south of the crossing midpoint, on an NB I-405 way; > 400 ft from the officer's NW-corner GPS |
| B 2327267 Stockton | the user's pin 37.957310, −121.311389 | **35 ft** |
| C 1428399 Martinez | the officer's GPS 37.9971, −122.0734 | **213 ft** |

Also covered:
- Nothing found → None: a street not on the map, a route not there, a route-numbered city street.
- Reading the report.
- Off by default → suggestion.
- Gate on → placed, and the disagreeing GPS moves.
- An arterial corridor is untouched.

Full suite: 483 passed with the network blocked. Vitest: 69 passed. ruff and eslint clean.

## Not done here
- **The measurement:** hidden-GPS accuracy on D1 crashes with trustworthy GPS, per sub-type, Wilson low, run 9 basis. That's the Tester's step. `freeway.place(raw, crash)` takes any Overpass-shaped network.
- **Wider reach:** placement's network is the corridor's OSM within 40 m of the line, which carries the ramps and crossing streets that touch the freeway. A ramp terminal far from the freeway on a street that doesn't reach it wouldn't be found. Run 9 will show whether that matters.

title: feat(#248): the derived Caltrans postmile of each counted state-highway crash
body:
Closes #248

## What
Each counted crash on a state route gets its **Caltrans postmile**, looked up by code (no agent). This is the user's decision of 2026-10-23 (docs/03). The postmile is **derived from where CrashIQ placed the crash and never changes placement.**

- **Layer:** the public **SHN Postmiles Tenth** layer: https://caltrans-gis.dot.ca.gov/arcgis/rest/services/CHhighway/SHN_Postmiles_Tenth/FeatureServer/0. It has a point every 0.1 mile on every state route, each side of a divided road separately.
  - It's the same layer, query and vintage as the Tester's measurement (agreed with the Tester): `/query`, `outSR=4326`, 2,000 rows a page, ordered by OBJECTID.
  - The layer reports no edit date, so the download date is the vintage.
- **Cache:** `data/cache/postmiles/shn_postmiles_tenth_<date>.sqlite` (gitignored; `CRASHIQ_POSTMILE_DIR` moves it).
  - Downloaded once in the background the first time it's needed; refreshed after a year. A failed download is retried after an hour.
  - Live data.ca.gov only. Tests and harnesses opt in with `app.state.postmiles`.
- **Lookup** (`postmile.py`), for a placed crash whose roads name a state route:
  - take the segment between two consecutive 0.1-mile points of one line (route, county, prefix, suffix, side) nearest the crash, within 100 m;
  - prefer the side of the stated travel direction;
  - interpolate the postmile along the segment;
  - never bridge gaps over 0.15 mi.
- **Format:** `LA-405 PM 12.345` (Caltrans style, with prefix and suffix), marked `derived`.
- **Where it appears:**
  - the crash list API (`postmile` per crash);
  - the location drill-down's crash list;
  - a new Excel sheet, **"State-highway postmiles"**: crash, roads, date, postmile, side, direction, distance to the route, assigned location.
- **Recorded:** source and date in `knowledge/sources/ca-caltrans-postmiles.md`; a Methods & references entry with the source.

## Tests (`tests/test_postmile.py`)
The fixture is LA-405 and LA-107 near Artesia, cut from the layer as its query API returns it: 84 points, served in two pages.
- A published point returns its postmile within 0.01 mi.
- A point between two published points is interpolated within 0.01 mi.
- The stated direction picks that side's points.
- Off the route, or another route → none.
- A crash gets a labelled, derived postmile; a city street gets none.
- The download is kept by date, and a failure waits.
- The crash list and the Excel export carry it.
- Fake CKAN never downloads.

Full suite passes with the network blocked. ruff clean.

## Checked on the real layer (the Tester's full copy, 311,198 points, read only)
- **2,000 random published points:** 2,000 within 0.01 mi, with the same county, prefix and suffix.
- **2,000 midpoints between consecutive points:** 2,000 within 0.01 mi of the interpolated postmile.

How close the postmile is to Caltrans' own (TASAS) depends on how well the crash was placed. That's the Tester's measurement against CCRS's postmile marker, on the same layer.

title: docs(knowledge): how California police capture crash GPS
body:
Docs-only. Adds `knowledge/sources/ca-police-gps-capture.md` and four dated entries in `knowledge/lessons.md`. No `backend/` or `frontend/` changes.

Requested after the user's 2026-10-25 decision to keep officer GPS when it fits the named roads (#262).

**Main findings (public sources, each cited in the file):**
- **CHP's manual (HPM 110.5 ch. 3, revised April 2021) treats GPS as the main crash location.** It is entered in decimal degrees to 5 places. The postmile ("Milepost") is filled only if GPS can't be collected, and isn't required on ramps or connectors. That explains the near-empty `Milepost*` fields.
- **The GPS can be a scene fix or a point picked later.** The manual allows the MDC, Streets and Trips or Google Earth "upon return to their local Area office". It is meant to be the crash point (or where the vehicle left the road), not the patrol car. The written distance is to be measured (tape, pacing or odometer), not estimated.
- **CHP replaced its report software in 2020–21** (CARS → Crash Manager, with one-click GPS). The big Auburn and Sacramento default piles appear only in 2021–22, so they are likely software defaults. That link is unconfirmed.
- **City PDs file the same CHP 555 fields** through vendor systems (e.g. Crossroads) or on paper. SFPD geocodes from street names in its own system. San Jose's open crash layer is keyed to intersections and carries the report (TCR) number, so it is a possible second truth for San Jose.
- **Still unconfirmed:** what sets `IsLocationReferToNarrative`, the device behind Crash Manager's GPS, and the LAPD and Long Beach vendors. These are listed as open questions. Confirming them would take a CHP contact or Public Records Act request, which is the user's call.

Proposes no rule change. It only gives reasons for the existing rules (report offset beats GPS on the crossing; pile points = no GPS; empty postmile is not a quality signal).

User request 2026-10-25 (PM chat): bring in an open, nationwide address layer, like the geocoder they used in ArcMap, to place D5 crashes. D5 is ~12,650 crashes whose report gives a house address instead of a cross street.

Today's `address` tier uses OSM house numbers only. That's sparse in CA, and it scored 81.4% on SF.

## Measure only (Tester), same basis as run 10
Candidates, all free and nationwide:
1. **Census Geocoder API** (batch ≤10,000 addresses; TIGER address ranges, interpolated).
2. **TIGER/Line ADDRFEAT address ranges**, local, from the 2026 vintage we already use (no network at runtime).
3. **USDOT National Address Database (NAD)**: address points, public domain. Report its CA county coverage.
4. **OpenAddresses**: address points by county. Record each source's licence. Some forbid commercial use, so licence fit for a paid product is a gate.

For each:
- how many D5 crashes it places;
- accuracy against hidden police GPS on D5-type crashes whose GPS fits the report (within 250 ft and 400 ft, Wilson low);
- by district;
- licence.
Downloads: the user asked for this source type. Record the source, date and licence in knowledge/sources/.

title: fix(#259): freeway placement matches/beats the reference; X TO Y by cross street; connectors held; GPS kept
body:
Closes #259

**Merge after #262 (keep officer GPS) and #276 (local-street "X TO Y" placed).** This PR builds both decisions, and docs/03 records them only once those merge.

## What changed
1. **Wording.** "about 95% of tested crashes" becomes "about 9 in 10 tested crashes" (export, references.json).
2. **Mainline meeting point** (`freeway._meeting`). The street crosses the stated-direction lanes: as before, the crossings when they are one place (600 ft). The street never crosses them (the map often draws an overpass without a crossing segment): its closest approach within **300 ft**. A street meeting **either** carriageway in two places more than **3,300 ft** apart is ambiguous and is never guessed (`STRICT`, the reference's rule).
3. **Freeway reference road.** "I-5 / SR-91" meets the route where their main lanes cross. Ways carrying both route numbers are excluded, since there the routes run together.
4. **Walk.** It starts on the lanes: the midpoint of several crossings can lie between carriageways, and before this the walk never started there. The first step goes toward the compass direction; after that the walk follows the freeway round bends, as the reference's walk does. Its segments are grid-indexed for county-wide raws.
5. **"X TO Y" read by its cross street.**
   - A **local street** is placed on X's lanes from that street's crossing, as approximate like mainline (`connector_local`; user 2026-10-25, worked example 4630945).
   - **Y**: along the connector from Y. Y's stated direction ("TO I-110 S/B") picks the connector.
   - **X**: from where the connector leaves X.
   - **True connectors (X or Y) are held for review** with their suggestion (`freeway_auto_kinds` = mainline, ramp, connector_local).
6. **Officer GPS that fits the named roads is kept.** `freeway_move_gps` is removed, along with `_freeway_gps` and the `freeway_gps_moved` count. The #218 snapped-offset rule is unchanged.
7. `knowledge/methods/freeway-crashes.md` has a new #259 section with the method and the numbers below.

## Measured
This is an Engineering scratch run on the Tester's run-10 accuracy sample: 6,000 freeway crashes whose police GPS fits the report, with the GPS hidden. It uses the Tester's fixed `fwy_raw` street lookup, with the street core and the core without a leading direction word, plus alt_name. "Main" is origin/main's `freeway.py` on the same raws; it agrees with the Tester's rewritten d1_compare (4,076 placed).

| Method | Placed | Within 0.5 mi of the officer's GPS |
|---|---|---|
| Reference (`freeway_report_point`) | 4,203 | 3,971 (94.5%) |
| App, main | 4,073 | 3,783 (92.9%) |
| **App, this PR (strict, default)** | **4,285** | **4,055 (94.6%)** |
| — auto-placed (mainline, ramp, local-street "X TO Y") | 4,248 | 4,024 (94.7%) |
| — local-street "X TO Y" (now auto, user 2026-10-25) | 74 | 64 (86.5%) |
| — true connectors (held for review) | 37 | 31 (83.8%) |
| App, lenient variant (no either-carriageway ambiguity check), not used | 4,647 | 4,368 (94.0%) |

The strict variant beats the reference on crashes placed, on crashes within 0.5 mi, and on rate. The PM chose strict.

Where the remaining difference from the reference is:
- **App only:** 401 crashes, 352 within 0.5 mi. 267 of these are cases the reference calls "cross street meets the route more than once".
- **Reference only:** 319 crashes, 272 within 0.5 mi; 268 of them are mainline.

## Tests
`tests/test_freeway.py`, all written before the code.

Synthetic tests:
- a street drawn short of the lanes still meets them;
- two meetings a mile apart: not guessed;
- a street over 300 ft from the lanes doesn't meet them;
- the walk follows a bend;
- the walk starts on the lanes when the crossings' middle is between them;
- a freeway reference road;
- what a connector report is measured from.

Fixtures, cut from the local OSM extract with the Tester's raw builder:
- **4630945 Euclid**: placed approximate within 400 ft of the officer's GPS; the spot is 9 ft from it.
- **1392922 Ontario** and **1818216 Harbor**: held for review, no automatic spot.

Also tested: connectors held with their suggestion, ramps still approximate, and officer GPS never moved.

Results: full suite 521 passed, 2 skipped; ruff clean.

## Harness note
The first d1_compare under-counted the app. `fwy_raw` looked up the reference street by exact core, so it never found "South Normandie Avenue" for NORMANDIE AVE. The Tester fixed it on test/run10 (PR #260).

title: Fatal freeway crashes: a FARS point that fits the named roads must beat the approximate freeway spot
body:
Found by Tester re-measuring #278 (main f14ba36). 9 fatal freeway crashes with no usable police GPS, which FARS placed precisely in run 9C, now get the approximate freeway spot (usually within 0.5 mi) instead. Examples: 1621490, 1695836, 1747193. 12 more in the not-in-app group move the same way.

**Cause:** `place_unmatched` runs the freeway step inside the locator loop, before `place_fatal_from_fars`. The approximate placement then counts as a usable location, so FARS never runs.

**Why it's a bug, not a choice:** these rules are already decided:
- fatal crashes first (docs/03, 2026-10-21);
- FARS fills a fatal crash's missing location when its point fits both named roads (2026-10-22);
- keep a GPS point that fits the named roads (2026-10-25).

A FARS point that fits is a coordinate fix; the approximate spot is an estimate.

## Fix
- [ ] For fatal crashes, try FARS before the approximate freeway spot. Or: an approximate placement is replaced by a FARS point that fits the named roads.
- [ ] Failing test first, using one of the example records' fixtures.
- [ ] Tester confirms the 9 (+12) fatal crashes are back on FARS, and that fatal on-map is unchanged.

title: State-highway crash rates from Caltrans AADT (segments, ramps, trucks) on tab 3 and in Findings
body:
User decision 2026-10-26 ("BUILD IT"; docs/03 PR #286).

## Data: Caltrans Traffic Census Program (public)
- AADT points: ArcGIS `https://caltrans-gis.dot.ca.gov/arcgis/rest/services/CHhighway/Traffic_AADT/FeatureServer/0` (14,080 points). Fields: DISTRICT, RTE, RTE_SFX, CNTY, PM_PFX, PM, PM_SFX, DESCRIPTION, BACK_/AHEAD_ PEAK_HOUR, PEAK_MADT, AADT. Annual .xlsx 2013–2024 at https://dot.ca.gov/programs/traffic-operations/census. Check which year the GIS layer holds; per-year rates need the per-year .xlsx.
- Truck AADT: `CHhighway/Truck_Volumes_AADT/FeatureServer/0` (6,865). Fields include TOT_TRK_AADT, TRK_2/3/4/5_AXLE(_PCT), EST_YEAR, LEG.
- Ramp volumes: per-district .xlsx 2016–2024 on the same page.
- Cache by download date, as for postmiles (#254). Live data only; tests use small fixtures and no network. Source note in knowledge/sources/ca-caltrans-traffic-census.md.

## Build
- [ ] Segment AADT: for each state-route corridor, split at count points (route, county, prefix, suffix). Use the BACK leg before a point and the AHEAD leg after it. Each crash gets its segment through its derived postmile (#248). Per year: the AADT for the matching count year (Oct–Sep); 2025 uses the latest year available, labelled.
- [ ] Rates (code only): crashes per million vehicle-miles = crashes / (AADT × length mi × 365 × years) × 10^6, for fatal, fatal + injury (KSI too) and all. Ramps: crashes per million vehicles using ramp AADT. Trucks: truck-involved (3+ axle definition, docs/03) crashes / (3+ axle truck AADT × length × 365 × years) × 10^6.
- [ ] Comparisons: (2) against the corridor average and (3) year over year, now. (1) The Caltrans statewide average for the same highway type is shown **only** with a cited published table in data/reference/. Find the source (e.g. the annual "Crash Data on California State Highways" book or Caltrans rate-group tables). If it isn't public, leave that column out and open a decision-needed issue. Never type values from memory.
- [ ] Counting rule: a statewide-average comparison uses Caltrans' on-highway rule (exclude 'associated with' crashes, suicides, beat 902 where identifiable; see knowledge/sources/ca-caltrans-tasas.md), or is labelled approximate.
- [ ] Tab 3: a "Crash rates" table on state-highway corridors, plus a map marker on segments above the comparison. Every row cites the AADT year and source.
- [ ] Findings: a "rate above average" finding with every number traced to the table (validator).
- [ ] Not on state highways: no rates, with the note "local traffic counts needed".
- [ ] Tests first; no-change proof for non-SHS corridors.

## Tester first (measure only)
How many SHS crashes (2021–25) get a segment AADT through #248's postmile: by district, by route type, with ramps matched to ramp volumes. Gaps: count points missing, or postmile not derived. Report before Engineering wires the UI.

feat(#287): Caltrans AADT loader and segment join (part 1 of #287)
body:
Part of #287 (not closing it). This is the data loader and segment join the Tester measures first. Rates, the tab 3 table, map markers and findings come after that measure.

**Source:** Caltrans Traffic Census Program annual workbooks, 2021–2024 traffic volumes and truck AADT (`config/aadt.json`; public, dot.ca.gov). The user approved downloading them on 2026-10-26. The ArcGIS `Traffic_AADT` layer has no year field, so the per-year workbooks are the source. Source note: `knowledge/sources/ca-caltrans-traffic-census.md`.

**`backend/crashiq/aadt.py`:**
- **`AadtCache`:** downloads the configured years into `data/cache/aadt/caltrans_aadt_<download date>.sqlite`, with the same background, retry and refresh pattern as postmiles (#254). It reads both header styles, blanks as `''` / `' '` / None, text or numeric postmiles, and zero-padded routes.
- **`count_year(date)`:** October to September.
- **`segment(route, county, pm, year)`:**
  - It takes the count points of one line (route + suffix, county, postmile suffix) in postmile order and returns the segment around the postmile.
  - **Leg rule:** the volume changes between points (in 2024 the AHEAD of one point and the BACK of the next differ on 2,662 of 6,527 segments, by 20% or more on 943). So the crash takes the **nearer point's leg facing it**: the AHEAD of the point behind in the first half, the BACK of the point ahead in the second half. This is the issue's "BACK leg before a point, AHEAD leg after it". It returns that half (`piece`) for the rates later.
  - Route breaks are never bridged. Before the first loaded year there's nothing; after the newest year it uses the newest, `latest_used`.
  - `prefix_change` flags segments whose postmile length is approximate: 938 in 2024.
- **`truck_segment`:** truck AADT and trucks with 3 or more axles (TRK_3+4+5), from the A leg of the truck point behind.
- **`for_crash(c)`:** uses the crash's derived postmile (#248) and count year, and labels its source ("Caltrans Traffic Census Program, 2024 AADT").

**Checked on the real files** (scratch copy): 7,116 / 7,116 / 7,134 / 7,258 count points for 2021–24, built in 9 s. LA-405 at 13.5 gives Vermont→Normandie, 285,000.

**Tests** (`tests/test_aadt.py`, written first; no network):
- small .xlsx files built from rows cut from the 2021 and 2024 workbooks;
- both header styles;
- the nearer-leg rule (ORA-1 8.6 → 37,900, 9.0 → 38,800);
- route break, past the ends, no route;
- count year and latest-labelled year;
- 3+ axle trucks;
- the crash join through its postmile;
- retry after a failure.

Results: full suite 535 passed, 2 skipped. ruff clean.

**Not in this PR:** ramp volumes, rates, UI, findings, and the statewide-average table (that still needs a cited published source, or a decision-needed issue).

title: Decision needed (#287): how to assign Caltrans rate groups for the statewide-average crash rate
body:
From #287 point 5. **The published table exists and is public.** It is Caltrans, *2024 Crash Data on California State Highways*, "Basic Average Crash Rate Table" for Highways (H01–H67), Intersections (I01–I31) and Ramps (R01–R80), printed pages 83–90:
https://dot.ca.gov/-/media/dot-media/programs/research-innovation-system-information/documents/annual-collision-data/2024-crash-data-on-cshwy-book-v2-a11y.pdf

**How the table works:**
- Each group gives a base rate (crashes per million vehicle-miles, or per million vehicles for intersections and ramps), an ADT factor, and % fatal / % injury / % F+I.
- The rates are from 2015–2019 crashes and were revised in March 2022.
- The book's preface says the broad statewide tables (pp. 7–24) are "generally not refined enough for comparative purposes"; use these base rates instead.
- Its counting rule excludes crashes "associated with" (not on) the highway, suicides, and beat 902.

**The gap:** using a base rate needs each segment's **rate group**. For a highway, that means its type (conventional, expressway, divided, freeway), lanes, terrain, design speed, and rural, suburban or urban area. Caltrans keeps these in TSN, which CrashIQ doesn't have. CrashIQ knows the route and county (postmile), its AADT, and OSM's lanes and motorway/trunk tags. It doesn't reliably know terrain, design speed or area.

**Options:**
- **A. The engineer picks the rate group** for each state-highway segment, intersection and ramp in the app, from the published list. CrashIQ then computes the expected rate (base + ADT factor) and the comparison. Nothing is guessed. One setup step per study.
- **B. CrashIQ suggests a group** from OSM (lanes, freeway or not) plus Census urban areas. Terrain and design speed would be the conservative default. The suggestion is labelled "suggested", and the comparison shows only after the engineer confirms it.
- **C. No statewide comparison.** Show only the corridor average and year over year (both being built now).

Whichever option is chosen, the table goes into `data/reference/` with this citation, and the rates use Caltrans' on-highway counting rule or are labelled approximate (#287).

**Recommendation (Engineering):** A, with B's suggestion as a later convenience. A is exact, and it's how a TASAS Table B comparison is done today.

title: feat(#287): state-highway crash rates from Caltrans AADT (part 2: segment rates, corridor average, by year)
body:
Part of #287 (not closing it). This builds the user's 2026-10-26 decision (docs/03 #286) for **segments**. Ramps, trucks, the statewide comparison (#294), the map marker and the findings follow.

**Join changes** (`aadt.py`, PM decisions on #289):
- **End tolerance:** up to **0.05 mi** before a line's first count point or past its last uses that point's facing leg, labelled `aadt_end_tolerance`.
- **Breaks:** a blank AHEAD is still a route break and is never bridged.
- **Prefix changes (#287 point 1):** when a segment's two ends differ in prefix, nothing is measured across it. The crash takes the leg of the end whose prefix it shares, and the piece has no length.

**Exposure** (new `shs.py`):
- **Routes:** a corridor's route numbers come from its OSM names. With none, it isn't on the SHS and gets no Caltrans exposure; the no-rates caveat now says local traffic counts are needed.
- **Sampling:** each study segment is sampled every 0.05 mi. Each sample gets its postmile (#248), then each count year's AADT.
- **Calendar years:** a calendar year = **0.75 × its count year + 0.25 × the next**, since count years run October to September. A year after the newest file uses the newest, and the row's `count_years` says so.
- **Coverage:** a segment-year has exposure only when every sample has a count. There's no partial guess.
- **Lengths:** from the study geometry, never from postmiles, so prefix changes can't distort them.
- **Wiring:** `profile.with_shs` attaches the volumes in the profile endpoint and both exports, through `aadt_for(app.state)` (fake or recorded CKAN never downloads, as for postmiles; `CRASHIQ_AADT_DIR`).

**Rates** (`profile.shs_rate_tables`; code only):
- **T22**, per segment: crashes, fatal + injury (K, A, B, C and injury-level-unknown), fatal, length, window-average AADT, million vehicle-miles, and rates per MVM (all, F+I, fatal). Each row has the **corridor average** (all crashes over all MVM of the rated segments), the rate ÷ average, **count years** and **source**.
- **T23**: the corridor's rate **year by year**.
- The T2 rates from entered AADT are unchanged.
- **Caveat:** these count crashes as CrashIQ places them, not by Caltrans' on-highway rule, so they're not comparable with Caltrans' averages (labelled, per docs/03).

**Tab 3:** a **"State-highway crash rates"** section after the location ranking, shown only when T22 exists.
- It has the T22 table with a source mark. A segment above the corridor average is marked. Each row's tooltip shows the AADT, count years and source, and the sources and count years are also stated above the table.
- The year-by-year table (T23) sits under "By year".

title: Decision needed (#287): which crashes count in a state-highway segment crash rate
body:
From the design check of PR #296 (checked live on El Camino Real, CA 82, Burlingame). The rates currently count **segment crashes only**. On ECR that's 1 of 58 corridor crashes, and both fatal crashes were at intersections, so the corridor average reads 0.02 per MVM.

Options:
- **(a) All crashes on the corridor stretch, intersections included.** This is how Caltrans' highway rates in TASAS / the Crash Data book count crashes on a highway segment. It's also the only basis comparable with Caltrans' highway base rates (#294).
- **(b) Segment crashes for the segment rate, plus separate intersection rates** (crashes per million entering vehicles). Intersection rates need the cross street's volume, usually a local count we don't have.
- **(c) As built: segment crashes only.**

PM recommendation: **(a)**, with intersections still shown in their own tables. Until the user decides, #296 labels the rate: "segment crashes only: N of M crashes at intersections aren't in these rates".

decision-needed (#287 ramps): how a crash's ramp is identified, and where ramp rates show
body:
**Context:** #287 point 2 (PM): "show ramp rates only where the crash's ramp is identified; otherwise no ramp rate, with a note." docs/03 says ramps get "crashes per million vehicles" from Caltrans ramp ADT. The user approved the 48 ramp files (2021–24) on 2026-10-30.

**What the docs don't say:**
- What counts as "identified."
- Where ramp rates appear. Study networks have segments and intersections, not ramps.

The Tester's #292 found 3,732 ramp crashes with a Caltrans ramp row within 0.3 mi. But an interchange has several ramps there, and CCRS rarely says which one.

**Options for identification** (Engineering suggests A):
- **A. Strict report match:** the report names a ramp ("ON RAMP", "OFF RAMP", "ONR"/"OFR"), its direction of travel and the cross street, and **exactly one** Caltrans ramp row within 0.3 mi on the same route and county matches all three (direction, on/off, cross street in the description). Anything else gets no ramp rate, with a note. Conservative; coverage unknown until measured.
- **B. A plus the engineer picks:** where A finds 2+ candidates, the review list offers them and the engineer picks one (approved once, like an alias).
- **C. Geometry:** the crash's GPS lies on an OSM ramp way (motorway_link), and that ramp's freeway end matches a Caltrans ramp row by postmile and direction. Covers GPS crashes, but more complex and needs its own accuracy measure.

**Where shown** (suggested): a "Ramps" table on tab 3 for state-highway studies, with one row per identified Caltrans ramp that has crashes in the study. Each row gives:
- crashes;
- ramp ADT (the latest count at or before each crash year, labelled with its year, never a later one);
- crashes per million vehicles.

The small-number rule applies (most ramps have under 10 crashes, so mostly counts). The D7 placeholders 1001/999 count as missing.

Engineering stops on ramps until the user decides. Trucks are in #299; the #294 input waits for its ADR.

title: feat(#287): ramp crash rates (T25) from Caltrans district ramp ADT; identified ramps only (#300)
body:
Part of #287 (ramps). Implements the user's decision on #300 (2026-10-30): **B, "A + engineer picks"**, and **a Ramps table on tab 3**. The decision is recorded in docs/03 by **#301**, which should merge first.

**Stacked:** #296 → #299 (trucks) → this PR. The base is `feat/287-truck-rates`.

**What it does**
- **Ramp counts** (`aadt.py`): loads the 48 district ramp ADT workbooks (2021–2024 editions, 12 districts; the user approved the downloads 2026-10-30) into a `ramp` table.
  - Each edition carries ten years per ramp; where editions overlap, the newest wins.
  - `ramp_adt(ramp, year)` is the latest count at or before the year, with its count year, never a later one (#287 point 2).
  - A cache copy without ramps (schema 1) refreshes; the old copy keeps serving until the new one is in.
- **Placeholders (#287 point 3, wider than asked):** 1001 and 999 aren't only in D7 2021. They appear in **every district and edition** (5,650 values). Examples:
  - runs of 1001 ending in 999 on closed ramps (LA-405 "SB OFF TRUCK SCALES (CLOSED)");
  - a lone 999 between real counts (LA-405 "NB ON FROM WB RTE 105": 9,793 / 999 / 33,373);
  - D1 "SB ON FR RTE. 20": 1001 in 2016, then 500 to 6,520.
  
  No key in the files or on the census page explains them, so they count as missing everywhere. Tested on the real 999 row.
- **Which ramp** (`ramps.py`):
  - The report gives direction (from the ramp road, never a local street's own direction), on/off and cross street. Caltrans' descriptions are parsed in their several styles ("099/NB ON FR…", "NBOFF…", "NORWOOD TO WB-80").
  - **Identified** = exactly one ramp within 0.3 mi on the same route and county fits all three. "SEG" pieces and "CONN" connectors are left out.
  - **2 or more fit** → status `pick`. `identify(..., picks=)` already honours an engineer's pick. **The review-list UI to make and store the pick is the next PR.**
  - Otherwise `none`, with the reason.
- **T25** (`profile.ramp_rate_tables`), per identified ramp: crashes, fatal + injury, postmile, ramp ADT (window average), million vehicles, crashes and F+I per MV, count years used (e.g. "2021–2023 (2024, 2025 use 2023)"), crashes on picked ramps, and source. If any window year has no count at or before it, the ramp gets counts only (never a partial guess). The small-number rule applies. A scope line counts every ramp crash: "N ramp crashes: X on an identified Caltrans ramp; Y with 2 or more possible ramps (the engineer picks); Z with no ramp rate (reasons)".
- **Tab 3:** "Ramp crash rates" after the state-highway rates. Columns: ramp (name + postmile), crashes, ramp ADT, per MV, count years.

**Measured** on the Tester's 4,424 statewide ramp crashes with a derived postmile (#292 `aadt_match.csv` + the CCRS mirror, read-only):

| Outcome | Crashes |
|---|---|
| Identified | 2,094 (47%) |
| 2 or more fit (engineer picks) | 186 |
| No ramp rate | 2,144 |

Of the no-rate crashes:
- **no ramp fits: 1,137.** Mostly CHP's compass direction against Caltrans' route direction (S/B on SR-70, where Caltrans writes EB/WB), or the cross street missing from Caltrans' description;
- no ramp within 0.3 mi: 286;
- no direction in the report: 240;
- no cross street: 204;
- on/off not stated: 156;
- two or more of these: 121.

**Count age on identified crashes:**

| Age of the count used | Crashes |
|---|---|
| 0 years | 382 |
| 1–4 years | 947 |
| 5–9 years | 546 |
| 10–14 years | 121 |
| No count at or before the crash year | 98 |

No age cap is applied (none is decided); every row shows its count years. The details are in the source note, plus pain points 38 and 39.

**For the PM / user:**
- (a) Should a ramp count older than N years be dropped? Not decided; currently any age, labelled.
- (b) The compass-vs-route-direction mismatch is the biggest miss. Mapping CHP's N/S to Caltrans' E/W per route would be a method change, so it's left strict.

**Checks:**
- `tests/test_ramps.py`: real D7 rows; loader, newest edition, latest-at-or-before, placeholders, report and description parsing, identify unique / pick / pick honoured / four no-rate reasons, T25 values, small rule and scope, missing-year counts only.
- `test_shs.py` (`with_shs` identifies ramp crashes) and `Profile.test.jsx` (the Ramps table).
- pytest 587 passed; ruff, vitest (97 passed) and eslint all exit 0.
- Not checked in a browser: no state-highway study here.

title: [C6] Mainline rates count mainline crashes only: ramp wording to ramps, cross streets out (#297)
body:
## Goal
Implement the user's #297 decision: a state-highway mainline (segment) rate counts only the highway's own mainline crashes. Ramp and connector crashes move to the ramp rates (#300); cross-street and frontage-road crashes leave the rate. Today a crash whose GPS sits on the highway line is counted as mainline even when the report puts it on a ramp or a cross street, which inflates mainline rates and undercounts ramps.

## Component
C6 safety tables / rates (#287), with the C4 freeway reading (#278).

## Read first
- docs/03-requirements.md § "Which crashes count in a state-highway mainline crash rate" (#297, PR #303)
- docs/03-requirements.md § ramp identification and ramp rates (#300, PR #301), freeway method (#249/#278), N7 grade separations (#67)
- docs/04-design.md § C6

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each state-highway crash on a rate corridor gets a rate class, with the reason, from deterministic rules (docs/03 #297 entry, user 2026-10-31 / 2026-11-01):
  - `mainline`: primary road is the highway, no ramp or connector wording. On a conventional (at-grade) highway this includes crashes at its intersections, and reports with the cross street as primary and the highway second when the crash is within the 250 ft intersection influence area (user 2026-11-01, "2A");
  - `ramp`: the report names a ramp (ON/OFF RAMP, ONR/OFR); or the road reads "<route> <dir> TO <local street>" (= the <dir> off-ramp to that street, which counts as naming the ramp for #300's strict match: direction <dir>, off, cross street = that street); or a true connector "<route> TO <route>" whose cross street is one of the two routes. Direction matched strictly as written (no compass/route translation; user 2026-11-01, #308 closed). Matched per #300: exactly one Caltrans ramp row within 0.3 mi, else the engineer picks, else no ramp rate with a note;
  - "<route> TO <route>" with a **local** cross street stays `mainline` (2026-10-25);
  - `cross_street`, not in any rate: on a conventional highway, cross-street or frontage-road primary beyond the 250 ft influence area; on a freeway (access-controlled), any cross-street primary. Applies regardless of where the GPS sits;
  - `excluded`: roads over or under a freeway (N7, already built).
- [ ] Intersection rates, if shown later (I01–I31, #294), are a separate view and never added to the segment rate.
- [ ] T22/T23 mainline rates use `mainline` only; the T22 "segment crashes only" interim label is replaced by a scope line: "Mainline crashes: N. Not in this rate: R ramp crashes (see Ramps), C cross-street crashes."
- [ ] Ramp rates (T25, #302) include the `ramp` crashes moved off the mainline.
- [ ] Placement is unchanged: this changes only which rate a crash counts in, never where it sits on the map.
- [ ] Tests (synthetic fixtures only): one crash per rule above, including a "<route> TO <route>" with a local cross street staying mainline; a GPS-on-the-mainline crash with "TO <street>" wording counts as ramp; a cross-street crash with GPS on the line counts as cross_street; the T22 scope line shows the right N/R/C.
- [ ] Tester re-measures on one real freeway corridor (counts by class) and reports in the PR.

## Out of scope
- Caltrans' other TASAS exclusions (suicides, "associated with"): CCRS has no field for them.
- Intersection rates per million entering vehicles.

## Depends on
#303 (decision, docs/03), #296 (segment rates), #302 (ramp rates)

title: [C4] D3: read the wording that hides a mapped street (route suffix, approved abbreviations, 'curb line of', two streets in one field)
body:
## Goal
D3 crashes ("street missing from the map") with police GPS in the right city fail the GPS-fits check because the report's wording isn't read, not because the street is missing. Tester's D3 breakdown (2026-10-31, 3,156 D3 crashes with GPS inside the reported city or county) found about 700 where the named street is within 400 ft of the GPS under a loose match. Make the name cleaner read these forms everywhere, including the GPS-fits check (`City.fits` / coverage outcome), so these crashes place by their own GPS.

## Component
C4 locate (names.py / aliases.py, the GPS-fits check).

## Read first
- docs/03-requirements.md § "Street aliases, batch A APPROVED" (2026-10-22): abbreviations (CYN = Canyon, HW = Highway, PW/PY/PKY = Parkway, RT/RTE = Route …) and the route-suffix pattern ("PACIFIC COAST HWY - SR1") were approved to become **general name-cleaner rules in every city**. Check whether they reach the GPS-fits check; the cases below suggest they don't.
- docs/03 § keep the officer's GPS when it fits (2026-10-25).
- docs/04-design.md § C4

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each of these forms matches the right mapped street (OSM ∪ TIGER), in the GPS-fits check and in intersection matching:
  - route suffix with a dash: "BEACH BL - SR39 BLVD" = Beach Blvd (Huntington Beach writes every Beach Blvd crash this way);
  - abbreviations already approved: "SAN MIGUEL CYN RD" = San Miguel Canyon Rd, "HARBOR BAY PK" = Harbor Bay Pkwy;
  - state routes written out: "STATE HIGHWAY 96", "STATE ROUTE 127", "SH-60" = the route ref;
  - position words before the name: "W CURB LINE OF LEMON ST" = Lemon St (curb line, side of, north of …);
  - two streets in one field: "SOUTH WESTBORO AVE AND NORWICH AVE" → try each;
  - a house number glued to the street: "2038 SAN MIGUEL CYN ROAD".
- [ ] Never matched: non-street text such as "2 SOUTH GARFIELD PARKING LOT", "CITY POLE 120217634" or "- ALY". These stay where they are.
- [ ] Tests: one unit case per form (synthetic names), plus a negative case for each "never" form.
- [ ] Tester measures before switching on: how many D3 crashes move to GPS placement, and spot-checks 20 on the map. Accuracy isn't at issue (the point is the officer's GPS); the check is that the named street really is the one at the GPS.
- [ ] Re-bucket D3 on the new code (D3 was bucketed in run 9A, before TIGER; Tester found 957 of the 3,156 now find both names within 1 mi).

## Out of scope
- Spelling variants (CHESEBRA = Chesebro …): separate issue, user approves each.
- GPS that sits on some other road with neither name found: needs a user decision.

## Depends on
none

title: knowledge: statewide playbook brought up to date (2026-11-01)
[C6] Ramp direction: translate compass to route direction by the postmile line's bearing (method needs user OK)
body:
## Goal
User decision (2026-11-01, Engineering session, #302): match a crash's direction to a Caltrans ramp row by translating compass and route directions, not strictly. A CHP "S/B" on a route Caltrans signs EB/WB should match the route direction it's closest to. **The method below is Engineering's proposal and waits for the user's confirmation before it's built.**

## Proposed method
- Take the bearing of the Caltrans postmile line at the crash. Postmile increasing = NB (for N–S signed routes) or EB (for E–W signed routes).
- Pick the signed route direction within 90° of the reported compass direction.
- Exactly 90° (e.g. "N/B" reported where the line runs due east–west) stays unmatched, with the reason "direction unclear".

## Component
C6 ramps (`ramps.py`), #302.

## Read first
- docs/03 § ramp identification and ramp rates (#300); § ramp count age and direction (2026-11-01)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Deterministic, no AI. Tests with synthetic lines: N–S route, E–W route, a diagonal route, the exact-90° case.
- [ ] Each ramp crash records the translation it used (e.g. "S/B → WB, line bearing 250°").
- [ ] Tester measures how many more ramp crashes are identified, and spot-checks 20 against the map.

## Out of scope
- Mainline direction (no direction-split rates).

## Depends on
#302; user confirmation of the method

title: feat(#305): name cleaner reads the D3 wording (route tag + type word, PK, SH, position words, two streets in one field)
body:
Closes #305 (code part). The Tester's measurement and the D3 re-bucket are the issue's remaining checks, before this is switched on.

## What changes
`names.py`, used by both the GPS fit check (`crashes._names_street` → `assign._names` → `_stated_intersection` / `_dms_check` / `_pile_fits`) and intersection matching (`locate.place`):

| Form | Example | Now reads as |
|---|---|---|
| Route tag followed by a type word | `BEACH BL - SR39 BLVD` | Beach Blvd (route 39 still read by number) |
| Approved abbreviation PK | `HARBOR BAY PK` | Harbor Bay Pkwy (CYN already worked) |
| Route written out | `STATE HIGHWAY 96`, `STATE ROUTE 127`, `SH-60` | SR 96 / SR 127 / SR 60; `SH` also added to the pull's route spellings |
| Position words before the name | `W CURB LINE OF LEMON ST`, `N SIDE OF …`, `100 FT NORTH OF …` | Lemon St. `… OF THE BRIDGE` is unchanged (a landmark, not a street) |
| Two streets in one field | `SOUTH WESTBORO AVE AND NORWICH AVE` | `street_keys()` returns the whole field first, then each street; the GPS check accepts either |
| House number glued on | `2038 SAN MIGUEL CYN ROAD` | already worked; now has a test |
| Never a street | `2 SOUTH GARFIELD PARKING LOT`, `CITY POLE 120217634`, `- ALY` | no key, and the GPS check never matches them |

**Locator, two streets in one field:** tried only when the fields as written don't place, so existing placements can't change.
- If the other field is empty or names one of the two streets, the pair is those two streets.
- If the other field names a third street, each of the two is tried with it. The crash places only when exactly one pair does; otherwise it goes to review with "two streets in one field: more than one pair fits".
- "LEWIS AND CLARK DR" is tried as itself first.

**One catch I fixed:** the live Crenshaw replay lost 3 crashes such as `8451 S. CRENSHAW BOULEVARD (99 CENTS ONLY STORE/PARKING LOT)`. The never-a-street check now ignores text in brackets, and the replay is back to 1602.

## Notes for review
- **PK = Parkway** follows the approved alias rows of the abbreviation kind (Alameda, Lathrop, Stockton …). As a trailing word it could stand for "Park" somewhere. The rows found none, but the Tester's spot check should look for it.
- **The Tester's coverage harness** (`tests/statewide/coverage.py`, `fatal.road_match`) uses its own independent cleaner (`checks.indep_core`), so this PR doesn't change it. The before/after D3 count needs the Tester to run the app's placement, or to choose whether its check should read through `names.street_key`. That's the Tester's call; I haven't touched their code.
- The playbook §3 is updated (rule #307).

## Tests
- Unit tests, one case per form plus negatives: `tests/test_names.py`.
- GPS street check: `tests/test_crashes.py::test_the_gps_street_check_reads_the_d3_wording`.

title: [C4] D3 plain fixes: EXPWY the map omits, route number vs local name, address in primary → D5, same street twice → D2
body:
## Goal
From the D3 no-GPS walkthrough sample (Tester, 2026-11-01; 20 crashes, 10 fatal), some D3 crashes fail for reasons that are plain fixes, not new methods. Fix them so these crashes either place or go to the bucket whose rule already handles them.

## Component
C4 locate (names.py, the D-bucket / review reason).

## Read first
- docs/03 § street aliases batch A (abbreviations as general rules), § house-address crashes D5 (#264, #283)
- #305 / PR #310 (the same kind of cleaner fixes)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] **Type words the map leaves out:** "65TH ST EXPWY" (crash) = "65th Street" (map). When the full name doesn't match, try the name without a trailing EXPWY/EXPY/FWY/HWY type word, only when the rest is unique in the city's network.
- [ ] **Route number vs the road's local name:** "RT 1" & "HANCOCK DR" in Lompoc: match a route number to a mapped way whose `ref` carries it (OSM `ref=CA 1` / TIGER "State Rte 1") even when the way's name is a local name (e.g. "Ocean Ave", "H St").
- [ ] **House address in the primary field goes to D5:** "5101 BUSINESS CENTER DR" (number + street), and "PARKING LOT OF 3000 TRAVIS BLVD" (a lot at an address), even when the secondary field names a street. They follow the D5 rule (NAD address point, else review with the TIGER suggestion), not D3.

title: feat(#304): state-highway rates count mainline crashes only (rate class per crash: mainline, ramp, cross street)
body:
Closes #304. The Tester's re-measure on a real freeway corridor (counts by class) is the remaining check.

## What changes
**New `backend/crashiq/rate_class.py`** gives each placed crash on a state-highway rate corridor a class and the reason (docs/03 #297, #311, #312):

| Class | Rule | In which rate |
|---|---|---|
| `ramp` | names a ramp; or "<route> <dir> TO <local street>" (the <dir> off-ramp); or "<route> TO <route>" whose cross street is one of the two routes (a connector) | T25 ramp rates. A connector gets no ramp rate, with the reason "freeway connector" |
| `mainline` | the highway is the primary road ("<route> TO <route>" with a local cross street included); or, on a conventional highway, the highway is the secondary road and the crash is `at_intersection` | T22, T23, T24 |
| `cross_street` | any other primary road (a cross street, a frontage road); on a freeway, any cross-street primary | none |

- **`at_intersection(c, radius_ft)`** is one function: the distance is blank, or no more than the study's influence radius (250 ft by default). Miles are already converted to feet at parse time (`ca_ccrs`, SecondaryUnitOfMeasure "M").
- **`segment_for(intersection, segments, gps_station)`:** an intersection's mainline crashes count in the segment on their GPS side. With no GPS, or GPS within 25 ft (`STATION_TIE_FT`) of the intersection's station, they go to the segment after it; at the last intersection, to the segment before.
- **The TO wording** lives in `ramps.report()`, so the T25 ramp crashes and the `ramp` class always agree. The off-ramp reading feeds #300's strict match as direction <dir>, off, cross street = that street. Direction stays strict (#308 is withdrawn).
- **T22/T23/T24** use the mainline crashes only. T22's scope line now reads "Mainline crashes: N. Not in this rate: R ramp crashes (see Ramps), C cross-street crashes." `scope.classes` carries each crash's class and reason.
- **Placement is unchanged:** T2 is identical with and without the classes (tested). Only which rate a crash counts in changes.
- **Playbook §6** is updated (rule #307).

## Tests
- `tests/test_rate_class.py`: one case per rule, including:
  - a "<route> TO <route>" with a local cross street staying mainline;
  - blank, 0, 250 and 251 ft distances;
  - a freeway cross-street primary at 0 ft;
  - segment choice on either GPS side, at 25 ft, and at the last intersection.
- `tests/test_ramps.py`: the TO-wording off-ramp; a connector only when the cross street is a route; no dir = not a ramp; the connector's no-rate reason.
- `tests/test_shs.py`:
  - the scope line's counts (N/R/C);
  - intersection crashes at the highway counted in the segment rate (20 → 50 in S1);
  - a "TO <street>" crash whose GPS sits on the mainline counted as ramp;
  - placement unchanged.
- pytest 618 passed, 2 skipped; vitest 100; ruff and eslint clean.

Not checked in a browser: there's no state-highway study server here. The PM's review re-checks tab 3.

title: feat(#283): D5 house-address crashes at NAD address points (approximate), else review with the TIGER suggestion
body:
Closes #283 (code part). The Tester's re-measure and the 82-corridor no-change check are the remaining items.

## What changes
- **D5 routing (pull, `crashes.house_address`):** a no-GPS report counts as D5 when it gives a house number on the corridor street ("8451 S CRENSHAW BLVD", "CRENSHAW BL 24413") and the other field is blank, a placeholder, 1–2 letters, or the same street. It goes to `review_reason = "house_address"`.
  - Never D5: a route ("RT 101"), a numbered street ("AVENUE 200"), a distance ("100 FT N OF …"). Private property keeps its #94 exclusion.
- **NAD placement (`nad.py`, `placement.place_address`):**

- **Labels:**

title: feat(#319): mile-marker crashes at their Caltrans postmile (behind the postmile tier, off)
body:
Closes #319 (code part, behind a switch). The Tester's measurement and the user's switch-on decision are the remaining items. The decision text is in docs PR #317, which is still pending.

## What changes
- **Reading** (`mile_marker.marker`): "MILE MARKER 28.86", "MM", "MILEPOST", "MILE POST #95", "PM", "M/M", "MILEMARKER", and a prefix written onto the number ("R12.3"). Never "PMB 12", "SUMMIT 2" or "MILE SQUARE RD".
- **Pull** (`crashes._mile_marker_on`): a no-GPS report with a mile marker in one field and the corridor in the other gets `review_reason = "mile_marker"`. Before, it fell to "cross street not on corridor".
- **Point** (`postmile.places` / `PostmileCache.at`): the reverse of #248's lookup. For a route, county and postmile, it interpolates between the tenth points of every line (alignment, prefix, suffix) that spans the postmile.
  - Lines within 0.1 mi of each other are one place (the two sides of a divided road), and the point is their mean.
  - Lines farther apart are two places (e.g. 5.1 and R5.1) unless the report gives the prefix.
  - Counties come from `postmile.COUNTY`, CCRS codes 1–58 matched to the layer's 58 Caltrans abbreviations (all 58 checked against the local layer copy).
- **Place** (`mile_marker.place`):
  - Route: the route number the other field names, else the corridor's own route (its OSM ref, `shs.corridor_routes`, which covers "ANGELES CREST HWY" on a CA 2 corridor).
  - Offset: a stated distance moves along the route, toward whichever end lies in the stated compass direction. Under 50 ft is ignored as within the marker's precision.
  - Otherwise a reason: "no state route named", "postmile X isn't on route R in C", "… in more than one place …", "the stated … runs off …".
- **Switch:** the `postmile` tier in `config/placement.json` `auto_tiers`, **off** (its `_doc` updated). While off, the point is the review list's suggestion (`tier: postmile`, with its label, e.g. "SIS-96 PM 95.200"). When on, the crash is placed with provenance `postmile`. Counts go to `cleaning.mile_markers`.
- **Labels:** provenance "At the Caltrans postmile of the mile marker…", review reason "Mile marker on the state route…", export RULE_TEXT `mile_marker`, and a methods sentence shown only when the tier is on.
- `PULL_FORMAT` 28 → 29. Playbook and `knowledge/sources/ca-caltrans-postmiles.md` are updated.

## A first look on real data (read-only, not the Tester's measurement)
On the CCRS mirror there are 252 crashes with police GPS, mile-marker wording and a route number in their fields (123 more name no route number). The postmile lookup places 226.

| | |
|---|---|
| median distance to police GPS | 375 ft |
| within 0.1 mi | 53.5% |
| within 400 ft | 50.4% |
| within 1 mi | 87.6% |
| no point | 14 not on the route in the county, 5 two places, 7 offset off the route |

This is far from the 98% bar. As the issue suspected, CHP's mile markers are often not Caltrans postmiles: signed miles, rounded values, or the wrong county. The method is right to stay off; the Tester's measurement and the user decide.

## Tests

title: Bug: Caltrans postmile/AADT caches share one SQLite connection across threads: tab 3 requests fail (500) when sent together
body:
Found by Tester during #314's screen check (main 93b7888; same on #314 bea9346 merged with main). **Tab 3 of a state-highway study can fail to load.** The page asks for `/profile`, `/crashes` and `/assignment` at the same time, and some of those requests return 500.

**Reproduced on a live I-405 study (LA, PM 15.1–18.1, API 8001, Tester DB):** 5 rounds of 6 parallel requests (profile, crashes, assignment, each twice). Main: 2–3 of every 6 failed in every round (one 422 too). #314 merged: 2 of 6 in every round. Sequential requests all return 200.

**Cause:** `PostmileCache._db()` (postmile.py) and `AadtCache._db()` (aadt.py) open **one** read-only SQLite connection with `check_same_thread=False` and share it across FastAPI's worker threads with no lock. Concurrent cursors on it give:
- `sqlite3.InterfaceError: bad parameter or other API misuse` (aadt `_line`);
- `IndexError: tuple index out of range` (aadt `truck_segment`: a short row);
- `TypeError: NoneType - float` (postmile `nearest`: None coordinates).

These tracebacks are from the server log. Wrong answers are possible too, not just errors: the test below also gets results that differ from the single-thread answer.

## Failing test (Tester's; passes 0 of 4 runs on main)
`tests/test_cache_threads.py`: 135 errors and 144 wrong answers in a typical run.
```python
"""Tester bug: the Caltrans postmile cache shares one SQLite connection across the server's worker threads with no
lock (check_same_thread=False). Tab 3 of a state-highway study asks for the profile, the crash list and the assignment
at once; on a live I-405 study 2-3 of every 6 parallel requests fail (500: "bad parameter or other API misuse",
IndexError on a short row, None coordinates). Lookups from several threads at once must give the same answers as one
thread, with no errors."""

import threading

from test_postmile import cache, points  # noqa: F401  (the LA-405 fixture cache)


def test_postmile_lookups_from_many_threads_at_once_match_one_thread(cache):  # noqa: F811
    pts = points("405", "NB")[2:40]
    want = [cache.lookup(lat, lon, {"405"}, "N") for _, lat, lon in pts]
    errors, wrong, go = [], [], threading.Barrier(16)

    def work():
        go.wait()
        for _ in range(40):
            for (_, lat, lon), w in zip(pts, want):
                try:
                    if cache.lookup(lat, lon, {"405"}, "N") != w:
                        wrong.append((lat, lon))
                except Exception as e:      # noqa: BLE001  (any error is the bug)
                    errors.append(repr(e))

    ts = [threading.Thread(target=work) for _ in range(16)]
    for t in ts:
        t.start()
    for t in ts:
        t.join()
    assert not errors and not wrong, f"{len(errors)} errors, {len(wrong)} wrong answers; first: {errors[:2]}"
```
The same test is needed for `AadtCache` (`segment`/`truck_segment`/ramp lookups). The server traces show it fails the same way.

## Fix
- [ ] A connection per thread (e.g. `threading.local`), or a lock around every query on the shared connection, in both caches. Check any other cache with the same `check_same_thread=False` pattern.
- [ ] The test above, plus the AADT one, pass reliably.
- [ ] Tester re-runs the parallel-request check and #314's tab 3 screen check.

Closes #318 (code part, behind switches). The Tester's measurement, the 20-crash spot check and the user's decisions are the remaining items: switching on, precise vs approximate, and the bike-only path.

## What changes
- **Crossing features** (`network.crossing_query`): OSM `railway=rail|light_rail|tram|subway` and `highway=cycleway|path|footway` with a `name`, fetched across the corridor (whole ways, so a path can be walked past the query radius). They're kept apart from the street graph and never become streets. `fetch_overpass(..., allow_empty=True)` lets "no railway here" be an answer rather than a retried failure.
- **Reading** (`crossings.read`):
  - Railway: "RAIL ROAD", "RAILROAD", "RR TRACKS", "UPRR", "BNSF", "METROLINK", "TRAIN TRACKS"…, matching any railway.
  - Path: "<name> TRL / TRAIL / BIKE PATH / BIKEWAY / GREENWAY…", matched by name ("PACIFIC ELECTRIC TRL" = OSM "Pacific Electric Trail").
  - **A bike lane on the road is the road:** "BIKE LANE" joins `names.NOISE`, so "MAIN ST BIKE LANE" = Main St.
- **Pull:** a no-GPS report naming the corridor and a crossing feature that isn't one of the corridor's intersections gets `review_reason = "crossing"`. Before, it was excluded as `cross_street_not_on_corridor`. A trail-named *street* that is a study intersection never reaches this branch.
- **Place** (`crossings.place`):
  - Finds where the corridor line crosses the matched features. Points within 150 ft are one crossing (double track, a divided road).
  - **Exactly one crossing** → that spot.
  - **Two or more → review** ("the corridor crosses the Creek path in 2 places"), never the nearest. **None → review** ("doesn't cross … on the map").
  - **A stated distance** is walked along the path from the crossing, toward whichever end lies within 60° of the stated compass direction. Otherwise review, with the reason.
- **Switches:**
  - Tiers `crossing_rail` / `crossing_path`, not in `auto_tiers`: **off**. While off, the spot is the review list's suggestion.
  - **Bike-only path, pending the user:** a crash *on* a separate path (the path is the report's primary road) stays a suggestion even with the tier on, until `crossing_on_path` is set to true.
  - Counts go to `cleaning.crossings`.
- **Labels:** provenance "Where the corridor crosses the railway / trail or path…", review reason "At a railway, trail or path…", export RULE_TEXT `crossing`, and a methods sentence shown only when a tier is on.
- `PULL_FORMAT` 29 → 30. The playbook is updated.

## Tests
- `tests/test_crossings.py`, 15 synthetic cases:
  - reading railways and paths; streets and bike lanes aren't features;
  - one rail crossing; a named path by name, and an unknown name says why;
  - two crossings → review; a double track = one crossing;
  - 817 ft W walked along the trail (±1%), and N doesn't follow it;
  - off → suggestion; on → placed; on, but a crash on the bike-only path stays a suggestion;
  - off by default.
- The live Crenshaw replay is unchanged (1,597 crashes, no field changed).
- pytest 628 passed, 2 skipped; vitest 110; ruff and eslint clean.

## Note for the Tester
The statewide harness reads streets from the local OSM extract (`tests/statewide/osm_extract.py`), which keeps highway roads only. Measuring this needs railways and named paths in that extract, or live Overpass for the crossing query.

title: fix(#323): one SQLite connection per thread in the postmile and AADT caches
body:
Closes #323.

**Cause:** `PostmileCache._db()` and `AadtCache.db()` shared one read-only connection, opened with `check_same_thread=False`, across FastAPI's worker threads with no lock. Concurrent cursors on it gave "bad parameter or other API misuse", short rows and None values, and wrong answers too.

**Fix:**
- Both caches keep one read-only connection **per thread** (`threading.local`), reopened when a newer copy appears. The files are read-only, so this is cheap and needs no lock.
- `FakeCkan` (fixtures and screen tests) shares one in-memory connection, so it now takes a lock around each query. It failed the same test.
- The app `Database` already holds an RLock around every query. `tiger_files` and `ccrs_files` open a connection per call. Neither is affected.
- **NAD index (PR #315, not merged yet):** it has the same shared-connection pattern (a lock around the build only, not around queries). I'm fixing it on that branch the same way.

**Tests:** `tests/test_cache_threads.py` runs 16 threads × 40 rounds against the single-thread answers:
- the Tester's postmile test;
- the same for AADT (`segment`, `truck_segment`, the years query `shs.py` runs through `db()`);
- FakeCkan.

All three failed on main (for example 485 errors and 439 wrong answers for postmiles) and pass 5 of 5 runs here. pytest 631 passed, 2 skipped; ruff clean.

**For the Tester:** please re-run the 6-parallel-request check and #314's tab 3 screen check.

title: fix(#325): a freeway corridor's names come from its motorway ways only
body:

**Cause:** `network.detect` took every way running along the drawn line, within 80 ft and parallel, as a corridor way, and took its names as corridor names. On I-405, Freeman Ave, the frontage street about 60 ft away, qualified. Its nodes became corridor nodes, so its T-junctions with 164th and 165th St became study intersections, with a 0.07 mi segment between them.

**Fix:** when the corridor's main class is `motorway`, only the motorway ways stay corridor ways, and only their names are corridor names. A frontage or parallel surface street beside a freeway never names the corridor, and its side streets never make intersections. Arterials are unchanged: every parallel piece of their own street, such as a divided half, still counts.

**Existing studies:** a saved corridor keeps the names and intersections it was saved with, because the engineer may have edited those intersections. The fix applies when the corridor is drawn again; for the Tester's I-405 study, redraw it or draw a new study.

title: Bug: on a freeway corridor with no at-grade intersections, no-GPS crashes at far-off cross streets go to review instead of being excluded (after #327)
body:
Found by Tester re-verifying #325 on main f1f8119 (#327 merged). Live I-405 study, LA PM 15.1–18.1 (Crenshaw Blvd to Hawthorne Blvd), redrawn on the same line.

**What changed:** **17 no-GPS crashes now land on the review list.** Before #327 they were excluded as `cross_street_not_on_corridor`. Their cross streets are miles off the study stretch: Victory Blvd, Ventura Blvd, Mulholland Hwy, Moraga Dr, Sepulveda Blvd (SR-118), Centinela Ave, Constitution Ave, Normandie Ave, I-110, Imperial Hwy, Rosecrans Ave, US-101. Examples:
- `I-405 N/B (SAN DIEGO FWY) | VICTORY BLVD` (2364095);
- `I405 N/B | CENTINELA AVE` (2305398);
- `I-405 S/B | I-110` (2360673).

**Cause:** `crashes.no_gps` (crashes.py ~line 692) excludes a side street only when `cross_keys` (the corridor's intersections) is non-empty: `elif cross_keys and not at_crossing and not any(...)`. #327 correctly leaves a freeway corridor with **no** at-grade intersections, so `cross_keys` is empty and nothing is ever excluded. Every no-GPS report naming the freeway plus any cross street goes to review. The corridor's grade separations (11 here: Crenshaw, 182nd St, Artesia, Redondo Beach, Hawthorne, Manhattan Beach…) are known (`gs_keys`) but are used only for `at_crossing`.

**Expected:** on a freeway corridor, a no-GPS crash whose cross street is neither a grade separation nor an interchange street of the corridor is excluded as off the study stretch, as it was when the corridor had (bogus) intersections. The user sees only crashes that may be on the stretch.

## Failing test (to write first)
Synthetic motorway corridor with no intersections and two grade-separated crossings (A St over, B St under). Three no-GPS crashes:
- "I-405 N/B | A ST" → not excluded (at a crossing);
- "I-405 N/B | Z AVE" (not a crossing) → `exclude_rule == "cross_street_not_on_corridor"`. Today it goes to review;
- "I-405 N/B | NOT STATED" → review `no_cross_street` (unchanged).

## Fix
- [ ] On a freeway corridor, the known crossings for this check are the grade separations (and the interchange streets of its ramps). Exclude any other cross street.
- [ ] Tester re-runs the I-405 study: the 17 are excluded again, and nothing else changes.

title: Bug: freeway corridor buffer is measured from the drawn line only, so far-carriageway crashes are excluded (174 I-405 mainline crashes outside 100 ft)
body:
Found by Tester re-verifying #325 on main f1f8119. Live I-405 study, LA PM 15.1–18.1 (Crenshaw Blvd to Hawthorne Blvd), 2.98 mi, buffer 100 ft (the default), 2021–2025.

## The bug
The corridor buffer is measured from the **drawn line** only. On a divided freeway the two carriageways sit apart from any one line, so crashes on the freeway itself fall outside the 100 ft buffer and are excluded as `outside_buffer`.

**Evidence: 281 crashes excluded as `outside_buffer`; 174 of them are worded as I-405 mainline** (primary road is I-405, no ramp word, no TO/FROM). Their distance from the drawn line:

| From the drawn line | Crashes |
|---|---|
| 100–150 ft | 101 |
| 150–200 ft | 37 |
| 200–300 ft | 32 |
| 300+ ft (max 392) | 4 |

Median 141 ft. **Measured from the corridor's own motorway ways** (every OSM `highway=motorway` way with ref I 405 in the study box, both directions: 89 ways): **161 of the 174 are within 100 ft, median 17 ft**. The other 13 are 100–316 ft from any I-405 way.

**What a both-carriageway buffer (100 ft from any I-405 motorway way) would also bring in,** among the 281:
- 11 crashes with I-405 ramp/TO wording (`I-405 N/B TO ARTESIA BLVD.` etc.). #314 rates these as ramps, not mainline;
- 2 crashes on other road wording. Both are I-405 spelled another way: `405 SB | ARTESIA BOULEVARD` (40 ft) and `NORTHBOUND INTERSTATE 405 (SAN DIEGO FREEWAY) | YUKON AVENUE` (22 ft);
- **0 crashes on another route** in this study.

Earlier, 37 of these crashes were counted only because they were within 250 ft of the bogus Freeman Ave intersections (#325). #327 removed those intersections, so they dropped out, and that's how this came to light.

## Expected (PM, 2026-11-01)
On a freeway corridor, the buffer is measured from every motorway way of the corridor's route, both directions, keeping the user's buffer width. Study limits still apply, unchanged.

## Failing test (to write first)
Two parallel motorway ways with the same ref (e.g. `I 405`, one northbound and one southbound, about 160 ft apart). The corridor is drawn on one of them. A crash 150 ft from the drawn way and 10 ft from the other → **in the corridor** (not `outside_buffer`). A crash 150 ft from both → `outside_buffer` as now.

## Fix
- [ ] Freeway corridors: buffer distance = the minimum over the corridor route's motorway ways (both carriageways), within the study limits.
- [ ] Tester re-runs the I-405 study: about 161 crashes are back in the corridor, 0 other-route crashes come in, and nothing else changes.

title: fix(#328, #329): freeway corridors: off-stretch cross streets excluded with no intersections; buffer from both carriageways
body:
Closes #328. Closes #329.

## #328: off-stretch cross streets on a freeway with no intersections
`crashes.no_gps` excluded a side street only when the corridor had study intersections (`cross_keys`). Since #327, a freeway corridor correctly has none, so every no-GPS report naming the freeway plus any cross street, even miles away (Victory Blvd, Centinela Ave, I-110…), went to review. On a freeway (`is_freeway`) with grade separations, those separations are now the known crossings:
- a report naming one of them stays (`at_crossing`, as before);
- any other cross street is excluded as `cross_street_not_on_corridor`, as it was when the corridor had (bogus) intersections;
- "no cross street" reviews are unchanged.

Interchange streets are grade separations in OSM (the road over or under the freeway), so they're covered.

## #329: the freeway buffer is measured from both carriageways
On a freeway corridor the pull now fetches the motorway ways within 150 m of the drawn line (`network.carriageway_query`, Overpass, cached like the rest) and keeps those whose `ref` carries the corridor's route number (`network.carriageways`), both directions. It stores them as `pull["carriageways"]`. `assign` measures the buffer distance as the minimum over the drawn line and those carriageways; the user's buffer width is unchanged.
- **Unchanged:** station, and so the study limits and the segment, still come from the drawn line.
- **Other routes:** a motorway way with another route's ref (I-110 next to I-405) never counts.
- **Old pulls:** `PULL_FORMAT` 30 → 31, so existing pulls refetch and get the carriageways.

## Tests
- `test_crashes::test_a_freeway_with_no_intersections_excludes_cross_streets_that_are_not_its_crossings` (failed before the fix): by a crossing stays; Marine, not a crossing, is excluded; on the crossing road it's `grade_separated_crossing`; no-cross-street reviews are untouched.
- `test_grade_separations::test_a_freeway_buffer_is_measured_from_both_carriageways` (failed before the fix): two I 405 ways about 160 ft apart, and an I 110 way that's ignored. A crash 150 ft from the drawn line and about 10 ft from the far carriageway is a segment crash; a crash 150 ft from both is outside the buffer. Without carriageways, as before.
- pytest 664 passed, 2 skipped; ruff clean.

## Also
The playbook §4 gets the PM's standing rule: "No-change proofs run every corridor in tests/statewide/corridors_frozen.json; report every crash whose placement or assignment changes." There's also a freeway-corridor line.

**For the Tester:** re-run the I-405 study (redrawn, re-pulled). Expected: the 17 far cross streets are excluded again; about 161 far-carriageway mainline crashes are back in; no other-route crashes come in.

title: [C2] Detect roundabout and yield control at intersections (now 'unknown')

## Goal
Network detection only finds signal, stop or unknown control. Roundabouts and yield-controlled intersections come out as "unknown", so the crash-cost ranking (#273/#336) prices their fatal and serious crashes at the signalized price and marks them "control unknown". Detect them so they get the non-signalized price, and so the diagram, spine export and corridor screen show the right control.

## Component
C2 network (intersection control).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Roundabout: OSM `junction=roundabout` (or `junction=circular`) on a way through or around the node, or a mini-roundabout node (`highway=mini_roundabout`) → `roundabout`.
- [ ] Yield: `highway=give_way` on the node, or on an approach within ~30 m tagged for that intersection → `yield`.
- [ ] All-way stop: keep the existing `stop=all` handling if present.
- [ ] Unknown stays unknown when no tag is found (never guessed).
- [ ] Tests on synthetic OSM; the existing signal/stop tests are unchanged.

title: fix(#334): bare route spellings in freeway reports read as the corridor's route
body:

**What changes:**

A "1-" before an interstate number is a typo for "I-": "1-15 S/B" = 15, using the list of California interstates.
- **Never:** a house number ("405 MAIN ST"), a numbered street ("5TH ST", "405TH ST", "405 SBD AVE"), a number alone ("405"), "1-" before a non-interstate number ("1-23 S/B"), or 4 digits.
- **Gate:** it's read only against the **corridor's own route**:
  - the corridor street check (`crashes._names_street`, so assignment's GPS check and the pull);
  - mainline in `rate_class`.

**Tests:**
- each positive form;
- the never forms;
- the corridor check accepts "405 SB" and rejects "110 SB";
- `rate_class`: "405 SB" is mainline, "110 SB" a cross street.

title: feat(#337): detect roundabout and yield control at intersections
body:
Closes #337 (code part; the no-change run on corridors_frozen.json is the Tester's).

**Detection** (`network.detect`, step 5), in this order, from OSM tags near the intersection:
- signal (unchanged);
- **roundabout:** a `junction=roundabout` or `circular` way through the intersection's nodes, or a ring or `highway=mini_roundabout` node within 60 ft (`RING_FT`);
- stop (unchanged);
- otherwise **unknown**, never guessed.

There's no existing `stop=all` handling to keep: all-way stops come out as stop.

**Yield is not detected (PM, under the 2026-11-02 freeze).** The first version set yield from any `highway=give_way` node within 100 ft. The Tester's frozen-corridor run found 6 of 6 of those were wrong: crosswalk yield lines on the corridor itself, or slip lanes (`*_link`). So a give_way sign is no longer read, and those intersections stay `unknown`, as on main. The Tester's narrower rule (cross-street way only, not `*_link`, within 30 m, not next to a `highway=crossing`) is parked as backlog issue #368 with the 6 cases.

**Where it shows:**

title: feat(#274): a finding for every fatal crash, and the KSI over-representation test
body:
Closes #274.

## (a) KSI test
The screen already tests the KSI share (target `ksi`, "Fatal and serious-injury crashes", since #42), with the same method and #34 thresholds as every other type. It writes a T12 row and a finding like the others. Added the acceptance test: a location with 4 of 8 KSI against lower-share intersections gets the `ksi` signal and its T12 row (4, 8).

## (b) A finding for every fatal crash
`findings.fatal_findings` writes one finding per fatal crash placed at a study location, by code with no statistical test:
- **Text:** "Fatal crash at <T2 label> on <date>: <collision type>, primary collision factor "<PCF>" (<category>), involving <road users> | vehicles only." An approximate placement (freeway report or NAD address point) adds "Approximate location: no usable GPS, placed from the report." Those placements are never at an intersection, so they never reach a collision diagram (#255).
- **Citation:** the crash record through a new `RecordFilter.crash_id` (with its location), and the location's T2 row (`T2 <loc>/fatal_crashes`).
- **Identity:** id `fatal-<Collision Id>`, `source: screen`, `meta.kind_of_finding = "fatal"`. `run_screen` refreshes and prunes them like the `c7-` findings, keeping the accept or reject status while the text is unchanged.
- **Order:** they sort first in the findings list (`_order`), ahead of the #267 order.

## Validator
- A date written in a finding's text (`YYYY-MM-DD`) must be the date of one of its evidence records; otherwise the finding is rejected with "date X in the text is not the date of a cited crash record".
- Numbers inside the date were already ignored (year in the window, digits after "-"). The PCF code is quoted, so it's checked against the record's own field.

## Screen
A fatal finding's detail says no test is run (and whether the location is approximate) and hides the pattern-library block. Its audit reads "Test: None: every fatal crash is listed" and "Written by: Code, from the crash record and table T2 (no AI)". The card's "Fatal crash" chip already came from `rank.fatal_crashes`.

title: [bug] Live crash pull from the screen deadlocks: post_pull holds _LOCKS_GUARD while ckan_for → files_for takes it again
body:
## Bug
A crash pull started from the screen against **live data.ca.gov** never starts: the job sits at `step: "Starting"` forever, with 0% CPU and no network. Found by PM running main (1a53981) end to end on El Camino Real, Burlingame; reproduced 3 times across server restarts.

## Cause (thread dump, PYTHONFAULTHANDLER + SIGABRT)
`post_pull` (crashes.py ~1174) holds `_LOCKS_GUARD` (a plain `threading.Lock`) while it builds the thread's arguments, and `ckan_for(request)` → `files_for(st)` (~1129) and `tiger_for(st)` take `with _LOCKS_GUARD:` again. A non-reentrant lock taken twice by the same thread **deadlocks the request thread**. The background thread is never even started.

```
Thread (request):
  crashes.py:1129 in files_for      ← waits on _LOCKS_GUARD
  crashes.py:1096 in ckan_for
  crashes.py:1179 in post_pull      ← already holds _LOCKS_GUARD
```

It never shows in tests, fixtures or Tester's harness because with `app.state.ckan` set (fake or recorded CKAN), `files_for`/`tiger_for` return before the lock. Only the live path deadlocks.

## Fix
Build `ckan_for(request)` (and `overpass`) **before** entering `with _LOCKS_GUARD:` in `post_pull`, or give the caches their own lock. Check every other `with _LOCKS_GUARD:` caller for the same nesting (`study_lock`, `tiger_for`, `files_for`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A failing test first: a live-style app (no `app.state.ckan`, a stub transport injected another way) calls `POST /crashes/pull?background=true` and must return 202 within 2 s, with the job leaving "Starting".
- [ ] The fix; the test passes.
- [ ] A live smoke test: one real corridor pull through the API completes.

title: [bug] Default window 2020–2024 silently drops every state-highway rate (AADT starts 2021); caveat says 'no AADT entered'
body:
## Bug (PM end-to-end run, main 1a53981, El Camino Real SR-82 Burlingame)
The app's **default window is "Last 5 years (2020–2024)"**, but the Caltrans AADT cache holds count years 2021–2024. `shs.segment_volumes` gives a segment-year no AADT when the year is before the oldest count year (2020 → None), and a segment needs every window year, so **no state-highway segment gets a rate on the default window**. The caveat then says "Crash rates were not computed (no AADT entered)", which is wrong.

Measured: on 2020–2024, by_year = {2020: None, 2021: 22,125, …}, so no T22. On 2021–2024, T22/T23/T24 appear (corridor average 1.29 per MVM).

## Fix (code)
- [ ] The caveat says the real reason: "Caltrans traffic counts start in 2021; window years before that (2020) have no count, so state-highway rates need a window from 2021 on", naming the missing years.
- [ ] Failing test first.

## Needs a user decision (PM asks)
Which fix for the data gap: (a) load the 2020 (and earlier) Traffic Census workbooks (a download, user OK needed); (b) use the oldest count year for earlier window years, labelled like "later count years use 2024"; (c) change the default window to 2021–2025 once 2025 CCRS is complete. Until then, the caveat fix alone.
