title: Crashes reported at a signalized driveway (#420) aren't placed: 75 left unmatched
body:
**Found by:** Tester, in the frozen-corridor check of #420 (head c2d0517, base main ab22045).

## What happens
#420 makes a driveway that meets the corridor at a traffic signal a study intersection, named after the driveway. A crash whose report names that driveway as its cross street ("PACIFIC COAST HWY / DOHENY PARK PLZ") is no longer excluded as `cross_street_not_on_corridor`, which is right. But it isn't placed either. The street-name locator (`placement.place_unmatched` → `locate.place`) works on the street network from `overpass_query`, and that has no `service` ways, so it can't find the driveway's name. The crash stays `unmatched`, with no review reason and no suggestion: it's counted in no location and reaches the engineer only as part of the unmatched count.

On the frozen corridors, **84 crashes** stop being excluded. **9** are placed: 7 in Victorville (BEAR VALLEY RD / MARIPOSA RD) and 2 in Encinitas (VILLAGE SQUARE DR), streets the street network also has. **75 stay unmatched** (30 O, 24 C, 20 B, 1 A), in 9 corridors:

| Corridor | Crashes | Report's cross street |
|---|---|---|
| Signal Hill | 26 | TOWN CENTER (13), TOWN CENTER WEST (8), TOWN CENTER DR (2), WILLOW (2), TOWN CENTER EAST (1) |
| Dana Point | 23 | DOHENY PARK PLZ / PLAZA (16), DOHENY PARK RD (4), the corridor named second (3) |
| San Jacinto | 8 | VILLAGE AT / OF SAN JACINTO |
| Aliso Viejo | 6 | PARK PLZ / PARK PLAZA |
| Laguna Niguel | 4 | COMMUNITY PARK (DR) |
| Redlands | 3 | CITRUS AV |
| Wildomar | 3 | OAK CREEK MALL |
| Inglewood, Westminster | 1 each | HP CASINO DRIVE, COMMERCE LN |

The crashes with GPS move to the new intersections as expected. This is only the crashes that need the locator.

Not checked: whether "CITRUS AV" (Redlands) and "WILLOW" (Signal Hill) really are the driveways ("Citrus Plaza", and the driveway at Willow) or other streets whose names match one of their words.

## Failing test (`tests/test_tester_bug420_unplaced.py`, uses `test_driveways.py`'s network)
```python
"""Tester (on #420, head c2d0517): a crash reported at a signalized driveway that #420 makes a study intersection isn't
placed there. The pull no longer excludes it (its cross street now names a study intersection), but the street-name
locator works on the street network (overpass_query), which has no `service` ways, so the crash stays `unmatched`.
Frozen run: 75 crashes in 10 corridors (Dana Point "PCH / DOHENY PARK PLZ" 15+, Signal Hill "TOWN CENTER" 23, ...)."""

from crashiq import network, placement

from test_driveways import LINE, MAIN, drive


def test_a_crash_at_a_named_signalized_driveway_is_placed_at_it():
    found = network.detect(MAIN, LINE, driveways=drive("Corte Madera Town Center"))
    net = {"line": LINE, **found, "intersections": [{**i, "is_study": True} for i in found["intersections"]]}
    at = next(i for i in net["intersections"] if i["name"] == "Corte Madera Town Center")
    crash = {"crash_id": "1", "primary_road": "MAIN ST", "secondary_road": "CORTE MADERA TOWN CENTER", "offset_ft": 0,
             "offset_dir": None, "location_source": "unmatched", "lat": None, "lon": None, "severity": "C",
             "killed": 0, "year": 2024}
    control = {**crash, "crash_id": "2", "secondary_road": "1ST ST"}      # a street the locator does know
    result = {"crashes": [crash, control], "cleaning": {}}
    placement.place_unmatched(None, net, result, raw=MAIN)
    assert control["location_source"] == "exact"
    assert crash["location_source"] != "unmatched", crash          # c2d0517: still unmatched
    assert abs(crash["lat"] - at["lat"]) < 0.0005 and abs(crash["lon"] - at["lon"]) < 0.0005
```
On c2d0517 it fails at the first assert: the crash stays `unmatched`. The control crash at 1ST ST is placed `exact`, so the setup itself works.

Frozen-run evidence (Tester folder): `m359/pd420.json` (per crash), `m359/int420.json`.

title: An unnamed signalized driveway (#420) merges neighbouring intersections: 14 pairs, a signal and 7th St lost
body:
**Found by:** Tester, in the frozen-corridor check of #420 (head c2d0517, base main ab22045).

## What happens
Step 4 of `network.detect` (cluster along the line) puts a node onto the previous cluster when it's within `CLUSTER_FT` (150 ft) and "same street". A node with **no cross-street name counts as the same street as anything** (`same_street = not a or not b or ...`). #420 adds the driveway node at each signal as a candidate. An unnamed driveway node within 150 ft of the intersections on both sides therefore chains them into one intersection, even when they're more than 150 ft apart and were two intersections before. The merged one takes the first intersection's name, and its control comes from all its nodes.

On the frozen corridors **14 pairs of intersections merge into one**. In each pair the two had different controls, and only one survives:

| Corridor | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Hayward | Unnamed road **signal** (st 2,704) + Jefferson St stop (st 2,892) | Jefferson St **stop**, 4 legs: the signal is gone |
| Buena Park | Auto Center Dr signal (1,601) + **7th St** stop (1,971), 370 ft apart | Auto Center Dr only: 7th St is gone |
| Long Beach | E Wardlow Rd signal (4,821) + Unnamed road stop (5,177), 356 ft apart | E Wardlow Rd signal |
| Burbank, Jurupa Valley, Solana Beach, Compton, Lemon Grove, La Puente, Moraga, Hawaiian Gardens | a signal + an Unnamed road (unknown control) 157–282 ft away | the signal only |
| Albany, Cudahy, Newport Beach | the same cross street twice, 160–226 ft apart (signal + stop/unknown) | one signal, 4 legs |

The last row is offset T intersections of one cross street, where one intersection may be the better answer. The others are separate streets.

In Compton, La Puente, Lemon Grove and Jurupa Valley, the Unnamed road that disappears was the intersection at B. The study's end moves with it: crashes there are now `outside_study_limits` (Compton +4, La Puente +4, Lemon Grove +1; Jurupa Valley 0).

## Failing test (`tests/test_tester_bug420_merge.py`)
```python
"""Tester (on #420, head c2d0517): an unnamed signalized driveway chains two separate intersections into one.
Frozen run: 14 pairs merged, e.g. Hayward (a signal 188 ft from Jefferson St becomes part of the stop-controlled
Jefferson St), Long Beach (a stop 356 ft past E Wardlow Rd), Albany (Washington Av signal + stop 183 ft apart).
Step 4 of detect clusters a node with no cross-street name onto any neighbour within CLUSTER_FT, so a driveway node at
the signal bridges the gap. Where the second intersection was at A or B, the study's end moves (Compton, La Puente)."""

from crashiq import network

from test_driveways import LINE


_FT = 1 / 364000            # degrees of latitude per foot, near 34° N


def _n(i, lat, lon, **tags):
    return {"type": "node", "id": i, "lat": lat, "lon": lon, **({"tags": tags} if tags else {})}


def test_an_unnamed_driveway_at_a_signal_does_not_merge_its_neighbours():
    s, u, d = 34.010, 34.010 + 240 * _FT, 34.010 + 110 * _FT     # Oak St signal; an unnamed street 240 ft on; driveway
    osm = {"elements": [_n(1, 34.000, -118.300), _n(3, s, -118.300, highway="traffic_signals"), _n(40, d, -118.300),
                        _n(41, u, -118.300), _n(5, 34.020, -118.300),
                        _n(6, 34.000, -118.310), _n(7, 34.000, -118.290), _n(8, 34.020, -118.310), _n(9, 34.020, -118.290),
                        _n(60, s, -118.302), _n(61, s, -118.298), _n(62, u, -118.302), _n(63, u, -118.298),
                        {"type": "way", "id": 10, "nodes": [1, 3, 40, 41, 5], "tags": {"highway": "primary", "name": "Main Street"}},
                        {"type": "way", "id": 11, "nodes": [6, 1, 7], "tags": {"highway": "residential", "name": "1st Street"}},
                        {"type": "way", "id": 12, "nodes": [8, 5, 9], "tags": {"highway": "residential", "name": "9th Street"}},
                        {"type": "way", "id": 13, "nodes": [60, 3, 61], "tags": {"highway": "residential", "name": "Oak Street"}},
                        {"type": "way", "id": 14, "nodes": [62, 41, 63], "tags": {"highway": "residential"}}]}
    drive = {"elements": [_n(40, d, -118.300), _n(70, d, -118.302),
                          {"type": "way", "id": 30, "nodes": [40, 70], "tags": {"highway": "service"}}]}
    before = [i["name"] for i in network.detect(osm, LINE)["intersections"]]
    assert before == ["1st Street", "Oak Street", "Unnamed road", "9th Street"]
    after = [i["name"] for i in network.detect(osm, LINE, driveways=drive)["intersections"]]
    assert "Unnamed road" in after, after               # c2d0517: merged into "Oak Street"
```
On c2d0517 the "before" assert passes and the last one fails: `['1st Street', 'Oak Street', '9th Street']`.

Evidence (Tester folder): `m359/int420_changes.csv` (every intersection that changed, matched by shared OSM node), `scripts/int420.py`.

body:
Written by Hermes (user 2026-11-07: start the other states; then: state picker first, per-state methods as cited data). Engineering, please review.

Docs only: `docs/state-pack-design.md`, the design for #19 (state pack). No code changes.

- **Inventory:** 36 California assumptions with file:line (CCRS columns, KABCO map, CCRS county code → FIPS `2n-1`, CA bounds, CHP placeholders, "CA" route prefix, Caltrans postmiles/AADT/rate groups/LRSM costs, CVC PCF table, reference files, export/profile wording).
- **Seam:** a `StatePack` dataclass and a `PACKS` registry in a new `packs.py`; `study.state` (default CA); one dispatch at `crashes.ensure()` (line 1117). CA keeps today's `pull()`, and any other state goes through `pull_reader()` → `reader.fetch()` → the same shared cleaning. `packs.get()` has no default, so nothing falls back to CA.
- **Reader contract:** what the `sources/<st>_<source>.py` readers should return: CCRS-shaped crash dicts with `severity`, `county_fips`, `state`, `is_freeway` and the mode flags already set.
- **State picker (new):** migration 16 `study.state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'CA'` (existing studies = CA); fixed after creation (not in `StudyPatch`). Setup gets a first "State" dropdown from `/studies/meta?state=`: ready states enabled, researched ones greyed "(coming)". A line outside `pack.bounds` is refused at `put_corridor`; a border corridor is kept, with a caveat naming the other state and its share (Overpass admin level 4, already queried at levels 6/8).
- **Methods (new):** inventory M1-M16 of hard-coded Caltrans methods (LRSM costs, TASAS rate groups, critical-rate K, Traffic Census AADT, LRSM 3-year rule, ...). `methods_<st>.json`: every value cites manual + edition + page or says `missing`; a manual's jurisdiction must be the state or US, so a non-CA pack citing Caltrans fails to load. Missing/unverified values drop their table and show a caveat plus a "State methods and sources" block; never CA's numbers. Tonight's `<st>-summary.json` `methods` keys convert verbatim into drafts marked `verified: false`.
- **Migration:** 8 steps plus 2b (picker), 2c (corridor outside the state), 4b (CA methods file), 9 (research drafts), written as draft issues (not filed). Each keeps the suite (955 tests) and the Tester's CA statewide numbers green.

#19 is still parked (2026-11-02), so building any step needs the PM to reopen it.

title: state(DC): sources, placement sample, importer
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-07: start the other states). Engineering, please review.

## Washington DC: bucket A* (open, CC BY 4.0, 100% located; KABCO B/C merged)

**Source:** DDOT "Crashes in DC" (MapServer/24, 356,985 crashes) + "Crash Details" (MapServer/25, 906,895 persons), linked by `CRIMEID`. Open ArcGIS REST, nightly, newest crash 2026-11-05. The licence is **CC BY 4.0** on both items (the earlier screen said CC0, now corrected): paid use is OK with attribution.

**Catch:** severity is fatal / major / minor. K and A are exact; "minor" = MMUCC B+C merged. The data has no collision type, lighting, weather or surface, and no US Park Police (federal land) crashes.

**Placement sample** (2,000 random 2025 crashes, TIGER 2024 11001 + MAR address points, police GPS hidden):
- MPD GPS in DC: 100%. Placed from the address text: 88.6% (address 1,709, exact 56, fuzzy 6). Auto under `Gate()`: 2.8%.
- Within 250 ft of MPD GPS: 98.7% (Wilson low 98.1%). **This is circular:** MPD's GPS is the MAR geocode of the typed address (90.6% of address placements land within 5 ft). No-GPS crashes added: 0. DDOT drops unlocatable crashes before publishing.

**Shared-code fixes needed (not made here):** `names.street_key` must keep DC quadrants (`U STREET NW` loses its suffix today) and must read lettered streets (`N ST NW` → core `NORTH NW`). `locate.offset` only takes N/E/S/W, but DC gives diagonal approach directions. The address tier is not in `auto_tiers`.

## Files
- `backend/crashiq/sources/dc_crashes.py`: standalone reader (`fetch(year)`, `records()`), stdlib only

the intersection: 83.5% (low 78.2%). The diagnosis (`placement_diag.py`) points at officer-typed GPS and noisy

- A registry entry per reader; NC county FIPS (Raleigh rows carry none).
- NC's severity U = "injury unknown" (NCDOT's code, weighed like PDO in its severity index), not CA's U.

The catch: **no licence for paid use**. ODOT gives only a disclaimer that expects re-release. Portland, Salem, Eugene and Bend have no crash feeds of their own; they all use ODOT's data.

### What's in this PR
- `backend/crashiq/sources/or_odot.py`: standalone reader, **not wired in**.
  - `read_decode()` reads the yearly decode DB tables exported to CSV, with KABCO per person and crash severity in `KABCUO`.
  - `fetch_layer()` reads ODOT's public ArcGIS layer (2019-2024, crash level only).
  - Both use the shared crash shape.

  - `or-methods.md`: APM Ch. 4 rates, Table II, critical rate, SPIS, crash costs, HSM calibration, CRF Manual, differences from California
  - the placement-sample script and its output

### Placement sample (Multnomah 2024, 2,000 crashes, TIGER 2024, GPS hidden, `locate.place`, `Gate()`)
- GPS present and in Oregon: 98.7%. Both street names: 97.1%. House addresses: 0.
- City streets: 1,170 of 1,492 (78.4%) auto-placed; 96.6% of those land within 250 ft (Wilson low 95.4%). That is below the 98% bar.
- Freeways: 3 of 449 placed. ODOT writes ramp codes such as `WB EF 181ST AVE C3`. Every state-highway crash has `HWY_NO` + `MP_NO`, so a milepoint tier is needed.
- No-GPS crashes: names add 0 of 156; 151 of them name only one road.

### Shared code is untouched. Wiring would need
1. A way to read the .mdb on the server (mdbtools, or a pure-Python reader).
2. A per-year cache of the decode zips.
3. An Oregon alias table and name splitting in `names.py`: slash pairs, `AV`/`FY`/`HY` abbreviations, ramp codes, bridges.
4. A milepoint tier on ODOT's LRS layer.
5. Oregon method tables in the state pack (#19).

- Choose the decode DB (persons, 2015-2024), the ArcGIS layer (2019-2024), or both.

Within 250 ft of S4's point: 76.3% overall (Wilson low 73.9%), **91.3% off freeways (low 89.5%)**, **4% on I-95/Turnpike**. The truth is S4's mapped point, not independent GPS.

title: feat(#19): state packs — Virginia, Massachusetts, Washington, Oregon, DC, New York statewide (CA unchanged)
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-08: "build where the data for a state, get all the data in"; earlier "start the other states"). Engineering, please review. **Replaces #425, #426, #428, #429, #431, #433** (their reader commits are merged here; those PRs are left open for reference). Follows `docs/state-pack-design.md` (#424, included).

## What it does
1. **State packs (#19).** `packs.py` holds the registry. Every non-CA value lives in `data/reference/methods_<st>.json`, and each one cites a manual and page or is marked `missing` with the reason. A pack that cites another state's manual doesn't load. Outside CA no Caltrans value is used: no LRSM costs, TASAS rate groups, postmiles, AADT, PCF wording or references.
2. **A study belongs to a state.** Migration 16 adds `study.state`, default CA, fixed once the study is created. **State is the first Setup field**: ready states are selectable, the rest show greyed out as "coming". A corridor with no point inside the study's state is refused.
3. **`pull_reader`** handles non-CA packs; the dispatch is one line in `crashes.ensure()`. California runs today's `pull()` unchanged.
4. **Statewide packs:**

   | Pack | Source | Notes |
   |---|---|---|
   | VA | VDOT Full Crash | Cited 2026 VDOT costs; 23 USC 407 / DPPA notice |
   | MA | MassDOT IMPACT | KABCO from persons. Boston under-count caveat on Boston corridors. The 2024 costs were found but are unverified, so they aren't printed |
   | WA | WSDOT Crash Data Portal, statewide | SDOT Seattle used as enrichment by report number. Cited WSDOT costs; §148/§407 footer. No rate tables (WSDOT uses none) |
   | OR | ODOT public crash layer, 2019–2024 | The yearly .mdb files (2015+) aren't read yet. Costs/rates `missing`: ODOT prices levels together |
   | DC | DDOT Crashes in DC + persons | DDOT "minor" counted as **U**; no invented B/C. CC BY credit |
   | NY | DMV cases by reference marker outside NYC; NYPD open data in the five boroughs | **K/U/O only**: KSI = fatal only, labelled everywhere, and the findings validator blocks serious-injury claims |

5. **Shared-code fixes the readers needed**, each with a regression test (California goldens unchanged):
   - bare numbered streets (`E 26 ST`, `63 DRIVE`)
   - `M L KING`
   - block crashes (`A between B and C`) placed mid-block
   - TIGER shape ids unique across counties
   - quadrant prefixes/suffixes (`SE POWELL BLVD`, `GEORGIA AVE NW`): without this, every Portland and DC crash was dropped as "not on corridor street"
   - NYC persons queried by a quoted `collision_id`

## Tests
- Backend full suite, green at each state commit: 1021 (MA), 1023 (WA), 1029 (OR), 1038 (DC); all 2 skipped. 07de8e6 (VA) had one failure in `test_background_pull::test_two_requests_share_one_pull` that passed 3/3 alone (flaky under load).
- **HEAD 8a7b49c: 1044 passed, 2 skipped** (full suite, 4 min).
- Frontend: vitest 124/124 (`--maxWorkers=2`), eslint clean.

## Live end-to-end (real data, 2020–2024; Setup → corridor → pull → profile → findings → PDF + Excel)
| State | Corridor | Counted | K/A/B/C/U/O | Crash cost | PDF / Excel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VA | W Broad St, Richmond | 426 | 1/19/102/15/0/289 | $77.5M (VDOT 2026) | 83 / 41 KB |
| MA | Blue Hill Ave, Boston | 213 | 1/8/41/31/0/132 | not shown (unverified) | 93 / 45 KB |
| WA | Rainier Ave S, Seattle | 169 | 2/8/22/30/5/102 | $57.2M (WSDOT) | 55 / 39 KB |
| OR | SE Powell Blvd, Portland | 151 | 5/7/34/49/0/56 | none (missing) | 69 / 38 KB |
| DC | Georgia Ave NW | 829 | 1/12/0/0/242/574 | none (missing) | 95 / 36 KB |
| NY | Queens Blvd, Queens (0.93 mi, 9 intersections) | 328 | 0/0/0/0/124/204 | $3.8M, **PDO only** | 51 / 39 KB |

- The Boston under-count note appears in the MA PDF.
- The NY PDF says "New York's sources don't report injury levels".

## Open decisions (for the user)
1. **Costs where injury levels are missing (NY, DC):** today the injury crashes (U) are left unpriced and counted in a column. NY's Queens Blvd total ($3.8M) is then property damage only, which ranks locations by PDO. Recommendation: no cost column or ranking at all when U crashes are present and unpriced.
2. **DC "minor" injury:** B, or U as built?
3. **Licence for paid use:** only DC (CC BY) and NYC are clear. VA, MA, OR and WA need each DOT's written OK before customers in those states are charged.

## Not done
- Oregon's yearly .mdb files for 2015–2018.
- MA cost verification.
- NY upstate reference-marker placement checked live.
- TX, FL and NC: gated, and need the user's login or an export.
- Per-state AADT, so rates are omitted outside CA and the reports say so.
- Full suite at HEAD: done (1044 passed).

title: statepack(AR): Arkansas statewide
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-08: across the country). Engineering, please review.

## Arkansas statewide: `status="active"`
- **Source:** ARDOT Arkansas Crash Analytics Tool layer (ASP eCrash reports cleaned by ARDOT), public ArcGIS REST, no login: `gis.ardot.gov/referenced/rest/services/TPP_TrafficSafety/NotForOfficialUse/FeatureServer/20`.
- **Bucket A\***: 401,279 crashes 2021–2025 (rolling 5 years, ~80k/yr), GPS on 99.63%, KABCO at crash level. No person/vehicle tables, no weather, no readable street text (road name is inside `AH_RoadID` with spaces removed), so the reader places by GPS only.
- **Licence for paid use: unclear.** Quote: "The data contained in the web-based dashboard is not an official record for crash statistics … Users are advised that their use of any ARDOT GIS Data is at their own risk … (see 23 USC, Section 409)." It's in `legal`.
- **Placement sample:** Pulaski County 2025, all 15,030 crashes: GPS 100%. A hidden-GPS locator test wasn't run because there's no primary street text to place from.
- **End-to-end** (S University Ave, W 12th St to Asher Ave, Little Rock, 1.55 mi, 2021–2025): pulled 1,174, counted 263; K 0 / A 3 / B 24 / C 36 / U 0 / O 200; cost $8,641,000 (ARDOT HSIP Process 2022 App. E, 2020 $); PDF 36,568 B, Excel 34,499 B.
- **Costs** come from the ARDOT HSIP Process (2022), App. E. Statewide rates and minimum years are `missing`, with the reason given.

## Files (add-only)
`statepacks/ar.py`, `sources/ar_ardot.py`, `methods_ar.json`, `county_boxes_ar.json`, `tests/test_source_ar.py` + fixture (58 KB), `research_notes/ar-2026-11-08/`.

## Shared fixes needed (not made here): `research_notes/ar-2026-11-08/shared-fixes.md`
1. A squeezed street-name match (`NRODNEYPARHAMRD`), which would let the reader fill `primary_road`.
2. `AR` as a state-route prefix.
3. **`test_packs.py::test_setup_lists_ready_states_first` and `test_study.py::test_meta_lists_states_ready_first_and_answers_for_one` fail on this branch.** They assume CA sorts first, but Arkansas sorts ahead of it alphabetically.
4. `default_window` should clamp to `pack.first_year`.

Full suite on this branch: 1052 passed, 2 failed (the 2 above), 2 skipped.

## User actions
- Ask the ARDOT Traffic Safety Section for written permission to show ACAT data in a paid product.
- Optional: ask ARDOT for its statewide average crash rates by roadway type.

- **Part years are never counted.** The reader asks the layer for its newest crash date with one statistics query. Any year after the last full year goes into `years_missing` and its rows are dropped. `final_lag_months=46` keeps the default window at 2018–2022; see shared-fixes #1 for the proper fix.
- **Placement sample:** Ada County 2022, all 6,682 crashes: GPS 100%, 99.97% inside Ada's box, serial numbers unique. There's no street text, so no locator test was run.

**Source:** Kentucky State Police, Collision Analysis for the Public (crashinformationky.org, KyOPS reports from every Kentucky agency). Open, no login. Bucket **A\*** (open + GPS; catches: no KABCO, undocumented site calls, no licence).

- If the site says a range is "too large", the reader splits it in half and tries again. Each year is cached once it's over.
- Years: 2015 to now (updated daily).
- **Severity is K / U / O only.** The public rows give only the number killed and injured. `severity_note` is set; A/B/C are never invented. KABCO exists only in KYTC's CRASH/CDAT (needs an MOU).
- Licence: none. The site says "no warranty, either expressed or implied, is given to the accuracy, completeness, reliability, or suitability for any particular purpose".

## Measured (2026-11-08)
- Sample: central Louisville, Jan–Feb 2025, 1,970 crashes.

## Colorado statewide: CDOT Statewide Crash Data Listing (2021 on)

- **Bucket A, status active**, with one engineering blocker (below). CDOT posts one Excel listing per year, 2007-2026,

- GPS 75.8% (2021) → 97.8% (2024) → 99.75% (2025). Street pair (Location 1 / Link / Location 2) on ~83%; Link gives

`download()` repeats OnBase's page flow. It fetched 2021-2023 at 11:57; from ~12:28 every scripted attempt got OnBase's
**Sign In** page (fresh cookies, fresh app id, two server nodes) while headless Chrome still downloaded 2025
anonymously. The reader now reports a year that won't download as missing (`cleaning.download_failed`), never part-counted;
downloaded years are cached (gzip JSON ~6 MB/yr, keyed by docid). A fresh server with an empty cache may get no

## Alabama statewide pack: `status="reader_only"` (built and passes end-to-end; not offered yet)

**Source:** the CARE eCrash map layer (`care-esriext.aladata.com/.../eCrash/Red/MapServer/0`). University of Alabama CAPS runs it for ALDOT/ALEA. It's an open ArcGIS service with no token.
- Every Alabama eCrash report from 2020 to today: about 140k a year, and the newest crash is dated 2026-11-08.
- KABCO severity, 85% with a point, street and cross street.
- **Why `reader_only`:** ALDOT's *Safety Data Access Guidebook* (PDF p. 6) says "These data are not to be shared with the public pursuant to Alabama Law and 23 U.S.C. §§148(h)(4) and 409". CAPS keeps location data behind a password portal. The layer looks unintended, so the summary buckets the state as **D** until ALDOT/CAPS give permission.
- **Shifted rows, repaired:** from OBJECTID 746,179 on (227,676 rows: April 2025 on, plus 1,699 late 2024 loads), CARE's text columns sit two places to the left. `CrashSev` holds the at-intersection flag, `County` the year, and so on.

- Severity "Unknown" (2–5%) isn't counted.

## Measured (2026-11-08)
- Placement test: Jefferson County 2024, 2,000 crashes with a point.

  - Only **44.1%** land within 250 ft of CARE's point (Wilson 95% lower bound 41.3%). By point source: node-derived 74%, manual 78%, officer GPS 35%, route-milepost 11%.
  - **Root cause in shared code:** `names.street_key("3rd Ave N") == street_key("3RD AVE S")`. Birmingham's N/S twin grid collides. See `shared-fixes.md`, which includes a proposed test.
  - Of the 8,079 no-point crashes, 35% would be auto-placed by name.

title: Shared fixes the state packs need (AL quadrants, AR squeezed names, KS per-person costs, PA U at C, ID last year, ramps, 35E/35W)
body:
From the state-pack builds (2026-11-08); each item is quoted from its build's `research_notes/<st>-2026-11-08/shared-fixes.md`. Hermes already merged the route-prefix fixes (5df876e on `feat/state-pack-wa-ny`). **These are left for Engineering**: each touches matching or costs that California's goldens depend on.

1. **Trailing single-letter quadrant on numbered streets (AL).** `street_key("3rd Ave N") == street_key("3RD AVE S")`. Birmingham repeats its numbered avenues north and south, so a pair "meets in more than one place" or lands on the twin. In the Jefferson County sample, "4th Ave S & 15th St S" was auto-placed 11,594 ft off, and auto-placed accuracy was 44%. Proposal: keep N/S/E/W in the key when the core is numbered. Risk: California numbered streets with a trailing direction.
2. **Names written with no spaces (AR).** ARDOT writes `NRODNEYPARHAMRD` and `KAVANAUGHBLVD`, about 19% of its cross streets. Proposal: a squeezed-form fallback in `crashes._names_street`. Until then the AR reader blanks the roads (GPS-only).
3. **Per-person crash costs (KS).** KDOT prices each injured person (2023 Kansas Traffic Crash Facts p. 77). `profile._cost` prices once per crash, so KS ships with `crash_costs` missing. The patch and test are in ks shared-fixes.
4. **U priced at C (PA).** PennDOT Pub 638 prices "injury, unknown severity" at the C cost. This needs a per-pack rule (the CA LRSM rule already does it for CA). Related to the open user decision on costs where injury levels are missing (NY, DE, VT, DC).
5. **A source's last full year (ID).** `StatePack.last_year: Callable` as an upper bound on `default_window`. ITD's open service is about 3 years behind; today it's fixed with `final_lag_months=46`.
6. **Ramp text in the cross street (KY, CO, AL).** "I264 EB EXIT17A OFF RAMP TO KY155 SB", "I-70 WB ON RAMP": these give "no intersection" instead of a ramp tier.
7. **Two streets in one field (MS).** "Pear Orchard Dr. / North Town Dr."
8. **Block numbers (CO).** "WELTON ST" & "1400 BLK": a bare "<n> BLK" secondary should be a house address on the primary (D5).
9. **35E / 35W (MN, TX).** `I-35E` keys as `I 35`, so the two roads become one. Decide whether lettered interstate branches stay distinct.

Each item needs a regression test, and the California suite and goldens must stay green.

title: statepack(IL): Illinois statewide
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-08: across the country). Engineering, please review.

## Illinois statewide pack: `status="active"`

**The 2026-11-02 screen was wrong** (it said bucket D, Safety Portal login). IDOT also publishes every crash statewide as open ArcGIS layers on its hub: "Crashes - 2014" … "Crashes - 2025", owner IDOTAdmin, no login. Bucket **A**.

- **Volume:** about 300,000 crashes a year, Chicago included (100,055 Chicago crashes in 2025).
- **GPS:** on 99.82% (2025: 538 of 303,087 have no point).
- **Severity:** IDOT's KABCO. The worst of the K/A/B/C counts matches IDOT's crash level row for row (2014, 2025).
- **Street names: 2025 layer only.** It has the road, a "road/cross street" pair, the house number, and the distance and direction from the intersection. 2014-2024 have a route number and milestation only, so those years are read by GPS.
- **2019 layer defect:** about 25% of rows have every column after `TrafficwayDescrip` shifted by an unquoted comma. The reader reads severity from the counts (which sit before the shift) and freeway from `ClassOfTrafficway` as well.
- **Licence:**
  - 2014-2020: CC BY-SA 2.0.
  - 2024: IDOT's map disclaimer, quoted in `legal`.
  - 2021-2023 and 2025: no licence text.
  - **Paid use: unclear.**
- **Chicago's portal (85ca-t3if)** is not read: IDOT already covers Chicago. The only gap is the current year, which isn't final.

## Measured (2026-11-08)
- **Placement the California way:** hide the GPS, place the street pair on TIGER 2024, `Gate(tiger_only_auto=True)`, 2025 layer.
  - DuPage County, random 2,000:
    - Road + cross street on 39.6%.
    - Auto-placed **32.0%**.
    - Within 250 ft of the hidden GPS **92.5%** (Wilson 95% lower bound 90.2%).
  - Chicago, 2,000: reports give a house number (84.6%), not a cross street (0.5%), so street-pair placement is 0.4%. House-address placement was not measured.
- **End-to-end on port 8101:** N Western Ave, Chicago, Fullerton to Belmont, 1.01 mi, 2021-2025.
  - Pulled 1,773, counted **796**, excluded 977, unplaced 0.
  - K/A/B/C/U/O = 1/13/67/49/0/666.
  - No cost column (methods: missing).
  - 9 findings.
  - PDF 88,752 B, Excel 39,588 B, 112 s.
- **Full suite:** **1068 passed, 2 skipped**.

## Files (added only)
- `backend/crashiq/statepacks/il.py`, `backend/crashiq/sources/il_idot.py`
- `data/reference/methods_il.json`:
  - Safety 1-06 (2006): min years = **5**, cited p. 8.
  - Crash costs `missing`: IDOT publishes per-person NSC costs (Crash Facts 2024 p. 23), not per-crash costs.
  - Statewide rates `missing`.
- `data/reference/county_boxes_il.json`: the shared builder run with IL added in-process; the script itself is not edited.
- `tests/test_source_il.py`, with a 121 KB fixture (2025, 2019 and 2014 rows).
- `research_notes/il-2026-11-08/`: import notes, methods, summary, HTML, `il_pull.py`, placement and e2e JSON, and `shared-fixes.md`, which covers:
  - `packs.COMING` still lists IL. The plug-in pops it for now; delete the entry centrally.
  - `Il Route 59` / `E Il-38` aren't read as state routes.
  - `Route 30` could be US 30 or IL 30.
  - `S S Highland Ave`.
  - `North Ave / Il-64`.

## User actions
1. Ask IDOT (DOT.DTS.DataRequests@illinois.gov) in writing whether the hub crash layers may be used in a paid product, and under which licence for 2021-2025.
2. Optional: ask IDOT for street names for 2014-2024 and its current per-crash HSIP costs.

title: statepack(OH): Ohio statewide
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-08: across the country). Engineering, please review.

**Ohio: active, bucket A\*.** The 2026-11-02 screen said D because it looked only at GCAT; TIMS is open. Checked
live 2026-11-08.

**Source:** ODOT TIMS public crash layers, `Safety/<year>_Crash_Locations/MapServer/0`, 2021-2025, no login.
- Rows: 2021 269,674; 2022 265,502; 2023 252,570; 2024 251,091; 2025 264,530.
- 2025 matches ODOT's own table (264,529 crashes, 1,033 fatal; CrashCostsUpdate.pdf p. 1), so the layer isn't filtered.
- GPS on every row. Severity is KABCO.
- Licence: TIMS says *"in the public domain and as such it is not copyrighted. Individuals can use, reproduce or
  copy material from TIMS … without seeking permission"*. The catch is that the REST endpoints are *"subject to
  change without notice"*.
- Missing from the layer: the **day of the month** (dates are blank; year, month, weekday and hour are kept),
  street names, people counts, light, weather and surface. These are listed in `data_notes`.

**Files (added only):**
- `sources/oh_tims.py` (`fetch_contract`)
- `statepacks/oh.py`
- `methods_oh.json`: ODOT 2025 economic unit costs, K $2,266,992 … O $11,648, sha256 saved; rates and min years
  `missing`
- `county_boxes_oh.json`
- `tests/test_source_oh.py`: 8 tests, 20 KB fixture of live Columbus rows
- `research_notes/oh-2026-11-08/`: import.md/html, methods.md, summary.json, placement_sample.json,
  e2e_result.json, shared-fixes.md

**Placement sample:** Franklin County 2024, 2,000 rows. GPS is plausible on 2,000/2,000 (all inside the county box).
The source has no street names, so name placement isn't measurable (and isn't needed).

**End-to-end (port 8102):** N High St (US 23), Columbus, 5th Ave–Lane Ave, 1.21 mi, 2021-2025.
- 643 pulled, **500 counted** (486 intersection, 14 segment); 143 excluded by buffer or limits; 0 unplaced.
- K 1, A 13, B 98, C 60, O 328.
- Cost $19,297,824.
- 9 findings.
- PDF 92,589 B, XLSX 42,605 B.

**Tests:** full suite **1071 passed, 2 skipped**.

**Shared fixes** (see shared-fixes.md):
1. Allow `YYYY-MM` dates in the contract.
2. A single-road mode for sources that give one route per crash.

**User actions (optional):**
1. Request an ODPS Crash Statistics CSV (free; email + captcha) for full dates and streets.
2. Choose economic (used) or comprehensive ODOT costs.

title: statepack(TN): Tennessee statewide
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-08: across the country). Engineering, please review.

## Tennessee statewide, as a plug-in (status `active`)

The 2026-11-02 screen called Tennessee gated (D). Verified live: **A\***. Two public statewide ArcGIS layers, no login:

- **TDOT "Tennessee Crashes JAN 2021_JAN 2025"** (TDOT_GIS): every crash 2021-2024 (~190k/yr), a point on each, **KABCO**, manner of collision, route number (I 24 / SR 11). Read for 2021-2024.
- **TDOSHS crash dashboard layer** (TITAN reports, weekly): fatal + injury only, 2024 on, GPS, KABC. Read for 2025 on.
- **Metro Nashville Traffic Accidents** (open data): its no-injury crashes fill the PDO gap inside Davidson County from 2025 (0.56% look like a state crash already; left in).

No street names in either state layer, so placement is by point; the name test wasn't run.

**Licence:** TDOT: informational-use, no-warranty disclaimer only; TDOSHS: nothing published → *unclear*. Metro: its ToS exempts Open Data Portal data from the commercial-use ban → *ok with attribution*.

## End to end (port 8104)
Nolensville Pike, Nashville, 0.92 mi, 2021-2024: pulled 516, **counted 406: K 3 / A 9 / B 107 / C 41 / O 246**, 0 unplaced, 0 contract errors, 11 findings, PDF 79 KB, Excel 39 KB. No crash cost (TDOT has no table; cited `missing`). An earlier run of the TDOSHS + Metro path (2024) counted 94 (A 6 / B 28 / C 8 / O 52).

## Files (added only)
- `backend/crashiq/sources/tn_tdot.py`, `backend/crashiq/statepacks/tn.py`

## Missouri statewide, as a plug-in (status `active`)

The 2026-11-02 screen called Missouri "aggregate only" (D). Verified live: **A\***. MSHP's "Traffic Crashes Online Mapping" runs on a public ArcGIS layer, `STARS_CRASHES/MapServer/0`: **1.97 M crash reports**, 2013-current (plus 2002-03), no login. GPS on 95%, the officer's On / Intersecting street and After / Before distance on 85%.

- Severity **K / A / U / O**: the layer keeps disabling (A) and minor injuries; MoDOT maps "Minor Injury" to "B & C" (EPG 905.3.6.1.4), so minor = U. No `severity_note` (A is real), said in `data_notes`.
- **PDO crashes stop in 2024** (2023: 101,342; 2024: 24,623; 2025: none). Said in `data_notes`.
- No-GPS crashes in the corridor's counties are read too; the core sorts them by street name.

**Placement (Jackson County 2023, 2,000 with GPS hidden, TIGER 2024, `Gate(tiger_only_auto=True)`):** street pair 87%, **auto-placed 61.9%, within 250 ft 95.6% (Wilson low 94.3%)**. 995 no-GPS crashes, 607 with a street pair.

**Licence:** none published by MSHP → *unclear*.

## End to end (port 8104)
Troost Ave, Kansas City, 0.99 mi, 2020-2024: read 5,143 (4,654 no-GPS county rows), kept 523, **counted 307: K 1 / A 5 / U 116 / O 185**, 5 unplaced, 0 contract errors, 8 findings, PDF 54 KB, Excel 37 KB. No crash cost (MoDOT gives values only on request; cited `missing`).

title: statepack(RI): Rhode Island statewide
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-08: across the country). Engineering, please review.

## Rhode Island: gated (bucket D, verified live 2026-11-08). No pack.

- **RIDOT statewide crash repository.** RIGL 38-2-17 (2026-H 7576 / S 2480, effective June 2026) made it a public record, *"provided, however, the records may not be used for purposes prohibited by"* 23 U.S.C. 407. Access is still by **APRA request only**. RIDOT's own Traffic Design Manual 2025 (§7.1.1, p. 7-1) says crash data *"must be requested from the RIDOT Office of Safety"*. Paid-use terms: unclear.
- **Checked:** RIDOT's ArcGIS Online org (`owner:DOT_AGOL.Admin`, 44 services) and RIGIS hosting (86 services) have no crash layer. The "Crash Data 2023-2025" links are Crash Facts PDFs, i.e. aggregates (2025: 36,850 crashes; KABCO split K 0.1 / A 0.6 / B 2.5 / C 15.7 / O 75.6 / unknown 5.5%).
- **Providence** PVD Crash Map: a community project from PPD records, with no licence. Not used.
- **Column map** (`ri-column-map.json`): built from the 2006 Uniform Crash Report form and the TDM 2025 crash-summary fields. No field dictionary is published, and GPS isn't documented.
- **Methods:** KABCO and a 5-year minimum (TDM 2025, pp. 7-1 to 7-2). Costs and rates are missing from the HSIP 2025 report.

Files (notes only): `research_notes/ri-2026-11-08/` `ri-import.md`, `ri-import.html`, `ri-summary.json`, `ri-column-map.json`.

**User actions:** file an APRA request with RIDOT for 2021-2025 plus 2026 crash, vehicle and person tables, the dictionary and lat/lon, as CSV. Ask about online publication and paid use. Send one delivered file.

No code changed. Tests aren't affected.

The 2026-11-02 screen was half wrong: HDOT **does** publish record-level crash points with no login
(`HDOT_Crash_Layer` 2015-2023 + `HDOT_Crash_Layer_2024`, 37,315 crashes, a point on 99.9%; fatal layer 2012-2025,
1,416 crashes, public domain). They still can't feed a pack:

- **year only**: no date, no time, no report number
- **no KABCO**: one undocumented "major injury" flag (blank 2015-2017), no fatal flag
- **no street names, route or milepost**
- **state highways only until 2022**; county roads (most Honolulu streets) start in 2023
- licence: "for highway safety and educational purposes only" (no paid-use grant)

Building a study on it would mean inventing dates and severities. Full data is in HDOT's SHACA, by request.
Honolulu open data has no crash table.

Files (adds only, `research_notes/hi-2026-11-08/`): `hi-import.md`, `hi-import.html`, `hi-summary.json`,
`hi-methods.md`, `hi-column-map.json`, `hi_measure.py` + `hi_measure.json` (rows per year, jurisdiction, flags).

report number and written paid-use permission; or ask HDOT to add date + KABCO to the open layer (then it's a pack).

title: statepack(NH): New Hampshire statewide
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-08: across the country). Engineering, please review.

## New Hampshire: gated (bucket D), no pack: notes, column map, placement sample

Verified live: no agency-published record-level crash data. Searched the NH state ArcGIS org by owner (0 crash
layers), NHDOT's GIS quarterly snapshots on GRANIT 2022-2026 (55 layers, none crashes), the NHDOT GIS Data Catalog.
Crash records sit in NH DMV VISION under RSA 260:14 (release only for listed uses; bulk via Saf-C 5602, DSMV 494).

Re-hosts of NHDOT's crash layer (UVLSRPC 2002-2017, a consultant's NH 114 layer 2017-2023) aren't sources, but they
give the export layout (KABCO severity, date/time, town, road, NHDOT point, SRI + milepoint): `nh-column-map.json`.

**Placement sample** (UVLSRPC re-host, Grafton 2015-16, n = 1,773, TIGER 2024): street pair 84%, placed 43%
(51% of pairs), auto 37.9% with `tiger_only_auto`. Within 250 ft of the layer's point: 34.9% (low 31.6%). The
"truth" is NHDOT's LRS-snapped point, not GPS: 39% of crashes share a point with 5+ others; where the point is
unique, at-intersection agreement is 57%. Route spellings (`RT 4`, `USHY 4`, `ROUTE 4-A`, `89 N`, bare route codes)
and house numbers in front of streets are what a reader must normalise.

Methods: NH crash costs (2021 $, FHWA-assisted): K $13.6M, A $737,900, KABC avg $582,125, O $8,623; HSM Part D,
B/C >= 2.0. Unverified: dot.nh.gov 403s scripted downloads.

Files (adds only, `research_notes/nh-2026-11-08/`): `nh-import.md`, `nh-import.html`, `nh-summary.json`,
`nh-methods.md`, `nh-column-map.json`, `placement_sample.py` + `.json`.

**User actions:** ask NHDOT (GISMaps@dot.nh.gov / crash data analyst) for one county-year sample of its GIS crash
layer with written paid-use permission; re-check in 2027 for NH OHS's planned public crash portal.

No code changed.

Breaks: Tulsa grid names written many ways, direction after the route ("I-244 WESTBOUND", "(EASTBOUND)"), parenthesised second names: see `shared-fixes.md`.

title: statepack(NM): New Mexico statewide
body:
**Written by Hermes** (user 2026-11-08: across the country). Engineering, please review.

## New Mexico: Bernalillo County from UNM/NMDOT data (plug-in, `status="reader_only"`)

- **Statewide is gated (bucket D, verified live).** NMDOT gives crash data only through its request form; UNM-GPS
  "will not release traffic crash data directly to end users." NMDOT's ArcGIS org (searched by owner) has subsets only
  (VRU 2013-2023, I-40 2016-2021).
- **The 2026-11-02 screen missed an open county feed:** the City of Albuquerque's `Crashes Five Year 2020 - 2024`
  layer, "all reported crashes in Bernalillo County ... compiled by UNM's Geospatial and Population Studies group on
  behalf of NMDOT". 75,460 crashes, GPS on 99.8%, street + cross street/landmark with distance and direction, people
  killed and class A/B/C injured → KABCO. No persons/vehicles/surface.
- **Licence for paid use: unclear.** Layer: "All data is provided AS IS from UNM/NMDOT"; cabq.gov's website licence is
  "non-commercial, personal, or educational purposes only"; the ABQ Data disclaimer asks derivative apps to show a notice.
- **Why reader_only:** 1 of 33 counties, plus the licence. Outside Bernalillo (or outside 2020-2024) the reader returns
  the years as **missing**, never zero crashes.

### Files (all new; no shared file touched)
- `backend/crashiq/statepacks/nm.py`: `PACK` (legal = the layer's text + 23 USC 407, data notes)
- `backend/crashiq/sources/nm_cabq.py`: `fetch_contract`: LAT/LON box + YEAR query, OBJECTID paging, raw-JSON cache;
  landmark used as the cross street when it names a street (offset kept only when it's measured from that street);
  collision type from the first harmful event (the old CLASSIFICATION field is blank on 95% of 2024 rows); date from
  `DATE` when the time is missing (1.7%); 4 repeated report numbers dropped.
- `data/reference/methods_nm.json` (`check_methods` clean): costs = NMDOT's AASHTOWare defaults from a vendor page,
  `verified: false`, never printed; severity rule cited to UNM's dictionary pp. 7-8; rates/min years/SPF `missing`.
- `data/reference/county_boxes_nm.json` (33 counties, Census cb_2024 + 5 km)
- `tests/test_source_nm.py` + 79 KB fixture (36 live 2024 rows + 1 duplicate)
- `research_notes/nm-2026-11-08/`: import, methods, summary JSON, phone HTML, placement script + result, e2e result,
  `serve_active.py` (harness only)

### Placement sample (Bernalillo 2024, 2,000 crashes with both names, GPS hidden, TIGER 2024)
Placed from names 76.4%; default `Gate()` 0% auto (TIGER-only network); `tiger_only_auto` 71.5% auto, **91.7% within
250 ft** (Wilson low 90.2%). Only 11 of 15,528 crashes lack GPS, so it's a cross-check.

### End-to-end (live, port 8102, NM flipped to active in memory)
Central Ave (US 66 Hist), San Mateo to Louisiana, Albuquerque, 1.06 mi, 2020-2024: 1,079 read, 0 contract errors,
955 pulled, **779 counted** (K 11, A 18, B 65, C 165, U 0, O 520), no cost, 19 findings, PDF 94,034 B, Excel 39,011 B.

### Tests
`test_source_nm.py` + `test_packs.py`: 22 passed. Full suite (niced): **1072 passed, 2 skipped**.

### User actions
1. Ask the City of Albuquerque and NMDOT in writing whether a paid tool may load the layer, and what notice to show.
2. Other counties: NMDOT crash data request (crash-level export; the reader takes it after the column renames listed in `nm-import.md` §2).
3. Ask NMDOT HSIP for per-level crash costs and their dollar year.
4. Decide whether to offer NM as "Albuquerque only" (`active`).

Not checked: a real NMDOT export, the 2016-2019 Albuquerque layers, house addresses.

title: Decision needed: bring the CMF Clearinghouse into CrashIQ (countermeasures, D9)
body:
**Proposal (not built). Each numbered choice waits for the user's answer.** Context: docs/03 D9 (CMF Clearinghouse use, matching method to confirm) and phasing P2 HSIP → P3 ISOAP.

## What FHWA offers
FHWA publishes the whole Clearinghouse as one free download "for users who would like to use automated routines to regularly ingest data … into analytical tools": https://cmfclearinghouse.fhwa.dot.gov/cmf_data.php (CSV / XLSX / XML + a data dictionary PDF, refreshed about quarterly). There's no scraping and no per-study request.

Measured by code on the 2026-11-10 download (`cmfclearinghouse.csv`, 28.9 MB; kept outside the repo in `Workspace/data/crashiq/cmf/`):
- 10,178 CMFs for 1,300 countermeasures, 183 fields each.
- Every row has a CMF value and a standard error.
- Star rating: 5★ 612, 4★ 2,539, 3★ 3,299, 2★ 1,739, 1★ 746, unrated (negative codes) 1,243. That gives **3,151 at 4–5★, covering 375 countermeasures.**
- Developed in California: 551 (272 at 4–5★).
- Study method: 3,602 empirical/full Bayes before/after, 2,139 cross-section, 1,217 simple before/after (the weakest, prone to regression to the mean).
- Applicability fields per CMF: crash type, KABCO severity, area type, intersection vs segment, traffic control, roadway type, AADT range, lanes, speed limit, years of data, state.

## How it fits D9
D9's "curated, versioned table, built once, refreshed periodically, not scraped" becomes this download, saved with its date. Code filters it. The user approves what's on the shortlist (nothing is learned without approval).

## Choices for the user
1. **Source.** (a) *Recommended:* load the full file, versioned by download date, and filter it in code. (b) Hand-pick a short list and load only that.
2. **Quality floor.** (a) *Recommended:* offer 4–5★ only; 3★ only on request, with a warning. (b) Allow 3★ and up by default.
3. **How "crashes reduced" is worked out.** This is where accuracy is won or lost.
   - **HSIP mode:** Caltrans' required method stays: observed crashes × the LRSM CRF (its closed list). The Clearinghouse isn't used there.
   - **Other modes:** a site with few crashes gives a noisy count, and a site picked *because* of a recent spike will look better after any treatment (regression to the mean). (a) *Recommended:* use the HSM's empirical Bayes "expected crashes" where a safety performance function and AADT exist (state highways, via Caltrans AADT #287). Elsewhere, use observed crashes, labelled "observed, N crashes, not adjusted for regression to the mean". (b) Observed × CMF everywhere, labelled.
   - **Either way:** every reduction is shown as a low–high range from the CMF's standard error (95%), never a single bare number.
4. **Applicability.** (a) *Recommended:* a CMF whose stated ranges exclude the site (AADT, area type, control, crash type, severity) isn't offered. (b) Offer it with a warning.
5. **Combining** stays as D9 says: Caltrans max 3; warn when multiplying more than 2 CMFs.

## Not checked yet
- Licence/terms for redistribution inside a paid product. It's a US federal site, but the wording hasn't been read yet. That gets checked before anything ships.
- Whether every crash-type label maps cleanly onto CrashIQ's collision types. That gets measured once (1) is decided.

title: Surrogate safety: read trajectory files (SSAM .trj + CSV) and find conflicts by FHWA's SSAM method
body:
**User decision, 2026-11-10 (PM chat): "3a"**: start now, on its own branch, kept separate from the launch. Recorded in docs/03 (PR #483).

## Goal
CrashIQ reads vehicle trajectories and finds traffic conflicts (near-misses) following FHWA's published SSAM method. The same tool then shows simulated or video conflicts next to the real crashes.

## Inputs
- SSAM `.trj` binary (format 1.04 and 3.0, both endians, optional Z): exports from Vissim, Aimsun, Paramics and TEXAS. Spec: usdot-jpo-codehub/SSAM `Documentation/SSAM File Format v1.04.pdf` + `Open Source SSAM File Format v3.0.pdf`.
- A plain trajectory CSV (time, id, front x/y, rear x/y, length, width, speed, accel, optional link/lane), for video tracks (traffic-vision) and drone datasets.

## Method (from FHWA-HRT-08-051 Ch. 2, a US government publication)
- 50 ft / 15.25 m zone grid.
- Project each vehicle along its next 10 s of trajectory for up to MaxTTC (default 1.5 s).
- Rectangle overlap gives a conflict candidate; refine TTC in 0.1 s steps.
- Track PET (default max 5 s).
- Classify by conflict angle (<30° rear-end, >85° crossing, else lane change), using link/lane when present.
- Measures: TTC, PET, MaxS, DeltaS, DR, MaxD, DeltaV, plus the CSP/CEP points.

## Licence (read before coding)
- **The SSAM 3.0 source code is AGPL-3.0** (header of `SSAMDLL/SSAM/Source.cpp`). Porting it would put CrashIQ under AGPL. **Do not read or port the C++ algorithm source.** Implement from the published report and file-format spec only (clean room).
- Running FHWA's `SSAM_MT.exe` as a black-box answer key is fine.
- Credit FHWA's method, and never present ours as FHWA's SSAM (FHWA's notice: altered versions must be marked).

## Acceptance
1. A reader for both formats, with round-trip tests (our writer makes test files).
2. Known-answer scenarios built in code, each with a hand-computed TTC/PET:
   - rear-end with a braking leader;
   - right-angle crossing;
   - lane-change cut-in;
   - a near pass that is not a conflict.
3. **Matches FHWA SSAM 3.0** (`SSAM_MT.exe trjfiles=... csvfile=...`) run on the same files:
   - same conflicts (pairs + type);
   - TTC/PET within 0.1 s.
   - Every miss is explained in the PR.
4. Speed: a 1-hour, about 1,000-vehicle file runs in minutes, not hours (grid + numpy).
5. Not wired into the UI yet: the screens come after the user approves the visuals mockup.

title: Surrogate safety: SSAM .trj/CSV readers, conflict finding by FHWA's published method, compare command (#484)
body:
Closes #484

## What's built (backend only, no UI)
`backend/crashiq/ssam/`, standard library only (no numpy needed, see speed below):
- `trj.py`: reads and writes SSAM `.trj` files, format 1.04 and 3.0 (with or without the Z option), little and big endian. Record sizes follow the spec tables: FORMAT 6 bytes (7 in 3.0), DIMENSIONS 22, TIMESTEP 5, VEHICLE 42 (50 with Z). X/Y are scaled by Scale. Link/lane id 0 is read as "unknown". Bad or truncated files raise a clear error.
- `trj.py`: `read_trajectory_csv` for video/drone tracks: `t, vehicle_id, front_x, front_y, rear_x, rear_y, length, width, speed, accel`, optional `link, lane, z`.
- `ngsim.py`: `python -m crashiq.ssam.ngsim <NGSIM csv> <out folder>` writes one .trj per recording period (English units). Rear point = front minus length along the heading from successive front positions; link = section_id, or 100 + int_id inside an intersection; lane = lane_id.
- `conflicts.py`: `find_conflicts(trj, max_ttc=1.5, max_pet=5.0)`, following FHWA-HRT-08-051 Ch. 2:
  - 50 ft / 15.25 m zone grid;
  - each vehicle projected `speed x tau` along its own next 10 s of trajectory, tau = 0, 0.1 ... MaxTTC;
  - overlap = some side of one rectangle crosses some side of the other (report Step 3, fig. 13; a rectangle wholly inside the other is no overlap); the TTC is the first 0.1 s step that overlaps;
  - events tracked across timesteps; positions are recorded at the steps with a TTC (Step 4.2) and PET is measured against those (max 5 s);
  - end-of-event measures: TTC, tMinTTC, PET, xMinPET/yMinPET, MaxS, DeltaS, DR, MaxD, ConflictAngle, PostCrashV/Heading, First/Second/MaxDeltaV, FirstVID/SecondVID, links/lanes, headings, CSP/CEP;
  - type: link/lane rules first, then |angle| < 30 rear-end, > 85 crossing, else lane change.

Choices the report leaves open (written in the module docstring, so a reviewer can see them):
- a projection that runs past the end of the recorded path continues straight;
- an event with no PET seen is still listed, with PET empty (OPEN 1);
- events still open when the file ends are listed (OPEN 2);
- the projected rectangle faces along the path at the projected point (OPEN 3);
- PostCrashV/DeltaV assume equal masses (the report gives none);
- positions use the vehicle centre.

## Tests (offline): 46 SSAM tests, all passing
- `tests/test_ssam_trj.py` (15): round trip for L and B endian x 1.04 / 3.0 / 3.0 with Z, byte sizes, scaling, bad files, CSV reader, and a check that the committed `tests/fixtures/ssam/*.trj` still match the scenario code.
- `tests/test_ssam_conflicts.py` (18): known-answer scenarios from `tests/ssam_scenarios.py`, hand working in each test's comments:

| Scenario | Expected (hand-worked) | Ours | FHWA SSAM_MT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rear-end, braking leader (now a 20 s file) | TTC 0.949 -> 1.0; PET 0.45 -> 0.5; leader first; MaxD -5 | same | same (TTC 1.0, PET 0.5, tMinTTC 3.7) |
| Follower brakes and drops back (new) | TTC 1.2 at t=3; PET 0.29 -> 0.3 from the leader's position at a TTC step; xMinPET 47.15 | same | same |
| Lane-change cut-in | TTC 1.118 -> 1.2; PET 0.083 -> 0.1; lane change from the lane ids | same | same |
| 90 degree crossing | TTC 0.9 at t=3.1; **no PET**: A's positions at the TTC steps (t <= 3.6) are all west of B's path | TTC 0.9, PET empty | no conflict (OPEN 1) |
| Near pass | no conflict | none | none |
| Car wholly inside a bus outline, then drives out (new) | first side crossing at t=3.8 | TTC 0 at 3.8 | same |

  Plus a threshold test, 10 classification cases, and `test_busy_scene_unchanged`: the full conflict list of a dense synthetic scene (80 vehicles, 60 s), frozen before the speed work, so any speed-up must leave every value identical.
- `tests/test_ssam_compare.py` (8): against **real** SSAM_MT output. `tests/fixtures/ssam/fhwa/<stem>.csv` are SSAM_MT's CSVs for the fixture .trj files, saved unchanged (it wrote none for crossing and near_pass). Reader on the real layout; our conflicts equal FHWA's on rear_end, follow_brake and cut_in (pair, order, type, tMinTTC, TTC, PET); the compare command end to end; time alignment of same-pair events; bad files.
- `tests/test_ssam_ngsim.py` (3): converter on synthetic rows. No NGSIM data is committed (CC BY-SA).

Full suite on the head commit: 1347 passed, 2 skipped (serial, no xdist). `ruff check backend tests`: clean.

## Compare command
`python -m crashiq.ssam.compare <folder of .trj> --exe <path>\SSAM_MT.exe [--ttc 1.5 --pet 5.0] [--out report.txt]`, or `--fhwa-dir <dir>` to reuse saved CSVs (`<dir>/<stem>.csv`).
- SSAM_MT's CSV: a 'Summary Statistics' block, then `Conflict Listing,<n>`, then the table (`Time (min TTC)`, ..., `ConflictType`, `FristVID` [sic], `SecondVID`, `TTC`, `PET`, ...). ConflictType is text (`rear end`, `crossing`, `lane change`) and is mapped to ours. The listing has **no file column**, so the exe runs once per .trj (CSVs kept in `<folder>/fhwa/`). No CSV written = no conflicts. The `<n>` is checked against the rows.
- Paths go to SSAM_MT unquoted (it rejects quoted paths), so a path with a space will not work.
- Same-pair events are aligned in time (tMinTTC within 2 s), since the engines can split one long interaction differently.
- Our engine runs one process per .trj. The report ends with each engine's wall-clock time.

## FHWA SSAM 3.0 comparison: done (black box, SSAM_MT.exe)
- [x] Fixture scenes: FHWA and ours agree exactly wherever FHWA lists a conflict (table above).

### What the black-box runs found (why `rear_end` and `crossing` were silent)
Method: start from cut_in, where both engines agreed, and change one thing at a time (file length, lanes, ids, record order, heading, severity, MaxPET/MaxTTC), each run through SSAM_MT.exe.
1. **SSAM_MT drops an event that is still open when the file ends.** rear_end is listed once the file runs to 14.5 s (it was 10 s). The minimum length scales exactly with MaxPET: the last TTC step + 1 x MaxPET in some scenes, + 2 x MaxPET in others (rear_end: 4.5 + 2 x 5; with PET 3: 10.5). The report doesn't describe this, so ours keeps listing such events (OPEN 2). The rear_end fixture is now 20 s, so both engines agree on it.
2. **PET is measured only against positions held at TTC steps.** SSAM_MT's xMinPET is always a leader position at a TTC step (follow_brake: PET 0.3 at x 47.15, the leader at t=2.7). That is the report's Step 4.2 (positions are recorded for pairs that overlap). Ours also recorded positions for MaxTTC after the last TTC step, which went against the report. **Fixed in ours** (test first: follow_brake).
3. **SSAM_MT does not list events with no PET.** After fix 2 the crossing scene has no PET (A has not reached B's path at any TTC step). Every near-miss crossing I built (24-case braking grid, waits, 45 degrees) is silent in FHWA. Crossings that end in a collision are listed by both. Ours lists TTC events with PET empty (OPEN 1).
4. **Overlap is a side-crossing test** (report fig. 13: "testing all sides of one vehicle for intersection with all sides of the other"). In SSAM_MT a car wholly inside a bus outline is no overlap until a side crosses (tMinTTC 3.8). Ours used area overlap. **Fixed in ours** (test first: contain).
5. Seen but not explained: with MaxPET <= 1.6 s, SSAM_MT lists none of the rear-end scenes, even in 60 s files. SSAM_MT also reports CSP and DeltaS at the **start** of the event (rear_end DeltaS 9.5, ours 6.5 at tMinTTC). The report defines both at tMinTTC, so ours keeps the report (OPEN 4).

### NGSIM Lankershim Blvd (real trajectories)
Data: data.transportation.gov 8ect-6jqj, all 1,607,319 rows (pulled 2026-11-11), CC BY-SA 3.0, not committed. The portal file joins the two recording periods, and each period restarts frame ids and reuses vehicle ids: 115,277 (vehicle, frame) keys occur in both periods and are different cars. So the converter splits by period start (global_time - 100 ms x (frame_id - 1)) **before** dropping duplicates. Inside a period there were none. Files: `lankershim_p1.trj` (8:28-8:46 PDT, 11,205 steps, 705,294 records) and `lankershim_p2.trj` (8:45-9:02, 10,471 steps, 902,025 records). Both engines ran on the same files, TTC 1.5, PET 5.0, ours at the head commit.

| | Ours (head) | Ours if projected rectangles kept the current facing (OPEN 3, not committed) |
|---|---|---|
| FHWA conflicts | 5,152 | 5,152 |
| Our conflicts | 9,005 | 7,781 |
| Found by both | 3,811 (74% of FHWA's) | 4,430 (86%) |
| Only FHWA | 1,341 | 722 |
| Only ours | 5,194 (2,751 with no PET) | 3,351 (1,182 with no PET) |
| Same type | 2,803 of 3,811 (74%) | 3,352 of 4,430 (76%) |
| TTC difference | median 0.000 s, worst 1.5 s; identical in 2,792 of 3,811 | |
| PET difference | median 0.000 s, worst 4.6 s; identical in 3,096 of 3,811 | |

Main causes of the mismatches. I checked them on 2-vehicle extracts of mismatched pairs, and each extract gives the same result as the full file in both engines.
- **No-PET events** (OPEN 1): 2,751 of our 5,194 extra conflicts. SSAM_MT never lists one.
- **Projected rectangle orientation** (OPEN 3): ours turns the projected rectangle to the path direction at the projected point. SSAM_MT keeps the vehicle's current facing. NGSIM front positions jitter, so a car stopped in a queue that slips 0.1 ft backwards gets its 17 ft outline flipped onto the car ahead (pair 1104/1115: our TTC 0.1, FHWA nothing). Keeping the facing raises matches from 74% to 86% of FHWA's conflicts and cuts our extras by a third. The report says "the location and orientation of that vehicle at its projected future position", which reads like ours, so I have not switched without your decision.
- **Repeated overlaps of the same pair** in queues, where tracking error makes neighbouring outlines overlap: the engines split them into different numbers of events. 1,130 of the 1,341 FHWA-only conflicts have one of ours for the same pair within 10 s.
- **Types**: 1,008 differ. About 430 have a conflict angle within 15 degrees of the 30/85 degree cuts. The rest follow from different event start and end points (the headings and lanes at start and end decide the type).
- Events cut off by the end of a file (OPEN 2): 2.

### Speed (owner addition: keep .trj as is; ours must be fast)
Wall-clock on this PC, same two files:

| | FHWA SSAM_MT.exe | Ours before (commit 19d8fb1) | Ours now |
|---|---|---|---|
| lankershim_p1 (705k records) | 2.0 s | 98.7 s | 71.4 s |
| lankershim_p2 (902k records) | 2.5 s | 251.7 s | 147.6 s |
| Both, through the compare command | 5.9 s (one exe run per file, incl. CSV writing) | 350 s (one after the other) | 122.0 s (one process per file) |

SSAM_MT is multi-threaded native code (10 threads here). Ours is still about 20-50x slower per file.

- Changes that keep every result: a bounding-circle reject before the side test, cached rectangle boxes, and one process per file in the compare command. The NGSIM conflict lists before and after are identical (every field, both files), and `test_busy_scene_unchanged` guards this in CI.
- Not done: streaming the timesteps. Reading is about 1 s of the total, and each step needs every vehicle's next 10 s of path, so the tracks stay in memory anyway. Also not done: numpy. The profile shows the pair x 0.1 s projection/overlap loop is the hot spot, but numpy is not installed in the venv. It is the next step, behind the same identity test.

## OPEN (for the user)
1. **Events with a TTC but no PET**: list them with PET empty (ours now) or drop them (SSAM_MT)? The report applies both thresholds but doesn't say what happens when no PET is seen.
2. **Events still open when the file ends**: list them (ours) or drop them (SSAM_MT)? Dropping them loses near-misses in the last seconds of every recording.
3. **Projected rectangle orientation**: along the path at the projected point (ours, from the report's wording) or the vehicle's current facing (SSAM_MT; much more robust to jittery video tracks)?
4. **CSP and DeltaS**: at tMinTTC (report, ours) or at the start of the event (SSAM_MT)?
5. **NGSIM link coding**: section_id, or 100 + int_id inside an intersection. It feeds the lane-change and rear-end rules.

## Speed (synthetic, earlier round)
Synthetic 1-hour file, 1,000 vehicles (two crossing streams of 333 with no signal, one car-following stream of 334), 0.1 s steps: 36,001 timesteps, 711,346 vehicle records, up to 35 vehicles at once.
Read 3.6 s, conflict search 16.1 s (215 conflicts: 195 rear-end, 20 crossing), on this PC, standard library only. Numpy was not needed. The generator is a scratch script (not committed).

## Licence
Clean room. Written only from the public FHWA report FHWA-HRT-08-051 Ch. 2, the user manual FHWA-HRT-08-050 and the public file-format specs v1.04 / v3.0. The AGPL-3.0 SSAM source (SSAMDLL, include, SSAM3/SSAMAPP) was not opened or read. The package docstring credits FHWA's method and says this is an independent implementation, not FHWA's SSAM.

## Not done
- The OPEN choices above (user decisions).
- Speed: still much slower than SSAM_MT on Lankershim (numbers above). Numpy vectorisation of the pair x tau loop is the next step.
- Z values are read and written but not used to keep vehicles on different levels (overpasses) apart. Needs a rule for how far apart in Z counts as a different level.
- No UI, API or database wiring (per #484, after the visuals mockup).
- No CSV export of our conflict table.

title: Corridor: find intersections in a background job (no request over Cloudflare's 100 s)
body:
Fixes: the corridor step on the hosted site (crash.aitransportationtools.com). Behind the Cloudflare Tunnel any request is cut at 100 s (524); `PUT /corridor` called Overpass synchronously (up to 4 × 120 s + backoff, then driveways), so on a slow Overpass day (measured 2026-11-11: 116.5 s → 502; a tiny query took 27 s) the user got an error even when a retry would have worked.

## What changed
- **Backend (`network.py`)**: `PUT /studies/{sid}/corridor?background=true` validates the line in the request (state box → 400 as before), then starts or joins a per-study job in a thread — the crash pull's pattern (#54): `_JOBS` dict, `crashes._LOCKS_GUARD`, never held while calling out. It waits at most 1 s for the thread, so a corridor seen before (cached) still comes back at once with 200 + the network; otherwise **202 + `{job}`**.
- `GET /studies/{sid}/corridor/status` → `idle` | `running` (`step`, `attempt` n of `attempts` N, `last_error`, `line`) | `done` (+ `network`) | `error` (`status`, `error`).
- A new line while a job runs starts a new job; the old job's answer isn't saved.
- `fetch_overpass` gains an `on_attempt(n, of, last)` callback (the status' attempt count). Budget unchanged: the existing retries/backoff (4 × 120 s + 14 s), now off the request. Cache and old-map fallback untouched.
- The synchronous path (no `background`) is kept for tests, fixtures and scripts.
- **Frontend (`Corridor.jsx`)**: detection uses `?background=true` and polls status every 2 s. The button reads "Finding intersections… OpenStreetMap is busy, trying again (2 of 4)" on retries, "…checking driveways at signals" for the driveway query. A failure shows the server's plain message in the alert and the button becomes **Try again**. Coming back to the screen while a job runs shows its line and resumes polling.

## Other `fetch_overpass` callers inside a request
| Caller | Where it runs | What I did |
|---|---|---|
| `fetch_driveways` (#413) | corridor PUT | Now inside the corridor job |
| `roads_near` (FARS road check, #174) | `placement.place_unmatched` ← `crashes.ensure` | Nothing: runs in the crash-pull background job, which the screen already uses |
| `corridor_cities` (#142) | `crashes.ensure` | Same: crash-pull job |
| `union.corridor_network` | `crashes.ensure` | Same |
| `carriageway_query` (#329) | `crashes.ensure` | Same |
| `crossing_query`, `overpass_query` in `placement.py` | `place_unmatched` ← `crashes.ensure` | Same |
| `scripts/record_fixtures.py`, `record_live_fixture.py` | CLI | Not a request |

The synchronous `POST /crashes/pull` (no `background`) still runs Overpass in the request. The frontend never calls it; tests and scripts do.

## Mirrors
No new mirrors added. From this PC today the public mirrors private.coffee, kumi.systems and mail.ru all timed out at 40 s, so mirrors alone wouldn't fix this. `CRASHIQ_OVERPASS_URL` already supports our own server (#395).

## Tests
- `tests/test_corridor_job.py` (new): a fake transport that blocks, then fails twice, then answers. The PUT comes back in < 5 s while the network is still blocked (202), status shows attempt 1 of 4, then done at attempt 3 with the network saved. The same line joins the running job, and a cached repeat answers 200 in the request. All attempts failing → `error`, 502, plain text, nothing saved, and Try again starts a new job. A bad line is still refused in the request.
- `Corridor.test.jsx`: the busy message while polling, then the list; the final error + Try again; resume on return.
- Backend 1307 passed / 2 skipped; frontend 127 passed; ruff and eslint clean.
