title: SSAM: match FHWA's SSAM_MT on the four open rules (user decision 2026-11-11)
body:
Follows #487 (OPEN 1-4). Docs entry in `docs/03-requirements.md`, next to the 2026-11-10 SSAM decision.

## Decision
**SSAM matches FHWA's program DECIDED (user, 2026-11-11, PM chat: "I agree to the FWA. Let's do that. This is based on the guidelines.")**, answering "1a 2a 3a 4a: match FHWA's program on all four".

## The 4 rules (default `find_conflicts(..., fhwa_compatible=True)`)
1. An event with a TTC but no PET is dropped.
2. An event still open when the file ends is dropped. SSAM_MT's close time, fitted from black-box runs (below).
3. The projected rectangle keeps the vehicle's current facing at the projected point. It is no longer turned along the future path.
4. CSP and DeltaS are measured at the start of the event, not at tMinTTC.

`fhwa_compatible=False` is the report-literal variant (the old behaviour), unchanged bit for bit: `busy_conflicts_report.json` is the old frozen list and still matches. It's the only new option.

Two details inside the rules, both needed to match SSAM_MT's own numbers:
- **Rule 4, DeltaS**: SSAM_MT takes the velocities along the *conflict headings* (start centre to end centre), not along each vehicle's facing. cut_in: SSAM_MT 2.939621. Ours along the facing would be 3.50, and along the conflict headings it is 2.9396.
- **Rule 2, PET ties**: SSAM_MT breaks ties between equal 0.1 s PETs on the file's float32 times, comparing strictly less than. In FHWA mode PETs are now compared unrounded, and still reported rounded to 3 digits. This decides which position is the "best PET" one, which the close rule needs. It also gives SSAM_MT's xMinPET, e.g. 55.55 in place of 54.35 when the follower brakes at -3.

### Rule 2: SSAM_MT's closing rule (black box, SSAM_MT.exe only; no SSAM source opened)
I bisected the shortest file length at which SSAM_MT lists an event, at MaxPET 3 and 5, across 18 two-vehicle scenes. With e = last TTC step and dt = timestep, SSAM_MT lists the event only if the file runs to at least C + MaxPET - dt, where C is:
- e + dt, when the PET is 0 (a collision);
- the step the best PET was seen, when that PET was measured against the positions held at e (the "1 x MaxPET" scenes);
- otherwise e + MaxPET (the "2 x MaxPET" scenes from #487).

Our fitted rule gives SSAM_MT's exact shortest length in 31 of 36 (scene, MaxPET) runs. In 3 more it is 0.1 s off. Two are further off, both at MaxPET 3: 0.3 s and 1.2 s. What the vehicles do after the event (drop back, match speed, leader stops) never changed the result.

## Tests (TDD, one per rule, each also run in the report-literal variant)
- `test_rule1_no_pet_event_dropped`: crossing gives no conflict, as in SSAM_MT. Report-literal still gives TTC 0.9 with PET empty.
- `test_rule2_open_at_file_end_dropped`: rear_end without lanes is listed from 14.5 s, not at 14.4 (MaxPET 5), and from 10.5 s, not at 10.4 (MaxPET 3). Follower braking at -3: listed from 8.5 s, not at 8.4. All are SSAM_MT's measured thresholds. Report-literal lists it at 10 s.
- `test_rule3_projection_keeps_current_facing`: a stopped car with jittering front positions (1 cm backwards per step). Report-literal finds TTC 0.1 / PET 2.4. FHWA mode and SSAM_MT.exe find nothing.
- `test_rule4_csp_and_delta_s_at_event_start`: rear_end DeltaS 9.5, CSP 58.975 / 41.25, exactly SSAM_MT's CSV. Report-literal still gives 6.5.
- `test_ours_matches_fhwa` now also checks DeltaS and all four CSP values against SSAM_MT's CSVs (rear_end, follow_brake, cut_in, to 1e-4). New `test_no_conflict_where_fhwa_has_none` covers crossing and near_pass. `test_compare_command`: 3 both, 0 only FHWA, 0 only ours.
- `test_busy_scene_unchanged` is parametrised over both variants, floats compared to 9 digits.

### `busy_conflicts.json`: every change, by rule (116 -> 111 conflicts)
Rules applied in turn. Conflicts matched by pair + tMinTTC.
- **Rule 1** (no PET, removed): 13-28 t=34.6 (TTC 1.3), 14-72 t=46.7 (TTC 0.8), 14-79 t=23.7 (TTC 0.9).
- **Rule 2** (removed): 6-7 t=52.4, 9-54 t=54.5, 33-35 t=54.3, 9-16 t=57.1, 16-54 t=57.1, 33-36 t=57.4, 35-57 t=57.7, 43-58 t=57.9. All have PET 0, and the file ends at 60 s, before C + MaxPET - dt. No other field changed in this step. The float32 PET ties changed nothing in this scene.
- **Rule 3** (current facing; vehicle 14 has the most lateral jitter):
  - removed: 14-42 t=27.6.
  - new: 14-22 t=24.2, 14-24 t=47.2, 14-40 t=30.7, 14-42 t=26.3, 14-43 t=49.4, 14-72 t=47.3, 14-79 t=24.3.
  - start/end points moved, so headings, ConflictAngle, PostCrash and DeltaV changed: 12-20 t=6.9, 13-49 t=25.7, 14-22 t=25.9, 14-28 t=31.5, 14-34 t=51.2, 14-48 t=46.5, 14-50 t=31.8, 14-76 t=25.6, 18-62 t=10.0, 35-73 t=38.6, 55-61 t=22.2. Of these, 14-49 t=39.9 also changes type, rear-end -> lane-change (angle -5.1 -> -34.2).
- **Rule 4**: DeltaS and the four CSP fields change on all 111. Nothing else changes.

## Real data: NGSIM Lankershim Blvd (both periods, TTC 1.5, PET 5.0)
Same data and converter as #487: `ngsim.py` re-run here, and the .trj files are byte-identical to #487's. `python -m crashiq.ssam.compare <dir> --exe SSAM_MT.exe`. Before = main (#487), after = this branch.

| | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| FHWA conflicts | 5,152 | 5,152 |
| Ours | 9,005 | 6,590 |
| Found by both | 3,811 (74% of FHWA's) | 4,401 (85%) |
| Only FHWA | 1,341 | 751 |
| Only ours | 5,194 (2,751 with no PET) | 2,189 (0 with no PET) |
| Same type | 2,803 of 3,811 (74%) | 3,322 of 4,401 (75%) |
| TTC difference | median 0.000 s, worst 1.5 s; identical in 2,792 | median 0.000 s, worst 1.5 s; identical in 3,418 |
| PET difference | median 0.000 s, worst 4.6 s; identical in 3,096 | median 0.000 s, worst 3.5 s; identical in 3,834 |
| Wall-clock, ours | 122 s | 154 s (machine busy; rule 3 adds no work per step) |

### What still differs
- **Events split differently** (repeated overlaps of the same pair in queues): 1,052 of our 2,189 extras and 408 of the 751 FHWA-only conflicts have a conflict from the other engine for the same pair within 10 s. Our events close at e + best PET. SSAM_MT keeps some open longer (C above), so it merges what we split. Only the listing test uses SSAM_MT's C; event lifetimes were not changed, because that is beyond the 4 rules.
- **Vehicle leaves before the close**: black-box runs show SSAM_MT also drops an event when a vehicle's trajectory ends before C, even mid-file. We still list those. They are 87 of our extras here. The decision covered file end only, so this is not changed.
- **Types**: 1,079 differ, 489 of them within 15 degrees of the 30/85 degree cuts. The rest follow from different start/end points.
- **About 1,100 of our extras** have no SSAM_MT conflict for the pair nearby. Not explained yet.
- The rule-2 fit is off in 5 of 36 runs (above).

## Not done
- Matching SSAM_MT's event lifetimes and merges (its C as our close), and dropping events whose vehicle leaves before C. Both would be new rules for the user.
- SSAM_MT reports MaxDeltaV at the start too (rear_end 4.75 = 9.5 / 2), and its CEP comes later than ours (rear_end t=6.8, ours 5.1). Not part of the 4 rules, unchanged.
- OPEN 5 from #487 (NGSIM link coding) still open.
- No numpy or speed work. No UI/API wiring.
- Licence: SSAM_MT.exe used only as a black box. No SSAM `.cpp`/`.h` opened. No NGSIM data committed (CC BY-SA).

title: Basemap: aitt-map vector basemap (day style) replaces Esri
body:
Basemap swap only, no UI/UX changes (owner rule for this PR). Both maps drop the Esri Dark Gray Canvas raster and draw our own **aitt-map v0.1.0** vector basemap in its light `day` style. Tiles come from `https://tiles.aitransportationtools.com` (California PMTiles, OSM + Protomaps).

No issue number: the owner asked for this directly (decision 2026-11-16: aitt-map `day` style on every map, whatever the app theme). PM: please record the decision in `docs/`.

## What changed
- `frontend/src/lib/tiles.js`: registers the `pmtiles://` protocol and the MapLibre worker URL (moved here from ProfileMap). `basemapStyle()` = `buildStyle(readTokens(), 'day', …)` from `@aitt/map`, with tiles and fonts from tiles.aitransportationtools.com. The Esri URL and its attribution are gone.
- `CorridorMap.jsx` (Leaflet): the `TileLayer` is replaced by `L.maplibreGL({ style: basemapStyle() })` (`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-leaflet`). All Leaflet overlays and interactions are unchanged. The corridor ink colour (`fg`) is now near-black so it reads on the light map.
- `CorridorMap.jsx` `Fit`: the right padding is capped at half the map width. On a 390 px phone the 420 px padding gave Leaflet a NaN zoom. The Esri raster layer tolerated that, but the MapLibre layer throws (`Invalid LatLng (NaN, NaN)`) and the whole screen went blank. Desktop is unchanged, since 420 px is under half the map width.
- `ProfileMap.jsx` (MapLibre): the style spreads the day style's sources and layers under our own overlays. The dark background and dimmed raster are gone. The VRU ring and the approximate-location ring are darkened so they read on the light map.
- `public/sprites/v4/light*`: the day style's sprite, copied from the package. The tile host has no sprites.
- `package.json`: adds `@aitt/map` (public GitHub tarball, tag v0.1.0), `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-leaflet` and `pmtiles`, and moves `maplibre-gl` from 6.16.0 to ^6.18. `vite.config.js` excludes `@aitt/map` from dev pre-bundling.
- `ProfileMap.test.jsx` mocks `basemapStyle`, because tests don't load CSS tokens.
- CSP: there is none to update. `deploy/Caddyfile` sets no headers, and neither the backend nor `index.html` sets a CSP.

## Checked (vite preview :4173 + API :8000, study "union city" `c9efd441c4fb`, 81 crashes read, 12 on the corridor)
- **0 Esri/ArcGIS requests** on corridor and profile, desktop 1440×900 and phone 390×844. All basemap requests go to tiles.aitransportationtools.com (PMTiles range requests 206, fonts, local sprite).
- No console errors, page errors or CORS errors after the phone fix above.
- Street names show. The corridor line follows Union City Boulevard. At intersection zoom (Eastin Drive / Lowry Road, 2D) the crash dots sit on the boulevard. The line runs along one carriageway of the divided road, which is the same OSM geometry as before.
- Tile CORS allows `https://crash.aitransportationtools.com` (checked with curl), plus localhost 3000, 4173 and 5173.
- Screenshots: corridor and profile, desktop and phone, plus intersection zoom. Before shots (Esri, Crenshaw study) and after shots are kept outside the repo on the dev PC (`hermes/cache/scratch/crashiq-shots/`). I can attach them here on request. Before: a dark grey raster, blurry past z16. After: the light vector map with crisp labels at every zoom.

## Tests
- Frontend: `vitest` 12 files / 128 tests pass, `eslint` is clean, `vite build` passes. The bundle-size warning was already there.
- Backend: `pytest` 1358 passed, 2 skipped, and `ruff` is clean.

## How to go live (home-PC beta, docs/runbook-deploy.md "Free beta")
1. Merge this PR to `main` (PM, after review).
2. Update the beta checkout: `git -C C:/Users/aksha/Workspace/repos/Crash-beta pull --ff-only origin main`, then in it run `make setup` and `make build`. Use `make setup`, not only `make build`, because there are new npm dependencies and `npm ci` must run. The build fetches `@aitt/map` from codeload.github.com, which is public.
3. Restart the server with the runbook step 2 command (port 8090, `CRASHIQ_HOSTED=1`; the user types the password). The tunnel needs no change.
4. Check from a phone off Wi-Fi at `https://crash.aitransportationtools.com`: open a study's Corridor and Crash profile. The light basemap should show, and DevTools Network should show no `arcgisonline` requests. The tile host already allows this origin.
5. Docker / one-server path (`deploy/docker-compose.yml`): `git pull && docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d --build crashiq`. If that server gets its own domain, add the domain to the tile host's CORS allow-list first, or the map stays blank.
